sentences.zh: 皇甫謐

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Huangfu Mi.

sentences.zh: 皇甫謐，字士安，幼名靜，安定朝那人，漢太尉嵩之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi, courtesy name Shi'an, childhood name Jing, was a man of Chaona in Anding commandery, and a great-grandson of Song, Grand Commandant of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi, whose courtesy name was Shi'an and childhood name Jing, came from Chaona in Anding; he was the great-grandson of Huangfu Song, who had served the Han as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 出叔父，徙居新安。

translations.literal: He was given in adoption to an uncle and moved his residence to Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously transferred to his uncle's line and the family relocated to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 年二十，不好學，遊蕩無度，或以為癡。

translations.literal: At age twenty he did not care for study; he roamed idly without restraint, and some considered him dull-witted.
translations.idiomatic: By twenty he still scorned books, drifted without purpose, and people took him for a simpleton.

sentences.zh: 嘗得瓜果，輒進所叔母任氏。

translations.literal: When he obtained melons or fruit, he would always present them to his aunt by adoption, Lady Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had fruit, he would bring it first to his adoptive aunt, Lady Ren.

sentences.zh: 任氏曰：「《孝經》云：『三牲之養，猶為不孝。』

translations.literal: Lady Ren said: "The Classic of Filial Piety states: 'Even the nourishing of parents with the three sacrificial animals may still count as unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ren told him: "The Classic of Filial Piety says that even serving one's parents the finest triple sacrifice can still fall short of true filial piety.

sentences.zh: 汝今年餘二十，目不存教，心不入道，無以慰我。」

translations.literal: You are now past twenty; your eyes do not fix on instruction, your mind does not enter the Way—there is no way for you to comfort me."
translations.idiomatic: You are already past twenty, yet you pay no heed to teaching and your heart is not in the Way; that gives me no comfort."

sentences.zh: 因歎曰：「昔孟母三徙以成仁，曾父烹豕以存教，豈我居不卜鄰，教有所闕，何爾魯鈍之甚也！

translations.literal: Thereupon she sighed and said: "In olden days Mother Meng moved three times to complete her son's humanity; Zengzi's father cooked a pig to preserve teaching—could it be that I did not choose good neighbors for my dwelling, that there was some lack in my instruction, and that you are therefore so exceptionally dull!
translations.idiomatic: She sighed and went on: "Meng Ke's mother moved house three times to shape his character; Zeng Shen's father kept his word over a pig to teach honesty. Have I failed to pick our neighbors, or failed you as a teacher, that you should be so stubbornly slow?

sentences.zh: 修身篤學，自汝得之，于我何有！」

translations.literal: Cultivating the person and applying oneself earnestly to learning—you obtain these for yourself; what have they to do with me!"
translations.idiomatic: Moral self-cultivation and serious study are yours to earn—what credit would they bring me?"

sentences.zh: 因對之流涕。

translations.literal: Thereupon she wept before him.
translations.idiomatic: With that she wept in front of him.

sentences.zh: 謐乃感激，就鄉人席坦受書，勤力不怠。

translations.literal: Mi thereupon was stirred; he went to his fellow townsman Xi Tan to receive instruction in the classics and labored diligently without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her words, he studied under his townsman Xi Tan and applied himself without letting up.

sentences.zh: 居貧，躬自稼穡，帶經而農，遂博綜典籍百家之言。

translations.literal: Living in poverty, he personally plowed and harvested, carrying the classics with him as he farmed, and in the end broadly mastered the texts of the canon and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Poor as he was, he worked the fields himself, classics tucked in his belt, until he had mastered the standard works and the writings of every school.

sentences.zh: 沈靜寡欲，始有高尚之志，以著述為務，自號玄晏先生。

translations.literal: Calm and retiring with few desires, he began to harbor lofty aims, took writing and compilation as his occupation, and styled himself Master Xuanyan.
translations.idiomatic: Reserved and detached from ambition, he turned to scholarship as his life's work and took the sobriquet Master Xuanyan ('Dark Tranquility').

sentences.zh: 著《禮樂》、《聖真》之論。

translations.literal: He composed treatises titled 'Rites and Music' and 'Sagehood and Authenticity.'
translations.idiomatic: He wrote discourses on ritual and music and on sagehood and truth.

sentences.zh: 後得風痹疾，猶手不輟卷。

translations.literal: Later he contracted wind-numbness illness, yet still his hand did not lay aside his scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he fell ill with arthritic numbness, he never set his books aside.

sentences.zh: 或勸謐修名廣交，謐以為「非聖人孰能兼存出處，居田里之中亦可以樂堯、舜之道，何必崇接世利，事官鞅掌，然後為名乎」。

translations.literal: Some urged Mi to cultivate reputation and broaden his associations; Mi considered that 'unless one is a sage, who can simultaneously preserve both withdrawal and emergence? Dwelling in field and village, one may still take joy in the Way of Yao and Shun—why must one exalt contact with worldly profit, busy oneself with official duties in confusion, and only then count as having a name?'
translations.idiomatic: When others pressed him to network and seek fame, Mi replied, "Unless one is a sage, who can preserve both public service and withdrawal? In the countryside one can still delight in the Way of Yao and Shun. Why must one seek worldly profit and busy oneself in office before gaining a name?"

sentences.zh: 作《玄守論》以答之，曰：或謂謐曰：「富貴人之所欲，貧賤人之所惡，何故委形待於窮而不變乎？且道之所貴者，理世也；人之所美者，及時也。先生年邁齒變，饑寒不贍，轉死溝壑，其誰知乎？」

translations.literal: He composed "On Abiding in Mystery" to answer them. It says: Someone asked Mi, "Wealth and rank are what people desire, and poverty and lowliness are what people hate. Why do you entrust your body to hardship and remain unchanged? What the Way values is ordering the age; what people admire is meeting the right time. Sir, your years are advanced and your teeth are failing; hunger and cold are not supplied for, and you may die in a ditch. Who will know you?"
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "On Abiding in Mystery" in reply. It begins with someone asking Mi, "Wealth and rank are what people desire, poverty and lowliness what they hate. Why commit your body to hardship and refuse to change? The Way is prized because it orders the age; people admire seizing the right moment. Sir, you are old, hungry, and cold, and may die in a ditch. Who will ever know?"

sentences.zh: 謐曰：「人之所至惜者，命也；

translations.literal: Mi replied, "What people most cherish is life;
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied, "What people most cherish is life;

sentences.zh: 道之所必全者，形也；

translations.literal: what the Way must keep whole is the body;
translations.idiomatic: what the Way must keep whole is the body;

sentences.zh: 性形所不可犯者，疾病也。

translations.literal: what nature and body cannot withstand is illness.
translations.idiomatic: what nature and body cannot withstand is illness.

sentences.zh: 若擾全道以損性命，安得去貧賤存所欲哉？

translations.literal: If one disturbs the whole Way and injures nature and life, how can one escape poverty and lowliness while preserving what one desires?
translations.idiomatic: If one disturbs the whole Way and injures nature and life, how can one escape poverty and lowliness while preserving what one desires?

sentences.zh: 吾聞食人之祿者懷人之憂，形強猶不堪，況吾之弱疾乎！

translations.literal: I have heard that one who eats another man's stipend bears that man's anxieties; even a strong body can hardly bear this, much less my weak and sick one.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that one who eats another man's stipend bears that man's anxieties; even a strong body can hardly bear this, much less my weak and sick one.

sentences.zh: 且貧者士之常，賤者道之實，處常得實，沒齒不憂，孰與富貴擾神耗精者乎！

translations.literal: Poverty is the scholar's normal condition, and lowliness is the substance of the Way; to live in what is normal and gain what is real until the end of one's teeth is free of worry. How is that like wealth and rank, which disturb the spirit and exhaust the essence?
translations.idiomatic: Poverty is the scholar's normal condition, and lowliness is the substance of the Way; to live in what is normal and gain what is real until the end of one's teeth is free of worry. How is that like wealth and rank, which disturb the spirit and exhaust the essence?

sentences.zh: 又生為人所不知，死為人所不惜，至矣！

translations.literal: Moreover, to live unknown by others and die unlamented by others is the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to live unknown by others and die unlamented by others is the utmost.

sentences.zh: 喑聾之徒，天下之有道者也。

translations.literal: The mute and deaf are those under Heaven who possess the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The mute and deaf are those under Heaven who possess the Way.

sentences.zh: 夫一人死而天下號者，以為損也；

translations.literal: When one man dies and all under Heaven wails, people call that a loss;
translations.idiomatic: When one man dies and all under Heaven wails, people call that a loss;

sentences.zh: 一人生而四海笑者，以為益也。

translations.literal: when one man lives and the four seas smile, people call that a gain.
translations.idiomatic: when one man lives and the four seas smile, people call that a gain.

sentences.zh: 然則號笑非益死損生也。

translations.literal: Yet wailing and smiling do not make death a gain or life a loss.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wailing and smiling do not make death a gain or life a loss.

sentences.zh: 是以至道不損，至德不益。

translations.literal: Therefore the highest Way is not diminished, and the highest virtue is not increased.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the highest Way is not diminished, and the highest virtue is not increased.

sentences.zh: 何哉？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 體足也。

translations.literal: Because its substance is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Because its substance is complete.

sentences.zh: 如回天下之念以追損生之禍，運四海之心以廣非益之病，豈道德之至乎！

translations.literal: If one turns the thoughts of all under Heaven toward chasing the calamity of losing life, and moves the hearts of the four seas to enlarge the sickness of what is no gain, how could that be the height of Way and virtue?
translations.idiomatic: If one turns the thoughts of all under Heaven toward chasing the calamity of losing life, and moves the hearts of the four seas to enlarge the sickness of what is no gain, how could that be the height of Way and virtue?

sentences.zh: 夫唯無損，則至堅矣；

translations.literal: Only what has no loss is supremely firm;
translations.idiomatic: Only what has no loss is supremely firm;

sentences.zh: 夫唯無益，則至厚矣。

translations.literal: only what has no gain is supremely substantial.
translations.idiomatic: only what has no gain is supremely substantial.

sentences.zh: 堅故終不損，厚故終不薄。

translations.literal: Because it is firm, in the end it is not diminished; because it is substantial, in the end it is not thinned.
translations.idiomatic: Because it is firm, in the end it is not diminished; because it is substantial, in the end it is not thinned.

sentences.zh: 苟能體堅厚之實，居不薄之真，立乎損益之外，遊乎形骸之表，則我道全矣。」

translations.literal: If one can embody the reality of firmness and substance, dwell in the truth that is not thinned, stand outside loss and gain, and roam beyond bodily form, then my Way is whole."
translations.idiomatic: If one can embody the reality of firmness and substance, dwell in the truth that is not thinned, stand outside loss and gain, and roam beyond bodily form, then my Way is whole."

sentences.zh: 遂不仕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore never entered government service.

sentences.zh: 耽玩典籍，忘寢與食，時人謂之「書淫」。

translations.literal: He was addicted to and delighted in the classics, forgetting sleep and food; people of the time called him a 'book debauchee.'
translations.idiomatic: He lost himself in texts to the point of skipping meals and sleep, and his contemporaries nicknamed him a "book lecher."

sentences.zh: 或有箴其過篤，將損耗精神。

translations.literal: Some admonished him that he was too intense and would waste his vital spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Friends warned that such obsession would ruin his health.

sentences.zh: 謐曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣，況命之修短分定懸天乎！」

translations.literal: Mi said: 'In the morning hear the Way; in the evening die—acceptable! How much more when the length or brevity of life is apportioned and hangs fixed from Heaven!'
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "If I could hear the truth in the morning, I could die content that evening—and lifespan is heaven's decision anyway."

sentences.zh: 叔父有子既冠，謐年四十喪所生後母，遂還本宗。

translations.literal: When his uncle had a son who had already capped, Mi, at age forty, mourned the death of his birth mother who had been stepmother, and thereupon returned to his original clan.
translations.idiomatic: Once his uncle had an heir of age, and Mi turned forty, he buried the stepmother who had raised him and reverted to his natural father's line.

sentences.zh: 城陽太守梁柳，謐從姑子也，當之官，人勸謐餞之。

translations.literal: Liang Liu, governor of Chengyang, was the son of Mi's father's cousin; when he was about to go to his post, people urged Mi to hold a farewell feast for him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Liu of Chengyang commandery—Mi's cousin once removed—was leaving for his appointment, and neighbors wanted Mi to host a send-off banquet.

sentences.zh: 謐曰：「柳為布衣時過吾，吾送迎不出門，食不過鹽菜，貧者不以酒肉為禮。

translations.literal: Mi said: 'When Liu was a commoner visiting me, I did not go beyond my gate to see him off or welcome him, and our meals did not go beyond salted vegetables—the poor do not take wine and meat as ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Mi replied: "When Liang Liu was still a commoner and called on me, I never stepped outside my door for him and we ate nothing finer than pickles—modest households do not toast one another with meat and wine.

sentences.zh: 今作郡而送之，是貴城陽太守而賤梁柳，豈中古人之道，是非吾心所安也。」

translations.literal: Now that he holds a commandery and I send him off in this way, this would esteem the governor of Chengyang and slight Liang Liu—it cannot hit the mark of the ancients' Way; this is not what my heart finds acceptable.'
translations.idiomatic: To fuss over him now that he wears an official's sash would honor the title of governor while slighting the man Liang Liu himself—that is not how the old worthies behaved, and it would not sit right with me."

sentences.zh: 時魏郡召上計掾，舉孝廉；

translations.literal: At that time Wei commandery summoned him as clerk for the annual accounts and nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt;
translations.idiomatic: Wei commandery appointed him accounts clerk and nominated him for the Filial and Incorrupt examination;

sentences.zh: 景元初，相國辟，皆不行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingyuan era, the prime minister summoned him; in each case he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingyuan the chief minister tried to hire him as well, but he refused every summons.

sentences.zh: 其後鄉親勸令應命，謐為《釋勸論》以通志焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter his fellow villagers urged him to answer the summons; Mi composed 'Disquisition Explaining Persuasion' to clarify his intent.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors pressed him to accept office, he wrote his "Disquisition Explaining Persuasion" to spell out his resolve.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：相國晉王辟餘等三十七人，及泰始登禪，同命之士莫不畢至，皆拜騎都尉，或賜爵關內侯，進奉朝請，禮如侍臣。

translations.literal: Its text says: When the Prime Minister, the Prince of Jin, summoned the thirty-seven of us and then ascended through abdication in Taishi, those who shared the summons all arrived; all were appointed Cavalier Commandants, some were granted the rank of marquis within the passes, and they advanced to offer court attendance, with rites like attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Its text says: When the Prime Minister, the Prince of Jin, summoned thirty-seven of us and then ascended through abdication in Taishi, everyone who had shared the summons arrived. They were all made Cavalier Commandants, some received the rank of marquis within the passes, and they were admitted to court attendance with the rites of attendants.

sentences.zh: 唯余疾困，不及國寵。

translations.literal: Only I was trapped by illness and could not reach the state's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Only I was trapped by illness and could not reach the state's favor.

sentences.zh: 宗人父兄及我僚類，咸以為天下大慶，萬姓賴之，雖未成禮，不宜安寢，縱其疾篤，猶當致身。

translations.literal: My clansmen, elders, and colleagues all said that this was a great celebration for all under Heaven, on which the people depended; even if the rites were not yet complete, I should not sleep peacefully, and though my illness was grave, I should still present myself.
translations.idiomatic: My clansmen, elders, and colleagues all said that this was a great celebration for all under Heaven, on which the people depended; even if the rites were not yet complete, I should not sleep peacefully, and though my illness was grave, I should still present myself.

sentences.zh: 余唯古今明王之制，事無巨細，斷之以情，實力不堪，豈慢也哉！

translations.literal: I thought that in the institutions of enlightened kings ancient and modern, affairs great and small are judged by circumstances. If my actual strength could not bear it, how was that arrogance?
translations.idiomatic: I thought that in the institutions of enlightened kings ancient and modern, affairs great and small are judged by circumstances. If my actual strength could not bear it, how was that arrogance?

sentences.zh: 乃伏枕而歎曰：「夫進者，身之榮也；

translations.literal: Lying on my pillow, I sighed, "Advancement is the glory of the body;
translations.idiomatic: Lying on my pillow, I sighed, "Advancement is the glory of the body;

sentences.zh: 退者，命之實也。

translations.literal: withdrawal is the reality of one's allotment.
translations.idiomatic: withdrawal is the reality of one's allotment.

sentences.zh: 設余不疾，執高箕山，尚當容之，況餘實篤！

translations.literal: Even if I were not ill, if I clung to the height of Mount Ji, it should still be tolerated; how much more when I am truly gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I were not ill, if I clung to the height of Mount Ji, it should still be tolerated; how much more when I am truly gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 故堯、舜之世，士或收跡林澤，或過門不敢入。

translations.literal: Thus in the ages of Yao and Shun, some gentlemen withdrew their tracks to forests and marshes, and some passed the gate and dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the ages of Yao and Shun, some gentlemen withdrew their tracks to forests and marshes, and some passed the gate and dared not enter.

sentences.zh: 咎繇之徒兩遂其願者，遇時也。

translations.literal: That Gaoyao and his kind could both fulfill their wishes was because they met the right age.
translations.idiomatic: That Gaoyao and his kind could both fulfill their wishes was because they met the right age.

sentences.zh: 故朝貴致功之臣，野美全志之士。

translations.literal: Thus the court honored ministers who brought achievements, while the fields admired gentlemen who preserved their intent.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the court honored ministers who brought achievements, while the fields admired gentlemen who preserved their intent.

sentences.zh: 彼獨何人哉！

translations.literal: What kind of men were they alone?
translations.idiomatic: What kind of men were they alone?

sentences.zh: 今聖帝龍興，配名前哲，仁道不遠，斯亦然乎！

translations.literal: Now that the sage emperor has risen like a dragon and matches the former worthies in name, the humane Way is not far off; is this not also so?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the sage emperor has risen like a dragon and matches the former worthies in name, the humane Way is not far off; is this not also so?

sentences.zh: 客或以常言見逼，或以逆世為慮。

translations.literal: Some guests press me with ordinary arguments, and some worry that I am opposing the age.
translations.idiomatic: Some guests press me with ordinary arguments, and some worry that I am opposing the age.

sentences.zh: 餘謂上有寬明之主，下必有聽意之人，天網恢恢，至否一也，何尤於出處哉！」遂究賓主之論，以解難者，名曰《釋勸》。

translations.literal: I say that when above there is a generous and enlightened ruler, below there must be people who listen to intent; Heaven's net is vast, and arrival or obstruction is one. Why should service or withdrawal be blamed?" He then fully developed a dialogue of guest and host to answer the objections, naming it Explaining Persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: I say that when above there is a generous and enlightened ruler, below there must be people who listen to intent; Heaven's net is vast, and arrival or obstruction is one. Why should service or withdrawal be blamed?" He then fully developed a dialogue of guest and host to answer the objections, naming it Explaining Persuasion.

sentences.zh: 客曰：「蓋聞天以懸象致明，地以含通吐靈。

translations.literal: The guest said, "I have heard that Heaven brings forth brightness by hanging up the celestial patterns, and Earth gives out numinous things by containing and pervading.
translations.idiomatic: The guest said, "I have heard that Heaven brings forth brightness by hanging up the celestial patterns, and Earth gives out numinous things by containing and pervading.

sentences.zh: 故黃鐘次序，律呂分形。

translations.literal: Therefore the Yellow Bell gives sequence, and the pitch-pipes divide their forms.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Yellow Bell gives sequence, and the pitch-pipes divide their forms.

sentences.zh: 是以春華髮萼，夏繁其實，秋風逐暑，冬冰乃結。

translations.literal: Thus spring blossoms open their calyxes, summer makes their fruit abundant, autumn winds drive out heat, and winter ice then forms.
translations.idiomatic: Thus spring blossoms open their calyxes, summer makes their fruit abundant, autumn winds drive out heat, and winter ice then forms.

sentences.zh: 人道以之，應機乃發。

translations.literal: The human Way follows this: it responds to the moment and then acts.
translations.idiomatic: The human Way follows this: it responds to the moment and then acts.

sentences.zh: 三材連利，明若符契。

translations.literal: The three powers are joined in benefit, as clear as matched tallies.
translations.idiomatic: The three powers are joined in benefit, as clear as matched tallies.

sentences.zh: 故士或同升於唐朝，或先覺於有莘，或通夢以感主，或釋釣於渭濱，或叩角以幹齊，或解褐以相秦，或冒謗以安鄭，或乘駟以救屯，或班荊以求友，或借術于黃神。

translations.literal: Thus gentlemen sometimes rose together at the Tangchao, Tang's court, awakened first at Youxin, reached a ruler through dreams, left off fishing at Weibin on the Wei bank, knocked on an ox-horn to seek service in Qi, shed homespun to minister in Qin, braved slander to settle Zheng, rode a team to rescue danger, spread brambles to seek friendship, or borrowed arts from the Yellow Spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Thus gentlemen sometimes rose together at the Tangchao, Tang's court, awakened first at Youxin, reached a ruler through dreams, left off fishing at Weibin on the Wei bank, knocked on an ox-horn to seek service in Qi, shed homespun to minister in Qin, braved slander to settle Zheng, rode a team to rescue danger, spread brambles to seek friendship, or borrowed arts from the Yellow Spirit.

sentences.zh: 故能電飛景拔，超次邁倫，騰高聲以奮遠，抗宇宙之清音。

translations.literal: Thus they could fly like lightning and rise like shadows, leap beyond rank and surpass their peers, lift a high reputation to strive afar, and raise a clear sound through the universe.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they could fly like lightning and rise like shadows, leap beyond rank and surpass their peers, lift a high reputation to strive afar, and raise a clear sound through the universe.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，進德貴乎及時，何故屈此而不伸？

translations.literal: Viewed from this, advancing virtue values meeting the time. Why bend this talent and not extend it?
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from this, advancing virtue values meeting the time. Why bend this talent and not extend it?

sentences.zh: 今子以英茂之才，游精於六藝之府，散意於眾妙之門者有年矣。

translations.literal: Now you, sir, with brilliant and abundant talent, have for years roamed your essence through the storehouse of the Six Arts and let your mind wander at the gate of the many mysteries.
translations.idiomatic: Now you, sir, with brilliant and abundant talent, have for years roamed your essence through the storehouse of the Six Arts and let your mind wander at the gate of the many mysteries.

sentences.zh: 既遭皇禪之朝，又投祿利之際，委聖明之主，偶知己之會，時清道真，可以沖邁，此真吾生濯發雲漢、鴻漸之秋也。

translations.literal: You have met the court of imperial abdication, arrived at a moment of stipend and advantage, entrusted yourself to a sage and enlightened ruler, and encountered a meeting with one who knows you. The age is clear and the Way true; you can soar upward. This is truly the season for washing your hair in the Milky Way and advancing like a wild goose.
translations.idiomatic: You have met the court of imperial abdication, arrived at a moment of stipend and advantage, entrusted yourself to a sage and enlightened ruler, and encountered a meeting with one who knows you. The age is clear and the Way true; you can soar upward. This is truly the season for washing your hair in the Milky Way and advancing like a wild goose.

sentences.zh: 韜光逐藪，含章未曜，龍潛九泉，堅焉執高，棄通道之遠由，守介人之局操，無乃乖於道之趣乎？

translations.literal: To hide your light and chase the marshes, hold pattern within and not shine, let a dragon sink into the nine springs, stubbornly cling to height, abandon the distant route of the open Way, and keep the cramped conduct of an isolated man: does this not go against the direction of the Way?
translations.idiomatic: To hide your light and chase the marshes, hold pattern within and not shine, let a dragon sink into the nine springs, stubbornly cling to height, abandon the distant route of the open Way, and keep the cramped conduct of an isolated man: does this not go against the direction of the Way?

sentences.zh: 且吾聞招搖昏回則天位正，五教班敘則人理定。

translations.literal: Moreover, I have heard that when the Dipper turns in the dark, Heaven's stations are corrected, and when the five teachings are ranked in order, human principle is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I have heard that when the Dipper turns in the dark, Heaven's stations are corrected, and when the five teachings are ranked in order, human principle is settled.

sentences.zh: 如今王命切至，委慮有司，上招迕主之累，下致駭眾之疑。

translations.literal: Now the royal command has urgently arrived and concern has been entrusted to the offices; above, you incur the burden of defying the ruler, and below, you cause the suspicion of frightening the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Now the royal command has urgently arrived and concern has been entrusted to the offices; above, you incur the burden of defying the ruler, and below, you cause the suspicion of frightening the crowd.

sentences.zh: 達者貴同，何必獨異？

translations.literal: Those who understand value concord. Why insist on being uniquely different?
translations.idiomatic: Those who understand value concord. Why insist on being uniquely different?

sentences.zh: 群賢可從，何必守意？

translations.literal: The many worthies can be followed. Why insist on keeping your own intent?
translations.idiomatic: The many worthies can be followed. Why insist on keeping your own intent?

sentences.zh: 方今同命並臻，饑不待餐，振藻皇塗，咸秩天官。

translations.literal: Now those summoned with you have all arrived, hungry yet not waiting to eat, displaying their literary colors on the imperial road and all taking rank in Heaven's offices.
translations.idiomatic: Now those summoned with you have all arrived, hungry yet not waiting to eat, displaying their literary colors on the imperial road and all taking rank in Heaven's offices.

sentences.zh: 子獨棲遲衡門，放形世表，遜遁丘園，不睨華好，惠不加人，行不合道，身嬰大疢，性命難保。

translations.literal: You alone linger at a barred gate, release your body beyond the world, withdraw to hills and gardens, refuse to glance at splendor, give no benefit to others, act out of accord with the Way, and have a body entangled in great illness, so that your life is hard to preserve.
translations.idiomatic: You alone linger at a barred gate, release your body beyond the world, withdraw to hills and gardens, refuse to glance at splendor, give no benefit to others, act out of accord with the Way, and have a body entangled in great illness, so that your life is hard to preserve.

sentences.zh: 若其羲和促轡，大火西穨，臨川恨晚，將復何階！

translations.literal: If Xi and He hasten the reins and Great Fire declines westward, when you face the river and regret lateness, what steps will remain?
translations.idiomatic: If Xi and He hasten the reins and Great Fire declines westward, when you face the river and regret lateness, what steps will remain?

sentences.zh: 夫貴陰賤璧，聖所約也；

translations.literal: Valuing shade more than a jade disk is what the sages set down;
translations.idiomatic: Valuing shade more than a jade disk is what the sages set down;

sentences.zh: 顛倒衣裳，明所箴也。

translations.literal: putting robe and skirt upside down is what the enlightened warned against.
translations.idiomatic: putting robe and skirt upside down is what the enlightened warned against.

sentences.zh: 子其鑒先哲之洪范，副聖朝之虛心，沖靈翼于雲路，浴天池以濯鱗，排閶闔，步玉岑，登紫闥，侍北辰，翻然景曜，雜遝英塵。

translations.literal: You should take the great models of former philosophers as your mirror, answer the open mind of the sage court, lift your numinous wings to the cloud-road, bathe in the heavenly pool and wash your scales, push open the Gate of Heaven, step on jade peaks, ascend the purple gate, attend the Northern Pole, and suddenly shine with the bright dust of the talented.
translations.idiomatic: You should take the great models of former philosophers as your mirror, answer the open mind of the sage court, lift your numinous wings to the cloud-road, bathe in the heavenly pool and wash your scales, push open the Gate of Heaven, step on jade peaks, ascend the purple gate, attend the Northern Pole, and suddenly shine with the bright dust of the talented.

sentences.zh: 輔唐、虞之主，化堯舜、之人，宣刑錯之政，配殷、周之臣，銘功景鐘，參敘彝倫，存則鼎食，亡為貴臣，不亦茂哉！

translations.literal: Assist a ruler of Tang and Yu, transform the people of Yao and Shun, proclaim a government in which punishments are set aside, stand with the ministers of Yin and Zhou, engrave your merit on the great bell, join in ordering the constant relations; alive, you will dine from tripods, and dead, you will be an honored minister. Would that not be splendid?
translations.idiomatic: Assist a ruler of Tang and Yu, transform the people of Yao and Shun, proclaim a government in which punishments are set aside, stand with the ministers of Yin and Zhou, engrave your merit on the great bell, join in ordering the constant relations; alive, you will dine from tripods, and dead, you will be an honored minister. Would that not be splendid?

sentences.zh: 而忽金白之輝曜，忘青紫之班瞵，辭容服之光粲，抱弊褐之終年，無乃勤乎！」主人笑而應之曰：「籲！

translations.literal: Yet you neglect the brightness of gold and white, forget the gleam of blue and purple rank, decline the radiance of ceremonial dress, and embrace worn homespun to the end of your years. Is that not toil?" The host laughed and answered, "Ah!
translations.idiomatic: Yet you neglect the brightness of gold and white, forget the gleam of blue and purple rank, decline the radiance of ceremonial dress, and embrace worn homespun to the end of your years. Is that not toil?" The host laughed and answered, "Ah!

sentences.zh: 若賓可謂習外觀之暉暉，未睹幽人之仿佛也；

translations.literal: Guest, you may be said to be used to the glitter of outward appearances but not yet to have glimpsed the faint form of the hidden man;
translations.idiomatic: Guest, you may be said to be used to the glitter of outward appearances but not yet to have glimpsed the faint form of the hidden man;

sentences.zh: 見俗人之不容，未喻聖皇之兼愛也；

translations.literal: you see that vulgar people do not tolerate him, but have not understood the all-embracing love of the sage sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: you see that vulgar people do not tolerate him, but have not understood the all-embracing love of the sage sovereign;

sentences.zh: 循方圓於規矩，未知大形之無外也。

translations.literal: you follow square and circle by compass and carpenter's square, but do not yet know that the great form has no outside.
translations.idiomatic: you follow square and circle by compass and carpenter's square, but do not yet know that the great form has no outside.

sentences.zh: 故曰，天玄而清，地靜而甯，含羅萬類，旁薄群生，寄身聖世，托道之靈。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: Heaven is dark and clear; Earth is still and peaceful. They contain and net the ten thousand kinds, spread broadly over living things, lodge the body in a sage age, and entrust it to the numen of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said: Heaven is dark and clear; Earth is still and peaceful. They contain and net the ten thousand kinds, spread broadly over living things, lodge the body in a sage age, and entrust it to the numen of the Way.

sentences.zh: 若夫春以陽散，冬以陰凝，泰液含光，元氣混蒸，眾品仰化，誕制殊征。

translations.literal: As for spring dispersing through yang and winter congealing through yin, the Great Fluid containing light and primal qi steaming in mixture, the many kinds look up to transformation and are born with different signs.
translations.idiomatic: As for spring dispersing through yang and winter congealing through yin, the Great Fluid containing light and primal qi steaming in mixture, the many kinds look up to transformation and are born with different signs.

sentences.zh: 故進者享天祿，處者安丘陵。

translations.literal: Thus those who advance enjoy Heaven's stipend, and those who remain at home are at peace in hills and mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who advance enjoy Heaven's stipend, and those who remain at home are at peace in hills and mounds.

sentences.zh: 是以寒暑相推，四宿代中，陰陽不治，運化無窮，自然分定，兩克厥中。

translations.literal: Therefore cold and heat push each other on, the four lodges take turns at the center, yin and yang are not governed by force, movement and transformation are without end, natural allotment is fixed, and both sides attain their mean.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore cold and heat push each other on, the four lodges take turns at the center, yin and yang are not governed by force, movement and transformation are without end, natural allotment is fixed, and both sides attain their mean.

sentences.zh: 二物俱靈，是謂大同；

translations.literal: When the two things are both numinous, this is called great sameness;
translations.idiomatic: When the two things are both numinous, this is called great sameness;

sentences.zh: 彼此無怨，是謂至通。

translations.literal: when neither side resents the other, this is called perfect pervasion.
translations.idiomatic: when neither side resents the other, this is called perfect pervasion.

sentences.zh: 若乃衰周之末，貴詐賤誠，牽於權力，以利要榮。

translations.literal: At the end of declining Zhou, deceit was valued and sincerity despised; men were pulled by power and force, and sought glory through profit.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of declining Zhou, deceit was valued and sincerity despised; men were pulled by power and force, and sought glory through profit.

sentences.zh: 故蘇子出而六主合，張儀入而橫勢成，廉頗存而趙重，樂毅去而燕輕，公叔沒而魏敗，孫臏刖而齊寧，蠡種親而越霸，屈子疏而楚傾。

translations.literal: Thus when Master Su emerged, six rulers allied; when Zhang Yi entered, the horizontal strategy formed; when Lian Po remained, Zhao was weighty; when Yue Yi left, Yan was light; when Gongsun Shu died, Wei was defeated; when Sun Bin was mutilated, Qi became secure; when Fan Li and Wen Zhong were trusted, Yue became hegemon; and when Qu Yuan was estranged, Chu collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Master Su emerged, six rulers allied; when Zhang Yi entered, the horizontal strategy formed; when Lian Po remained, Zhao was weighty; when Yue Yi left, Yan was light; when Gongsun Shu died, Wei was defeated; when Sun Bin was mutilated, Qi became secure; when Fan Li and Wen Zhong were trusted, Yue became hegemon; and when Qu Yuan was estranged, Chu collapsed.

sentences.zh: 是以君無常籍，臣無定名，損義放誠，一虛一盈。

translations.literal: Therefore rulers had no constant register and ministers no fixed name; they damaged rightness and abandoned sincerity, now empty and now full.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore rulers had no constant register and ministers no fixed name; they damaged rightness and abandoned sincerity, now empty and now full.

sentences.zh: 故馮以彈劍感主，女有反賜之說，項奮拔山之力，蒯陳鼎足之勢，東郭劫于田榮，顏闔恥於見逼。

translations.literal: Thus Feng moved his lord by strumming his sword; the woman had the saying about returning the gift; Xiang Yu exerted strength to uproot mountains; Kuai Tong set out the tripod balance; Dongguo was coerced by Tian Rong; and Yan He was ashamed to be pressured.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Feng moved his lord by strumming his sword; the woman had the saying about returning the gift; Xiang Yu exerted strength to uproot mountains; Kuai Tong set out the tripod balance; Dongguo was coerced by Tian Rong; and Yan He was ashamed to be pressured.

sentences.zh: 斯皆棄禮喪真，苟榮朝夕之急者也，豈道化之本與！

translations.literal: All these abandoned ritual and lost truth, seeking only the urgent glory of a morning or evening. How could they be the root of transformation by the Way?
translations.idiomatic: All these abandoned ritual and lost truth, seeking only the urgent glory of a morning or evening. How could they be the root of transformation by the Way?

sentences.zh: 若乃聖帝之創化也，參德乎三皇，齊風乎虞、夏，欲溫溫而和暢，不欲察察而明切也；

translations.literal: As for the sage emperor's founding transformation, his virtue joins the Three Sovereigns and his teaching equals Yu and Xia. He wants warmth and harmonious ease, not sharp clarity and cutting brightness;
translations.idiomatic: As for the sage emperor's founding transformation, his virtue joins the Three Sovereigns and his teaching equals Yu and Xia. He wants warmth and harmonious ease, not sharp clarity and cutting brightness;

sentences.zh: 欲混混若玄流，不欲蕩蕩而名發也；

translations.literal: he wants a deep, blended flow, not broad display with names thrust forward;
translations.idiomatic: he wants a deep, blended flow, not broad display with names thrust forward;

sentences.zh: 欲索索而條解，不欲契契而繩結也；

translations.literal: he wants things loosely untied and ordered, not tightly knotted by cords;
translations.idiomatic: he wants things loosely untied and ordered, not tightly knotted by cords;

sentences.zh: 欲芒芒而無垠際，不欲區區而分別也；

translations.literal: he wants vastness without border or edge, not cramped distinctions;
translations.idiomatic: he wants vastness without border or edge, not cramped distinctions;

sentences.zh: 欲暗然而內章，不欲示白若冰雪也；

translations.literal: he wants dark inward pattern, not displayed whiteness like ice and snow;
translations.idiomatic: he wants dark inward pattern, not displayed whiteness like ice and snow;

sentences.zh: 欲醇醇而任德，不欲瑣瑣而執法也。

translations.literal: he wants rich simplicity that relies on virtue, not petty strictness that clings to law.
translations.idiomatic: he wants rich simplicity that relies on virtue, not petty strictness that clings to law.

sentences.zh: 是以見機者以動成，好遁者無所迫。

translations.literal: Therefore those who see the moment complete things by action, while those who love withdrawal are not forced.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore those who see the moment complete things by action, while those who love withdrawal are not forced.

sentences.zh: 故曰，一明一昧，得道之概；

translations.literal: Thus it is said: one bright and one dim is the outline of attaining the Way;
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is said: one bright and one dim is the outline of attaining the Way;

sentences.zh: 一弛一張，合禮之方；

translations.literal: one relaxed and one taut is the method of according with ritual;
translations.idiomatic: one relaxed and one taut is the method of according with ritual;

sentences.zh: 一浮一沈，兼得其真。

translations.literal: one floating and one sinking together obtain their truth.
translations.idiomatic: one floating and one sinking together obtain their truth.

sentences.zh: 故上有勞謙之愛，下有不名之臣；

translations.literal: Therefore above there is love that honors humility, and below there are ministers who are not named;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore above there is love that honors humility, and below there are ministers who are not named;

sentences.zh: 朝有聘賢之禮，野有遁竄之人。

translations.literal: at court there are rites for inviting worthies, and in the fields there are people who withdraw and hide.
translations.idiomatic: at court there are rites for inviting worthies, and in the fields there are people who withdraw and hide.

sentences.zh: 是以支伯以幽疾距唐，李老寄跡於西鄰，顏氏安陋以成名，原思娛道於至貧，榮期以三樂感尼父，黔婁定諡於布衾，幹木偃息以存魏，荊、萊志邁于江岑，君平因蓍以道著，四皓潛德於洛濱，鄭真躬耕以致譽，幼安發令乎今人。

translations.literal: Thus Zhi Bo rejected Tang because of hidden illness; Old Li lodged his traces in the western neighbor; Yan Hui became famous by resting content in poverty; Yuan Xian delighted in the Way amid utmost poverty; Rong Qiqi moved Confucius with his three joys; Qian Lou fixed his posthumous name under a cloth coverlet; Gan Mu preserved Wei by lying at ease; Jing and Lai set their aims beyond river peaks; Junping made the Way known through milfoil; the Four Graybeards hid their virtue by the Luo; Zheng Zhen won praise by personally farming; and You'an gave a model to people today.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhi Bo rejected Tang because of hidden illness; Old Li lodged his traces in the western neighbor; Yan Hui became famous by resting content in poverty; Yuan Xian delighted in the Way amid utmost poverty; Rong Qiqi moved Confucius with his three joys; Qian Lou fixed his posthumous name under a cloth coverlet; Gan Mu preserved Wei by lying at ease; Jing and Lai set their aims beyond river peaks; Junping made the Way known through milfoil; the Four Graybeards hid their virtue by the Luo; Zheng Zhen won praise by personally farming; and You'an gave a model to people today.

sentences.zh: 皆持難奪之節，執不回之意，遭拔俗之主，全彼人之志。

translations.literal: All held integrity that could not be taken from them, kept an intention that would not turn back, encountered rulers who rose above the vulgar, and preserved those men's aims.
translations.idiomatic: All held integrity that could not be taken from them, kept an intention that would not turn back, encountered rulers who rose above the vulgar, and preserved those men's aims.

sentences.zh: 故有獨定之計者，不借謀於眾人；

translations.literal: Therefore one who has a plan fixed alone does not borrow counsel from the crowd;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one who has a plan fixed alone does not borrow counsel from the crowd;

sentences.zh: 守不動之安者，不假慮於群賓。

translations.literal: one who keeps unmoving peace does not rely on the worries of many guests.
translations.idiomatic: one who keeps unmoving peace does not rely on the worries of many guests.

sentences.zh: 故能棄外親之華，通內道之真，去顯顯之明路，入昧昧之埃塵，宛轉萬情之形表，排托虛寂以寄身，居無事之宅，交釋利之人。

translations.literal: Thus he can abandon the splendor of outward attachment, reach the truth of the inner Way, leave the obvious bright road, enter the dim dust, turn beyond the forms of ten thousand feelings, entrust himself to emptiness and stillness, dwell in the house of non-activity, and associate with people who release profit.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he can abandon the splendor of outward attachment, reach the truth of the inner Way, leave the obvious bright road, enter the dim dust, turn beyond the forms of ten thousand feelings, entrust himself to emptiness and stillness, dwell in the house of non-activity, and associate with people who release profit.

sentences.zh: 輕若鴻毛，重若泥沈，損之不得，測之愈深。

translations.literal: Light as a swan's feather, heavy as sinking mud: diminish him and you cannot; measure him and he grows deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Light as a swan's feather, heavy as sinking mud: diminish him and you cannot; measure him and he grows deeper.

sentences.zh: 真吾徒之師表，餘迫疾而不能及者也。

translations.literal: Such men are truly models for our company; pressed by illness, I cannot reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Such men are truly models for our company; pressed by illness, I cannot reach them.

sentences.zh: 子議吾失宿而駭眾，吾亦怪子較論而不折中也。

translations.literal: You argue that I miss my station and alarm the crowd; I also wonder that your comparisons do not strike the mean.
translations.idiomatic: You argue that I miss my station and alarm the crowd; I also wonder that your comparisons do not strike the mean.

sentences.zh: 夫才不周用，眾所斥也；

translations.literal: Talent not fit for general use is rejected by the crowd;
translations.idiomatic: Talent not fit for general use is rejected by the crowd;

sentences.zh: 寢疾彌年，朝所棄也。

translations.literal: one bedridden with illness for years is abandoned by the court.
translations.idiomatic: one bedridden with illness for years is abandoned by the court.

sentences.zh: 是以胥克之廢，丘明列焉；

translations.literal: Thus Xu Ke's disablement was recorded by Qiuming;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xu Ke's disablement was recorded by Qiuming;

sentences.zh: 伯牛有疾，孔子斯歎。

translations.literal: when Boniu had illness, Confucius sighed over him.
translations.idiomatic: when Boniu had illness, Confucius sighed over him.

sentences.zh: 若黃帝創制於九經，岐伯剖腹以蠲腸，扁鵲造虢而屍起，文摯徇命于齊王，醫和顯術于秦、晉，倉公發秘於漢皇，華佗存精於獨識，仲景垂妙于定方。

translations.literal: If the Yellow Emperor established institutions in the Nine Classics, Qi Bo opened the belly to cleanse the intestines, Bian Que arrived in Guo and made a corpse rise, Wenzhi risked his life with the king of Qi, Physician He displayed his art in Qin and Jin, Cang Gong revealed secrets to the Han emperor, Hua Tuo preserved subtlety in solitary understanding, and Zhongjing left marvels in fixed prescriptions,
translations.idiomatic: If the Yellow Emperor established institutions in the Nine Classics, Qi Bo opened the belly to cleanse the intestines, Bian Que arrived in Guo and made a corpse rise, Wenzhi risked his life with the king of Qi, Physician He displayed his art in Qin and Jin, Cang Gong revealed secrets to the Han emperor, Hua Tuo preserved subtlety in solitary understanding, and Zhongjing left marvels in fixed prescriptions,

sentences.zh: 徒恨生不逢乎若人，故乞命訴乎明王。

translations.literal: I only regret that I was not born to encounter such men, and so I beg for life and appeal to the enlightened king.
translations.idiomatic: I only regret that I was not born to encounter such men, and so I beg for life and appeal to the enlightened king.

sentences.zh: 求絕編於天錄，亮我躬之辛苦，冀微誠之降霜，故俟罪而窮處。」

translations.literal: I ask that my broken register be removed from Heaven's rolls, that the hardship of my body be understood, and that my slight sincerity bring down frost; therefore I await guilt and remain in impoverished seclusion."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that my broken register be removed from Heaven's rolls, that the hardship of my body be understood, and that my slight sincerity bring down frost; therefore I await guilt and remain in impoverished seclusion."

sentences.zh: 其後武帝頻下詔敦逼不已，謐上疏自稱草莽臣曰：「臣以尪弊，迷於道趣，因疾抽簪，散發林阜，人綱不閑，鳥獸為群。

translations.literal: Afterward Emperor Wu repeatedly issued edicts and pressed him without cease. Mi submitted a memorial, calling himself "your servant of the grasses and thickets," saying, "Because I am weak and worn, confused about the direction of the Way, I used illness as cause to pull out my hairpin, let my hair loose among forests and hills, ignored the human bonds, and kept company with birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 陛下披榛采蘭，並收蒿艾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty clears the brush to gather orchids and at the same time gathers mugwort and wormwood.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty clears the thorns for orchids yet gathers humble mugwort as well.

sentences.zh: 是以皋陶振褐，不仁者遠。

translations.literal: Therefore Gao Yao shook his coarse cloak and the unkind went far away.
translations.idiomatic: Thus like Gao Yao of old in plain robes, you drive the vicious away.

sentences.zh: 臣惟頑蒙，備食晉粟，猶識唐人擊壤之樂，宜赴京城，稱壽闕外。

translations.literal: I am only stubbornly ignorant; yet though I merely partake of Jin millet, I still recognize the joy of Tang men beating the earth with clods—I ought to hurry to the capital and wish long life outside the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and untrained, yet even while eating Jin grain I remember the innocent delight of the ancient earth-clod song—I ought to rush to the capital and present my blessings below your gate.

sentences.zh: 而小人無良，致災速禍，久嬰篤疾，軀半不仁，右腳偏小，十有九載。

translations.literal: But this petty man lacks goodness; he has brought disaster and hastened calamity; long afflicted by grave illness, half his body is numb, his right foot is shrunken—it has been nineteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this worthless body has invited sickness: for nineteen years I have suffered paralysis down one side and wasting of the right foot.

sentences.zh: 又服寒食藥，違錯節度，辛苦荼毒，於今七年。

translations.literal: Moreover I took cold-food powder medicine, violated and confused its regimen, and suffered bitter torment—now seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Cold-food elixirs, wrongly dosed, have tormented me without cease these seven years.

sentences.zh: 隆冬裸袒食冰，當暑煩悶，加以咳逆，或若溫虐，或類傷寒，浮氣流腫，四肢酸重。

translations.literal: In deep winter I strip bare and eat ice; in summer heat I am vexed and stifled; added to this coughing fits, sometimes like warm malaria, sometimes resembling cold damage—floating qi flows into swelling, my four limbs ache and feel heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Deep winter finds me naked and chewing ice; midsummer brings feverish oppression, coughing attacks that mimic malaria or typhoid, watery swelling, and leaden limbs.

sentences.zh: 於今困劣，救命呼噏，父兄見出，妻息長訣。

translations.literal: Now I am exhausted and weak, crying out for rescue with gasping breaths; fathers and elder brothers have turned their backs; wife and children must take long farewell.
translations.idiomatic: I am reduced to gasping for breath while kin abandon me and my wife and children prepare their final goodbyes.

sentences.zh: 仰迫天威，扶輿就道，所苦加焉，不任進路，委身待罪，伏枕歎息。

translations.literal: Looking up I am pressed by heavenly majesty; leaning on a carriage I take the road—the suffering increases upon me; I cannot bear to advance on the route; I cast myself aside awaiting punishment, lying on my pillow sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Yielding to imperial pressure I would drag myself onto the road, yet the journey would only worsen my pain; I cannot travel—I throw myself on your mercy and sigh upon my pillow.

sentences.zh: 臣聞《韶》《衛》不並奏，《雅》《鄭》不兼禦，故郤子入周，禍延王叔；

translations.literal: I have heard that Shao and Wei are not performed together, Ya and Zheng are not driven together by reins—therefore when the Xi lord entered Zhou, calamity extended to Prince Shu;
translations.idiomatic: As Shao and Wei were never played together, nor courtly airs mixed with Zheng tunes, the Xi heir's entry into Zhou spelled doom even for royal uncles.

sentences.zh: 虞丘稱賢，樊姬掩口。

translations.literal: When Yuqiu was praised as worthy, Lady Fan covered her mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuqiu was hailed as a sage minister, Lady Fan of Chu hid a smile behind her sleeve.

sentences.zh: 君子小人，禮不同器，況臣糠䵃，糅之彫胡？

translations.literal: Gentleman and petty man—rite does not share the same vessel with them—how much more am I chaff and bran to be mixed with polished foxtail millet?
translations.idiomatic: Nobles and commoners were never served from the same bowl; how much less fit am I, mere bran, to be tossed with polished grain?

sentences.zh: 庸夫錦衣，不稱其服也。

translations.literal: A common fellow in brocade robes does not match his garments.
translations.idiomatic: Silk on a dullard never sits right.

sentences.zh: 竊聞同命之士，咸以畢到，唯臣疾疢，抱釁床蓐，雖貪明時，懼斃命路隅。

translations.literal: I have privately heard that gentlemen sharing the same summons have all arrived to completion; only I, sickly and clutching fault upon mat and bedding—though I covet this enlightened age, fear expiring by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: Others summoned with me have reported for duty; I alone lie sick on my couch—however much I cherish your reign, I would only collapse on the road.

sentences.zh: 設臣不疾，已遭堯、舜之世，執志箕山，猶當容之。

translations.literal: Suppose I were not ill: having encountered the age of Yao and Shun, yet holding firm my resolve on Mount Ji, they still ought to tolerate me.
translations.idiomatic: Even if I were well, in an age as benign as Yao and Shun's a recluse who clung to Mount Ji would still deserve indulgence.

sentences.zh: 臣聞上有明聖之主，下有輸實之臣；

translations.literal: I have heard that above there is an enlightened sage lord; below there are ministers who convey substance;
translations.idiomatic: Where the throne shines bright, ministers speak plain truth;

sentences.zh: 上有在寬之政，下有委情之人。

translations.literal: above there is governance that resides in lenience; below there are men who entrust their genuine feelings.
translations.idiomatic: where policy stays generous, subjects may lay bare their hearts.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下留神垂恕，更旌瑰俊，索隱于傅岩，收釣於渭濱，無令泥滓久濁清流。」

translations.literal: Please, Your Majesty, attend to this and extend forgiveness; further honor rare talents, seek hidden men at Fu Rock, gather the angler on the Wei bank, and do not let mud and sediment long foul the clear stream."
translations.idiomatic: Please, Your Majesty, attend to this and extend forgiveness; further honor rare talents, seek hidden men at Fu Rock, gather the angler on the Wei bank, and do not let mud and sediment long foul the clear stream."

sentences.zh: 謐辭切言至，遂見聽許。

translations.literal: Mi's words were cutting and his expressions extreme; thereupon he was heard and permitted.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was urgent and heartfelt, and the throne granted his excuse.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，又舉賢良方正，並不起。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was again nominated Worthy and Good and Upright and Irregular—all without rising.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was nominated again as Worthy and Upright but still refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 自表就帝借書，帝送一車書與之。

translations.literal: He personally memorialized asking to borrow books from the emperor; the emperor sent him a cartload of books.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the throne for library loans and received an entire cart of texts.

sentences.zh: 謐雖羸疾，而披閱不怠。

translations.literal: Although Mi was emaciated from illness, he read without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Frail as he was, he never tired of reading.

sentences.zh: 初服寒食散，而性與之忤，每委頓不倫，嘗悲恚，叩刃欲自殺，叔母諫之而止。

translations.literal: When he first took cold-food powder, his nature ran counter to it; each time he collapsed in disorder, once he was grief-stricken and angry, knocked a blade and wished to kill himself—his aunt by adoption remonstrated and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Cold-food elixirs disagreed with his constitution: fits left him half dead with rage; once he seized a blade to end his life until his aunt talked him down.

sentences.zh: 濟陰太守蜀人文立，表以命士有贄為煩，請絕其禮幣，詔從之。

translations.literal: Wen Li of Shu, governor of Jiyin, memorialized that for mandated scholars having gifts was troublesome and requested to cut off their ritual silk offerings—the edict followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Li, governor of Jiyin, petitioned to scrap presentation gifts for appointed scholars, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 謐聞而歎曰：「亡國之大夫不可與圖存，而以革歷代之制，其可乎！

translations.literal: Mi heard this and sighed, saying: 'The grand officers of a destroyed state cannot be plotted with for preservation—yet by this alter institutions handed down through dynasties—is it acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi sighed: "Ministers of a fallen regime are poor counselors—yet does that justify junking age-old courtesy gifts?

sentences.zh: 夫『束帛戔戔』，《易》之明義，玄纁之贄，自古之舊也。

translations.literal: As for 'bundles of silk in abundance'—it is the clear meaning of the Changes; dark and light silk as gifts is an ancient usage.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes celebrates stacked silks; dark-red presents are an immemorial custom.

sentences.zh: 故孔子稱夙夜強學以待問，席上之珍以待聘。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius praised studying hard morning and night to await questioning; treasures on the mat to await employment.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius urged scholars to master learning day and night and keep their talents like treasures spread for a worthy summons.

sentences.zh: 士於是乎三揖乃進，明致之難也；

translations.literal: The gentleman on this account bows three times only then advances—clarifying that bringing him in is difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Three deferential bows before stepping forward showed how hard it was to earn an invitation;

sentences.zh: 一讓而退，明去之易也。

translations.literal: one yielding then withdrawing—clarifying that leaving is easy.
translations.idiomatic: one courteous refusal and withdrawal showed how easily honor could be declined.

sentences.zh: 若殷湯之于伊尹，文王之于太公，或身即莘野，或就載以歸，唯恐禮之不重，豈吝其煩費哉！

translations.literal: Like Tang of Yin toward Yi Yin, King Wen toward the Grand Duke—sometimes the body itself goes to the wilderness of Shen, sometimes one rides the carriage to return—only fearing that the rite is not heavy; how could they be stingy about the bother and expense!
translations.idiomatic: King Tang visited Yi Yin in the wilds; King Wen fetched the Grand Duke in his carriage—they strained every ritual courtesy and never grudged the cost.

sentences.zh: 且一禮不備，貞女恥之，況命士乎！

translations.literal: Moreover if one rite is not complete, a chaste woman is shamed by it—how much more a mandated scholar!
translations.idiomatic: A modest maiden blushes if any courtesy is omitted—how much more a sworn scholar!

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『賜也，爾愛其羊，我愛其禮。』

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Si, you cherish your sheep; I cherish the rite.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius told Zigong: you fret over the sheep; I care about the ritual."

sentences.zh: 棄之如何？

translations.literal: If one discards it—what of it?
translations.idiomatic: What happens when we throw such traditions away?

sentences.zh: 政之失賢，於此乎在矣。」

translations.literal: The government's losing worthy men—herein does it lie.'
translations.idiomatic: This is how states lose their best men."

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，又詔曰：「男子皇甫謐沈靜履素，守學好古，與流俗異趣，其以謐為太子中庶子。」

translations.literal: Early in Xianning, another edict said: "The gentleman Huangfu Mi is calm, quiet, and plain in conduct, keeps to learning and loves antiquity, and his aims differ from vulgar currents. Let Mi be made Palace Attendant to the heir apparent."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning, another edict said: "The gentleman Huangfu Mi is calm, quiet, and plain in conduct, keeps to learning and loves antiquity, and his aims differ from vulgar currents. Let Mi be made Palace Attendant to the heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 謐固辭篤疾。

translations.literal: Mi firmly declined on account of grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded grave illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 帝初雖不奪其志，尋復發詔徵為議郎，又召補著作郎。

translations.literal: The emperor at first though not wresting his intent, soon again issued an edict summoning him as Gentleman Consultant, and again summoned him to supplement as Editorial Director.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first respected his wishes but soon summoned him as Gentleman Consultant and Editorial Director.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉劉毅請為功曹，並不應。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Commandant Liu Yi requested him as clerk of merit—together he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, the metropolitan inspector, wanted him as clerk of records—again he declined.

sentences.zh: 著論為葬送之制，名曰《篤終》，曰：

translations.literal: He composed a treatise setting forth regulations for burial and sending-off, titled "Steadfast at the End." It says:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a treatise on funeral practice titled "Steadfast at the End." It says:

sentences.zh: 玄晏先生以為存亡天地之定制，人理之必至也。

translations.literal: Master Xuanyan held that life and death are fixed ordinances of Heaven and Earth, and the necessary end of human principle.
translations.idiomatic: Master Xuanyan held that life and death are fixed ordinances of Heaven and Earth, and the necessary end of human principle.

sentences.zh: 故禮六十而制壽，至於九十，各有等差，防終以素，豈流俗之多忌者哉！

translations.literal: Therefore the rites prepare for longevity at sixty and continue to ninety, each with graded distinctions; guarding the end with plainness is not the many taboos of vulgar custom.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the rites prepare for longevity at sixty and continue to ninety, each with graded distinctions; guarding the end with plainness is not the many taboos of vulgar custom.

sentences.zh: 吾年雖未制壽，然嬰疢彌紀，仍遭喪難，神氣損劣，困頓數矣。

translations.literal: Although my age has not yet reached the point for arranging longevity rites, I have suffered illness for a full twelve years, repeatedly met bereavement and hardship, and my spirit and vital force are damaged and weak; I have been brought low many times.
translations.idiomatic: Although my age has not yet reached the point for arranging longevity rites, I have suffered illness for a full twelve years, repeatedly met bereavement and hardship, and my spirit and vital force are damaged and weak; I have been brought low many times.

sentences.zh: 常懼夭隕不期，慮終無素，是以略陳至懷。

translations.literal: I have often feared an unexpected early fall and worried that my end would have no prior arrangement, so I briefly set forth my deepest intent.
translations.idiomatic: I have often feared an unexpected early fall and worried that my end would have no prior arrangement, so I briefly set forth my deepest intent.

sentences.zh: 夫人之所貪者，生也；

translations.literal: What people cling to is life;
translations.idiomatic: What people cling to is life;

sentences.zh: 所惡者，死也。

translations.literal: what they hate is death.
translations.idiomatic: what they hate is death.

sentences.zh: 雖貪，不得越期；

translations.literal: Yet though one clings to it, one cannot pass beyond one's allotted term;
translations.idiomatic: Yet though one clings to it, one cannot pass beyond one's allotted term;

sentences.zh: 雖惡，不可逃遁。

translations.literal: though one hates it, one cannot flee away.
translations.idiomatic: though one hates it, one cannot flee away.

sentences.zh: 人之死也，精歇形散，魂無不之，故氣屬於天；

translations.literal: When a person dies, essence comes to rest and form disperses; the soul goes everywhere, and so the qi belongs to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When a person dies, essence comes to rest and form disperses; the soul goes everywhere, and so the qi belongs to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 寄命終盡，窮體反真，故屍藏於地。

translations.literal: When the lodged life has ended and the exhausted body returns to truth, the corpse is stored in Earth.
translations.idiomatic: When the lodged life has ended and the exhausted body returns to truth, the corpse is stored in Earth.

sentences.zh: 是以神不存體，則與氣升降；

translations.literal: Thus when the spirit no longer remains in the body, it rises and falls with qi;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the spirit no longer remains in the body, it rises and falls with qi;

sentences.zh: 屍不久寄，與地合形。

translations.literal: when the corpse is no longer lodged for long, its form joins the earth.
translations.idiomatic: when the corpse is no longer lodged for long, its form joins the earth.

sentences.zh: 形神不隔，天地之性也；

translations.literal: That form and spirit not be separated is the nature of Heaven and Earth;
translations.idiomatic: That form and spirit not be separated is the nature of Heaven and Earth;

sentences.zh: 屍與土並，反真之理也。

translations.literal: that the corpse be together with soil is the principle of returning to truth.
translations.idiomatic: that the corpse be together with soil is the principle of returning to truth.

sentences.zh: 今生不能保七尺之軀，死何故隔一棺之土？

translations.literal: If in life one cannot preserve a seven-foot body, why after death should one be separated from the soil by a coffin?
translations.idiomatic: If in life one cannot preserve a seven-foot body, why after death should one be separated from the soil by a coffin?

sentences.zh: 然則衣衾所以穢屍，棺槨所以隔真，故桓司馬石槨不如速朽；

translations.literal: Thus clothing and coverlets only foul the corpse, and coffin and outer coffin only separate it from truth. For this reason Huan Sima's stone outer coffin was not as good as quick decay;
translations.idiomatic: Thus clothing and coverlets only foul the corpse, and coffin and outer coffin only separate it from truth. For this reason Huan Sima's stone outer coffin was not as good as quick decay;

sentences.zh: 季孫璵璠比之暴骸；

translations.literal: Ji Sun's jade ornaments were compared to exposing the bones;
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sun's jade ornaments were compared to exposing the bones;

sentences.zh: 文公厚葬，《春秋》以為華元不臣；

translations.literal: when Wen Gong was buried extravagantly, the Chunqiu, the Spring and Autumn, judged Hua Yuan an unworthy minister;
translations.idiomatic: when Wen Gong was buried extravagantly, the Chunqiu, the Spring and Autumn, judged Hua Yuan an unworthy minister;

sentences.zh: 楊王孫親土，《漢書》以為賢于秦始皇。

translations.literal: and because Yang Wangsun returned directly to the soil, the Book of Han judged him wiser than the First Emperor of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: and because Yang Wangsun returned directly to the soil, the Book of Han judged him wiser than the First Emperor of Qin.

sentences.zh: 如今魂必有知，則人鬼異制，黃泉之親，死多於生，必將備其器物，用待亡者。

translations.literal: If the soul must have awareness, then humans and ghosts have different institutions; kin in the Yellow Springs are more numerous dead than alive, and must already have prepared vessels and goods with which to receive the deceased.
translations.idiomatic: If the soul must have awareness, then humans and ghosts have different institutions; kin in the Yellow Springs are more numerous dead than alive, and must already have prepared vessels and goods with which to receive the deceased.

sentences.zh: 今若以存況終，非即靈之意也。

translations.literal: If now one treats the end by analogy with the living, this does not accord with the intention of the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: If now one treats the end by analogy with the living, this does not accord with the intention of the spirit.

sentences.zh: 如其無知，則空奪生用，損之無益，而啟奸心，是招露形之禍，增亡者之毒也。

translations.literal: If the dead have no awareness, then one merely steals resources from the living, causes loss without benefit, and opens wicked hearts; this invites the calamity of exposed bodies and increases the harm done to the dead.
translations.idiomatic: If the dead have no awareness, then one merely steals resources from the living, causes loss without benefit, and opens wicked hearts; this invites the calamity of exposed bodies and increases the harm done to the dead.

sentences.zh: 夫葬者，藏也，藏也者，欲人之不得見也。

translations.literal: Burial means hiding; to hide means wishing people not to see.
translations.idiomatic: Burial means hiding; to hide means wishing people not to see.

sentences.zh: 而大為棺槨，備贈存物，無異于埋金路隅而書表於上也。

translations.literal: But to make great coffins and outer coffins and fully provide gifts and living goods is no different from burying gold by the roadside and writing a marker above it.
translations.idiomatic: But to make great coffins and outer coffins and fully provide gifts and living goods is no different from burying gold by the roadside and writing a marker above it.

sentences.zh: 雖甚愚之人，必將笑之。

translations.literal: Even the most foolish person would surely laugh at it.
translations.idiomatic: Even the most foolish person would surely laugh at it.

sentences.zh: 豐財厚葬以啟奸心，或剖破棺槨，或牽曳形骸，或剝臂捋金環，或捫腸求珠玉。

translations.literal: Rich goods and lavish burial open wicked hearts: some split coffins and outer coffins, some drag the body, some strip arms to pull off gold bracelets, and some grope through intestines in search of pearls and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Rich goods and lavish burial open wicked hearts: some split coffins and outer coffins, some drag the body, some strip arms to pull off gold bracelets, and some grope through intestines in search of pearls and jade.

sentences.zh: 焚如之形，不痛於是？

translations.literal: Could the burned and ravaged body suffer anything more painful than this?
translations.idiomatic: Could the burned and ravaged body suffer anything more painful than this?

sentences.zh: 自古及今，未有不死之人，又無不發之墓也。

translations.literal: From antiquity to now there has never been a person who does not die, and there is no tomb that will never be opened.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity to now there has never been a person who does not die, and there is no tomb that will never be opened.

sentences.zh: 故張釋之曰：「使其中有欲，雖固南山猶有隙；使其中無欲，雖無石槨，又何戚焉！」

translations.literal: Therefore Zhang Shizhi said, "If there is something desired inside it, then even if it is as solid as the Southern Mountain, there will still be a crack; if there is nothing desired inside it, then even without a stone outer coffin, what is there to grieve over?"
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zhang Shizhi said, "If there is something desired inside it, then even if it is as solid as the Southern Mountain, there will still be a crack; if there is nothing desired inside it, then even without a stone outer coffin, what is there to grieve over?"

sentences.zh: 斯言達矣，吾之師也。

translations.literal: These words are penetrating; they are my teacher.
translations.idiomatic: These words are penetrating; they are my teacher.

sentences.zh: 夫贈終加厚，非厚死也，生者自為也。

translations.literal: To make farewell gifts increasingly lavish is not treating the dead generously; it is something the living do for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: To make farewell gifts increasingly lavish is not treating the dead generously; it is something the living do for themselves.

sentences.zh: 遂生意于無益，棄死者之所屬，知者所不行也。

translations.literal: To let intentions grow around what has no benefit and abandon what belongs to the dead is not something the wise do.
translations.idiomatic: To let intentions grow around what has no benefit and abandon what belongs to the dead is not something the wise do.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱「古之葬者，衣之以薪，葬之中野，不封不樹」。

translations.literal: The Changes says, "In ancient burials, they clothed the dead in firewood and buried them in the open fields, without mound or trees."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "In ancient burials, they clothed the dead in firewood and buried them in the open fields, without mound or trees."

sentences.zh: 是以死得歸真，亡不損生。

translations.literal: Thus the dead returned to truth, and death did not injure the living.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the dead returned to truth, and death did not injure the living.

sentences.zh: 故吾欲朝死夕葬，夕死朝葬，不設棺槨，不加纏斂，不修沐浴，不造新服，殯唅之物，一皆絕之。

translations.literal: Therefore I wish that if I die in the morning I be buried that evening, and if I die in the evening I be buried the next morning; no coffin or outer coffin should be set up, no wrapping or shrouding added, no washing performed, no new clothes made, and all goods for lying-in-state or mouth-jade abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I wish that if I die in the morning I be buried that evening, and if I die in the evening I be buried the next morning; no coffin or outer coffin should be set up, no wrapping or shrouding added, no washing performed, no new clothes made, and all goods for lying-in-state or mouth-jade abolished.

sentences.zh: 吾本欲露形入坑，以身親土，或恐人情染俗來久，頓革理難，今故觕為之制，奢不石槨，儉不露形。

translations.literal: I originally wished to enter the pit with my body exposed and let my body touch the soil; but fearing that human feelings have long been dyed by custom and sudden reform would be difficult in principle, I now make a rough rule: its extravagance does not reach a stone outer coffin, and its frugality does not expose the body.
translations.idiomatic: I originally wished to enter the pit with my body exposed and let my body touch the soil; but fearing that human feelings have long been dyed by custom and sudden reform would be difficult in principle, I now make a rough rule: its extravagance does not reach a stone outer coffin, and its frugality does not expose the body.

sentences.zh: 氣絕之後，便即時服，幅巾故衣，以遽除裹屍，麻約二頭，置屍床上。

translations.literal: After my breath ceases, dress me immediately in a plain kerchief and old clothes, wrap the corpse with a coarse cover, tie both ends with hemp, and place it on a corpse-bed.
translations.idiomatic: After my breath ceases, dress me immediately in a plain kerchief and old clothes, wrap the corpse with a coarse cover, tie both ends with hemp, and place it on a corpse-bed.

sentences.zh: 擇不毛之地，穿坑深十尺，長一丈五尺，廣六尺，坑訖，舉床就坑，去床下屍。

translations.literal: Choose barren ground and dig a pit ten feet deep, one zhang and five feet long, and six feet wide; when the pit is finished, carry the bed to the pit and lower the corpse from the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Choose barren ground and dig a pit ten feet deep, one zhang and five feet long, and six feet wide; when the pit is finished, carry the bed to the pit and lower the corpse from the bed.

sentences.zh: 平生之物，皆無自隨，唯齎《孝經》一卷，示不忘孝道。

translations.literal: None of my lifetime possessions should accompany me; bring only one scroll of the Classic of Filial Piety, to show that I did not forget the Way of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: None of my lifetime possessions should accompany me; bring only one scroll of the Classic of Filial Piety, to show that I did not forget the Way of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 遽除之外，便以親土。

translations.literal: Apart from the coarse covering, let me touch the soil.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the coarse covering, let me touch the soil.

sentences.zh: 土與地平，還其故草，使生其上，無種樹木、削除，使生跡無處，自求不知。

translations.literal: Make the soil level with the ground, return the old grasses so they grow above it, plant no trees and clear away nothing, so that the trace of growth has no marked place and by itself seeks to be unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Make the soil level with the ground, return the old grasses so they grow above it, plant no trees and clear away nothing, so that the trace of growth has no marked place and by itself seeks to be unknown.

sentences.zh: 不見可欲，則奸不生心，終始無怵惕，千載不慮患。

translations.literal: If nothing desirable is seen, wickedness will not arise in the heart; from beginning to end there will be no fear, and for a thousand years there will be no worry over calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If nothing desirable is seen, wickedness will not arise in the heart; from beginning to end there will be no fear, and for a thousand years there will be no worry over calamity.

sentences.zh: 形骸與后土同體，魂爽與元氣合靈，真篤愛之至也。

translations.literal: The body and bones will share substance with the Queen Earth; the bright soul will join its spirit with primal qi. This is the utmost of true and deep love.
translations.idiomatic: The body and bones will share substance with the Queen Earth; the bright soul will join its spirit with primal qi. This is the utmost of true and deep love.

sentences.zh: 若亡有前後，不得移祔。

translations.literal: If deaths occur at different times, there must be no moving for joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: If deaths occur at different times, there must be no moving for joint burial.

sentences.zh: 祔葬自周公來，非古制也。

translations.literal: Joint burial has come down from the Duke of Zhou; it is not an ancient institution.
translations.idiomatic: Joint burial has come down from the Duke of Zhou; it is not an ancient institution.

sentences.zh: 舜葬蒼梧，二妃不從，以為一定，何必周禮。

translations.literal: Shun was buried at Cangwu and his two consorts did not follow him; take this as fixed. Why must one follow the Zhou rites?
translations.idiomatic: Shun was buried at Cangwu and his two consorts did not follow him; take this as fixed. Why must one follow the Zhou rites?

sentences.zh: 無問師工，無信卜筮，無拘俗言，無張神坐，無十五日朝夕上食。

translations.literal: Do not ask ritual masters or artisans, do not trust divination by turtle or milfoil, do not be bound by vulgar sayings, do not set up a spirit seat, and do not offer food morning and evening for fifteen days.
translations.idiomatic: Do not ask ritual masters or artisans, do not trust divination by turtle or milfoil, do not be bound by vulgar sayings, do not set up a spirit seat, and do not offer food morning and evening for fifteen days.

sentences.zh: 禮不墓祭，但月朔于家設席以祭，百日而止。

translations.literal: Ritual does not sacrifice at the tomb; merely set a mat at home and sacrifice on the first day of the month, stopping after a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual does not sacrifice at the tomb; merely set a mat at home and sacrifice on the first day of the month, stopping after a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 臨必昏明，不得以夜。

translations.literal: Condolence visits must be at dusk or dawn, not at night.
translations.idiomatic: Condolence visits must be at dusk or dawn, not at night.

sentences.zh: 制服常居，不得墓次。

translations.literal: Wear mourning garments in ordinary residence; do not stay beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Wear mourning garments in ordinary residence; do not stay beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 夫古不崇墓，智也。

translations.literal: In antiquity people did not exalt tombs; this was wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity people did not exalt tombs; this was wisdom.

sentences.zh: 今之封樹，愚也。

translations.literal: Today's mounds and trees are folly.
translations.idiomatic: Today's mounds and trees are folly.

sentences.zh: 若不從此，是戮屍地下，死而重傷。

translations.literal: If these instructions are not followed, this is to mutilate my corpse underground and wound me again after death.
translations.idiomatic: If these instructions are not followed, this is to mutilate my corpse underground and wound me again after death.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，則冤悲沒世，長為恨鬼。

translations.literal: If the soul has spirit, then its grievance and sorrow will last forever, and it will long remain a resentful ghost.
translations.idiomatic: If the soul has spirit, then its grievance and sorrow will last forever, and it will long remain a resentful ghost.

sentences.zh: 王孫之子，可以為誡。

translations.literal: The sons of Wangsun may serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Wangsun may serve as a warning.

sentences.zh: 死誓難違，幸無改焉！

translations.literal: A deathbed oath is hard to violate; I hope there will be no alteration!
translations.idiomatic: A deathbed oath is hard to violate; I hope there will be no alteration!

sentences.zh: 而竟不仕。

translations.literal: In the end, he never took office.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, he never took office.

sentences.zh: 太康三年卒，時年六十八。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Taikang, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Taikang, at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子童靈、方回等遵其遺命。

translations.literal: His sons Tongling, Fang Hui, and others followed his testamentary commands.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Tongling and Fang Hui carried out his last wishes.

sentences.zh: 謐所著詩賦誄頌論難甚多，又撰《帝王世紀》、《年曆》、《高士》、《逸士》、《列女》等傳、《玄晏春秋》，並重於世。

translations.literal: Mi wrote many poems, fu, laments, hymns, essays, and debates; he also compiled the Diwang Shiji, Calendars, biographies of Lofty Gentlemen, Retired Gentlemen, and Exemplary Women, and the Xuanyan Chunqiu, all of which were valued in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Mi wrote many poems, fu, laments, hymns, essays, and debates; he also compiled the Diwang Shiji, Calendars, biographies of Lofty Gentlemen, Retired Gentlemen, and Exemplary Women, and the Xuanyan Chunqiu, all of which were valued in his age.

sentences.zh: 門人摯虞、張軌、牛綜、席純，皆為晉名臣。

translations.literal: His disciples Zhi Yu, Zhang Gui, Niu Zong, and Xi Chun all became renowned ministers of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Among his pupils Zhi Yu, Zhang Gui, Niu Zong, and Xi Chun rose to distinction under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 子方回

translations.literal: Son Fang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fang Hui.

sentences.zh: =方回少遵父操，兼有文才。

translations.literal: Fang Hui, in his youth, observed his father's conduct; he also possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Hui followed his father's austere example from youth and showed literary gifts of his own.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，博士征，不起。
