translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongjia, the erudite office summoned him; he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongjia opened he was called to the academy doctorate but would not go.

sentences.zh: 避亂荊州，閉戶閒居，未嘗入城府。

translations.literal: Fleeing turmoil he went to Jingzhou, closed his doors and dwelt at leisure, never entering the commandery or prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: He fled the turmoil to Jingzhou, kept to his home, and never set foot in the regional seat.

sentences.zh: 蠶而後衣，耕而後食，先人後己，尊賢愛物，南土人士咸崇敬之。

translations.literal: He clothed himself after silkworms, ate after plowing; he put others before himself, honored the worthy and cherished creatures—gentlemen of the southern lands all revered him.
translations.idiomatic: He spun before he dressed, tilled before he ate, put others first, honored talent and cherished life—southerners held him in universal esteem.

sentences.zh: 刺史陶侃禮之甚厚。

translations.literal: Inspector Tao Kan treated him with very great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tao Kan showed him exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 侃每造之，著素士服，望門輒下而進。

translations.literal: Whenever Kan went to visit him, he wore plain scholar's garb; seeing the gate he dismounted from his carriage and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tao Kan called, he dressed as a simple scholar, dismounted at the gate, and walked in.

sentences.zh: 王敦遣從弟暠代侃，遷侃為廣州。

translations.literal: Wang Dun sent his cousin Wang Hao to replace Kan and transferred Kan to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun posted his cousin Wang Hao to supplant Tao Kan and moved Kan south to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 侃將詣敦，方回諫曰：「吾聞敵國滅，功臣亡。

translations.literal: When Kan was about to go to Wang Dun, Fang Hui remonstrated, saying: 'I have heard that when an enemy state is destroyed, the merit ministers perish.
translations.idiomatic: As Tao Kan prepared to visit Wang Dun, Fang Hui warned: "They say when the rival realm falls, its champions are next.

sentences.zh: 足下新破杜弢，功莫與二，欲無危，其可得乎！」

translations.literal: You have newly broken Du Tao; merit matches no second—desiring to have no danger—how can it be obtained!'
translations.idiomatic: You have just crushed Du Tao—no one rivals your fame—do you really expect to stay safe?"

sentences.zh: 侃不從而行。

translations.literal: Kan did not follow and went.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan ignored him and went anyway.

sentences.zh: 敦果欲殺侃，賴周訪獲免。

translations.literal: Dun indeed wished to kill Kan; he relied on Zhou Fang to obtain escape.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun nearly had him killed; only Zhou Fang's intervention saved him.

sentences.zh: 暠既至荊州，大失物情，百姓叛暠迎杜弢。

translations.literal: After Hao arrived in Jingzhou, he greatly lost the sentiment of things; commoners rebelled against Hao and welcomed Du Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Hao took Jingzhou he forfeited popular support; people rose against him and sided with Du Tao.

sentences.zh: 暠大行誅戮以立威，以方回為侃所敬，責其不來詣己，乃收而斬之。

translations.literal: Hao carried out great executions and slaughterings to establish awe; because Fang Hui was one whom Kan respected, he blamed him for not coming to visit himself—thereupon seized him and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao tried to terrify the region with executions; resenting Fang Hui's prestige—Tao Kan still revered him—he arrested Hui for refusing a personal audience and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 荊土華夷，莫不流涕。

translations.literal: Chinese and barbarians of Jing lands—there were none who did not shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese and tribal peoples across Jing mourned him.

sentences.zh: 摯虞

translations.literal: Zhi Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Zhi Yu.

sentences.zh: 摯虞，字仲洽，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu, courtesy name Zhongqia, was a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu, styled Zhongqia, came from Chang'an in the Jingzhao capital district.

sentences.zh: 父模，魏太僕卿。

translations.literal: His father Mo served Wei as Minister Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi Mo had been Wei Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 虞少事皇甫謐，才學通博，著述不倦。

translations.literal: Yu in youth studied under Huangfu Mi; his talent and learning were comprehensive and broad; he wrote tirelessly.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he studied under Huangfu Mi, mastered wide learning, and wrote indefatigably.

sentences.zh: 郡檄主簿。

translations.literal: The commandery drafted him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery drafted him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 虞嘗以死生有命，富貴在天。

translations.literal: Yu once held that death and life have their allotments, wealth and honor lie with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu held that life span and fate are fixed, rank and wealth heaven-sent.

sentences.zh: 天之所祐者義也，人之所助者信也。

translations.literal: What Heaven aids is righteousness; what men help is trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven blesses those who live rightly; men rally to those who keep faith.

sentences.zh: 履信思順，所以延福，違此而行，所以速禍。

translations.literal: Walking trust and thinking compliance—by this one extends blessing; violating this and acting—by this one hastens calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Integrity and prudence lengthen fortune; their opposite hastens disaster.

sentences.zh: 然道長世短，禍福舛錯，怵迫之徒，不知所守，蕩而積憤，或迷或放。

translations.literal: Yet the Way is long and the age short; blessing and calamity are crossed and confused; those driven by fear and pressure do not know what they guard; dissipated they accumulate resentment—some lost, some unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the path is long while life is brief; fortune and disaster tangle; anxious souls lose their bearings, drift, and stockpile resentment—some grow deluded, others reckless.

sentences.zh: 故借之以身，假之以事，先陳處世不遇之難，遂棄彝倫，輕舉遠遊，以極常人罔惑之情，而後引之以正，反之以義，推神明之應於視聽之表，崇否泰之運于智力之外，以明天任命之不可違，故作《思遊賦》。

translations.literal: Therefore he borrowed it with his person, lent it with affairs—first setting forth the hardship of not meeting one's time in dwelling in the world, thereupon abandoning constant norms, lightly rising and roaming far, to exhaust the feelings by which ordinary men are deluded and confused, and afterward leading them with rectitude, returning them with righteousness, inferring spirit illumination's responses beyond sight and hearing, exalting the turns of blockage and ease outside intelligence and strength, to clarify that Heaven-mandated destiny cannot be disobeyed—therefore he composed 'Fu on Pondering Roaming.'
translations.idiomatic: So he used his own story and imagined journeys—first sketching the bitterness of unappreciated scholars who abandon duty for restless travel, mapping ordinary confusion, then steering readers back toward righteousness, arguing that divine response lies beyond the senses and fortune beyond clever plans, all to show heaven's decree cannot be resisted; hence his "Rhapsody on Roaming Thought."

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：有軒轅之遐胄兮，氏仲任之洪裔。

translations.literal: Its text says: There was a distant descendant of Xuanyuan, a great scion of the house of Zhongren.
translations.idiomatic: The fu begins: There was a distant descendant of Xuanyuan, a great scion of the Zhongren clan.

sentences.zh: 敷華穎於末葉兮，晞靈根於上世。

translations.literal: He spread flower and tassel in the last leaves, and looked back toward numinous roots in the ancient age.
translations.idiomatic: He spread flower and tassel in the last leaves, and looked back toward numinous roots in the ancient age.

sentences.zh: 准乾坤以斡度兮，儀陰陽以定制。

translations.literal: He took Heaven and Earth as standard to turn the measures, and modeled yin and yang to fix institutions.
translations.idiomatic: He took Heaven and Earth as standard to turn the measures, and modeled yin and yang to fix institutions.

sentences.zh: 匪時運其焉行兮，乘太虛而搖曳。

translations.literal: It was not the movement of the age that made him go; he rode the Great Void and drifted.
translations.idiomatic: It was not the movement of the age that made him go; he rode the Great Void and drifted.

sentences.zh: 戴朗月之高冠兮，綴太白之明璜。

translations.literal: He wore a high cap of bright moonlight, and strung bright jade from Great White.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a high cap of bright moonlight, and strung bright jade from Great White.

sentences.zh: 制文霓以為衣兮，襲采雲以為裳。

translations.literal: He fashioned patterned rainbows as his robe and layered colored clouds as his skirt.
translations.idiomatic: He fashioned patterned rainbows as his robe and layered colored clouds as his skirt.

sentences.zh: 要華電之煜爚兮，珮玉衡之琳琅。

translations.literal: He belted flashing splendor of lightning and wore the jade balance ringing with gems.
translations.idiomatic: He belted flashing splendor of lightning and wore the jade balance ringing with gems.

sentences.zh: 明景日以鑒形兮，信煥曜而重光。

translations.literal: He used the bright sun to mirror his form; truly he blazed and doubled the light.
translations.idiomatic: He used the bright sun to mirror his form; truly he blazed and doubled the light.

sentences.zh: 至美詭好於凡觀兮，修稀合而靡呈。

translations.literal: Utmost beauty and strange loveliness are beyond common sight; rare perfection is seldom displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Utmost beauty and strange loveliness are beyond common sight; rare perfection is seldom displayed.

sentences.zh: 燕石緹襲以華國兮，和璞遙棄于南荊。

translations.literal: Yan stones are wrapped in red and used to adorn the state, while the He jade is cast far away in southern Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan stones are wrapped in red and used to adorn the state, while the He jade is cast far away in southern Jing.

sentences.zh: 夏像韜塵於市北兮，瓶罍抗方於兩楹。

translations.literal: The Xia image is hidden in dust north of the market, while jars and wine vessels stand squarely between the pillars.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia image is hidden in dust north of the market, while jars and wine vessels stand squarely between the pillars.

sentences.zh: 鸞皇耿介而偏棲兮，蘭桂背時而獨榮。

translations.literal: Luan and phoenix, upright and aloof, perch apart; orchid and cassia, out of season, bloom alone.
translations.idiomatic: Luan and phoenix, upright and aloof, perch apart; orchid and cassia, out of season, bloom alone.

sentences.zh: 關寒暑以練真兮，豈改容而爽情。

translations.literal: They pass through cold and heat to refine truth; how could they change appearance and betray feeling?
translations.idiomatic: They pass through cold and heat to refine truth; how could they change appearance and betray feeling?

sentences.zh: 感昆吾之易越兮，懷暉光之速暮。

translations.literal: He felt how Kunwu was easily surpassed and brooded that radiance quickly reaches dusk.
translations.idiomatic: He felt how Kunwu was easily surpassed and brooded that radiance quickly reaches dusk.

sentences.zh: 羨一稔而三春兮，尚含英以容豫。

translations.literal: He envied one harvest through three springs, still holding blossoms in leisurely grace.
translations.idiomatic: He envied one harvest through three springs, still holding blossoms in leisurely grace.

sentences.zh: 悼曜靈之靡暇兮，限天晷之有度。

translations.literal: He mourned that the shining spirit has no leisure, bounded by the measured shadow of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned that the shining spirit has no leisure, bounded by the measured shadow of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 聆鳴蜩之號節兮，恐隕葉於凝露。

translations.literal: Hearing the cicada cry the season, he feared falling leaves beneath congealing dew.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the cicada cry the season, he feared falling leaves beneath congealing dew.

sentences.zh: 希前軌而增騖兮，眷後塵而旋顧。

translations.literal: He longed for the tracks ahead and hastened more, yet looked back with care at the dust behind.
translations.idiomatic: He longed for the tracks ahead and hastened more, yet looked back with care at the dust behind.

sentences.zh: 往者倏忽而不逮兮，來者冥昧而未著。

translations.literal: What has gone is sudden and cannot be reached; what is coming is dark and not yet manifest.
translations.idiomatic: What has gone is sudden and cannot be reached; what is coming is dark and not yet manifest.

sentences.zh: 二儀泊焉其無央兮，四節環轉而靡窮。

translations.literal: The two powers lie vast without limit; the four seasons turn in a ring without end.
translations.idiomatic: The two powers lie vast without limit; the four seasons turn in a ring without end.

sentences.zh: 星鳥逝而時反兮，夕景潛而且融。

translations.literal: The starry Bird departs and returns with the season; evening light sinks away and melts.
translations.idiomatic: The starry Bird departs and returns with the season; evening light sinks away and melts.

sentences.zh: 景三后之在天兮，歎聖哲之永終。

translations.literal: He looked up to the Three Sovereigns in Heaven and sighed that sages and philosophers end forever.
translations.idiomatic: He looked up to the Three Sovereigns in Heaven and sighed that sages and philosophers end forever.

sentences.zh: 諒道修而命微兮，孰舍盈而戢沖。

translations.literal: Indeed the Way is long and fate is slight; who can abandon fullness and restrain emptiness?
translations.idiomatic: Indeed the Way is long and fate is slight; who can abandon fullness and restrain emptiness?

sentences.zh: 握隋珠與蕙若兮，時莫悅而未遑。

translations.literal: Holding the Sui pearl and fragrant angelica, he found the age neither pleased nor ready.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the Sui pearl and fragrant angelica, he found the age neither pleased nor ready.

sentences.zh: 彼未遑其何恤兮，懼獨美之有傷。

translations.literal: If they are not ready, why grieve over it? He feared only that solitary beauty might be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: If they are not ready, why grieve over it? He feared only that solitary beauty might be harmed.

sentences.zh: 蹇委深而投奧兮，庶芬藻之不彰。

translations.literal: Halting, he cast himself into depth and mystery, hoping his fragrant pattern would not be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Halting, he cast himself into depth and mystery, hoping his fragrant pattern would not be displayed.

sentences.zh: 芳處幽而彌馨兮，寶在夜而愈光。

translations.literal: Fragrance grows sweeter in seclusion; a jewel shines more brightly in night.
translations.idiomatic: Fragrance grows sweeter in seclusion; a jewel shines more brightly in night.

sentences.zh: 逼區內之迫脅兮，思攄翼乎八荒。

translations.literal: Pressed by constraint within the realm, he thought to spread wings across the eight wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by constraint within the realm, he thought to spread wings across the eight wilds.

sentences.zh: 望雲階之崇壯兮，願輕舉而高翔。

translations.literal: Seeing the lofty grandeur of cloud stairs, he wished to rise lightly and soar high.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the lofty grandeur of cloud stairs, he wished to rise lightly and soar high.

sentences.zh: 造庖犧以問象兮，辨吉繇于姬文。

translations.literal: He went to Paoxi to ask about images, and distinguished auspicious judgments with Ji Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Paoxi to ask about images, and distinguished auspicious judgments with Ji Wen.

sentences.zh: 將遠遊于太初兮，鑒形魄之未分。

translations.literal: He would travel far into the Great Beginning, seeing form and soul before they divided.
translations.idiomatic: He would travel far into the Great Beginning, seeing form and soul before they divided.

sentences.zh: 四靈儼而為衛兮，六氣紛以成群。

translations.literal: The four numinous creatures stood solemnly as guards, and the six qi gathered in clustered confusion.
translations.idiomatic: The four numinous creatures stood solemnly as guards, and the six qi gathered in clustered confusion.

sentences.zh: 驂白獸于商風兮，禦蒼龍于景雲。

translations.literal: He yoked white beasts to the autumn wind and drove blue dragons through bright clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He yoked white beasts to the autumn wind and drove blue dragons through bright clouds.

sentences.zh: 簡廝徒於靈圉兮，從馮夷而問津。

translations.literal: He selected servants from the numinous stables and followed Feng Yi to ask for the ford.
translations.idiomatic: He selected servants from the numinous stables and followed Feng Yi to ask for the ford.

sentences.zh: 召陵陽于遊溪兮，旌王子于柏人。

translations.literal: He summoned Lingyang at Wandering Stream and signaled the prince at Bairen.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Lingyang at Wandering Stream and signaled the prince at Bairen.

sentences.zh: 前祝融以掌燧兮，殿玄冥以掩塵。

translations.literal: Zhurong went before to hold the fire-drill, and Xuanming guarded the rear to cover the dust.
translations.idiomatic: Zhurong went before to hold the fire-drill, and Xuanming guarded the rear to cover the dust.

sentences.zh: 形飄飄而遂遐兮，氣亹癖而愈新。

translations.literal: His form drifted and went far; his qi moved on and grew ever new.
translations.idiomatic: His form drifted and went far; his qi moved on and grew ever new.

sentences.zh: 挹玉膏於萊嵎兮，掇紫英於瀛濱。

translations.literal: He scooped jade essence at Laiyu and plucked purple blossoms on the shore of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He scooped jade essence at Laiyu and plucked purple blossoms on the shore of Ying.

sentences.zh: 揖太昊以假憩兮，聽賦政於三春。

translations.literal: He bowed to Taihao and briefly rested, listening as government was assigned to the three springs.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed to Taihao and briefly rested, listening as government was assigned to the three springs.

sentences.zh: 洪范翕而復張兮，百卉隕而更震。

translations.literal: The Great Plan closed and opened again; the hundred plants fell and trembled anew.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan closed and opened again; the hundred plants fell and trembled anew.

sentences.zh: 睇玉女之紛彯兮，執懿筐於扶木。

translations.literal: He gazed at jade maidens fluttering thickly, holding fine baskets by the Fusang tree.
translations.idiomatic: He gazed at jade maidens fluttering thickly, holding fine baskets by the Fusang tree.

sentences.zh: 覽玄象之韡曄兮，仍騰躍乎陽穀。

translations.literal: He viewed the dark images in brilliant splendor and then leapt upward in Yanggu.
translations.idiomatic: He viewed the dark images in brilliant splendor and then leapt upward in Yanggu.

sentences.zh: 吸朝霞以療饑兮，降廩泉而濯足。

translations.literal: He sucked morning rosy clouds to cure hunger and descended to Lin Spring to wash his feet.
translations.idiomatic: He sucked morning rosy clouds to cure hunger and descended to Lin Spring to wash his feet.

sentences.zh: 將縱轡以逍遙兮，恨東極之路促。

translations.literal: He was about to loosen the reins and roam free, but regretted that the eastern limit's road was short.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to loosen the reins and roam free, but regretted that the eastern limit's road was short.

sentences.zh: 詔纖阿而右回兮，覿硃明之赫戲。

translations.literal: He ordered Xian'e to turn right and saw Zhuming blazing bright.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xian'e to turn right and saw Zhuming blazing bright.

sentences.zh: 蒞群神于夏庭兮，回蒼梧而結知。

translations.literal: He visited the assembled spirits in the summer court, turned to Cangwu, and formed acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: He visited the assembled spirits in the summer court, turned to Cangwu, and formed acquaintance.

sentences.zh: 纚焦明以承旂兮，駔天馬而高馳。

translations.literal: He lined up Jiaoming birds to hold the banners and drove heavenly horses galloping high.
translations.idiomatic: He lined up Jiaoming birds to hold the banners and drove heavenly horses galloping high.

sentences.zh: 讒羲和於丹丘兮，誚倒景之亂儀。

translations.literal: He complained of Xi and He at Red Hill and reproached the inverted shadow for confusing the rites.
translations.idiomatic: He complained of Xi and He at Red Hill and reproached the inverted shadow for confusing the rites.

sentences.zh: 尋凱風而南暨兮，謝太陽於炎離。

translations.literal: Following the warm south wind, he reached the south and took leave of the sun at fiery Li.
translations.idiomatic: Following the warm south wind, he reached the south and took leave of the sun at fiery Li.

sentences.zh: 戚溽暑之陶郁兮，余安能乎留斯！

translations.literal: Grieved by the steaming heat and oppressive damp, he asked, how could I remain here?
translations.idiomatic: Grieved by the steaming heat and oppressive damp, he asked, how could I remain here?

sentences.zh: 聞碧雞之長晨兮，吾將往乎西遊。

translations.literal: Hearing of the long dawn at Blue Rooster, I will go westward in travel.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the long dawn at Blue Rooster, I will go westward in travel.

sentences.zh: 奧浮鷁于弱水兮，泊舳艫兮中流。

translations.literal: He floated ornate boats on the Weak Water and moored prow and stern in the midstream.
translations.idiomatic: He floated ornate boats on the Weak Water and moored prow and stern in the midstream.

sentences.zh: 苟精粹之攸存兮，誠沈羽以泛舟。

translations.literal: If pure essence is where one remains, then even sinking feathers can float a boat.
translations.idiomatic: If pure essence is where one remains, then even sinking feathers can float a boat.

sentences.zh: 軼望舒以陵厲兮，羌神漂而氣浮。

translations.literal: He overtook Wangshu and rose fiercely; his spirit drifted and his qi floated.
translations.idiomatic: He overtook Wangshu and rose fiercely; his spirit drifted and his qi floated.

sentences.zh: 訊碩老于金室兮，采舊聞于前修。

translations.literal: He questioned the great elders in the golden chamber and gathered old learning from former cultivators.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned the great elders in the golden chamber and gathered old learning from former cultivators.

sentences.zh: 譏淪陰于危山兮，問王母於椒丘。

translations.literal: He criticized the sunken yin at Perilous Mountain and asked the Queen Mother at Pepper Hill.
translations.idiomatic: He criticized the sunken yin at Perilous Mountain and asked the Queen Mother at Pepper Hill.

sentences.zh: 觀玄烏之參趾兮，會根壹之神籌。

translations.literal: He observed the three-toed dark bird and joined Genyi's numinous tallies.
translations.idiomatic: He observed the three-toed dark bird and joined Genyi's numinous tallies.

sentences.zh: 擾毚兔於月窟兮，詰姮娥於蓐收。

translations.literal: He stirred the crafty hare in the moon cave and questioned Chang'e at Rushou.
translations.idiomatic: He stirred the crafty hare in the moon cave and questioned Chang'e at Rushou.

sentences.zh: 爰攬轡而旋驅兮，訪北叟之倚伏。

translations.literal: Then he gathered the reins and wheeled the carriage, visiting the northern elder about reversal and fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Then he gathered the reins and wheeled the carriage, visiting the northern elder about reversal and fortune.

sentences.zh: 乘增冰而遂濟兮，淩固陰之所滀。

translations.literal: He rode layered ice and crossed, climbing over what hardened yin had stored up.
translations.idiomatic: He rode layered ice and crossed, climbing over what hardened yin had stored up.

sentences.zh: 探龜蛇於幽穴兮，瞰罔養之潛育。

translations.literal: He sought turtle and snake in dark caves and looked down on hidden nourishment secretly growing.
translations.idiomatic: He sought turtle and snake in dark caves and looked down on hidden nourishment secretly growing.

sentences.zh: 哂倏忽之躁狂兮，喪中黃於耳目，偭燭龍而遊衍兮，窮大明于北陸。

translations.literal: He laughed at the frenzy of Shu and Hu, who lost central yellow through ears and eyes; turning from Zhulong, he wandered on and exhausted the great brightness in the northern land.
translations.idiomatic: He laughed at the frenzy of Shu and Hu, who lost central yellow through ears and eyes; turning from Zhulong, he wandered on and exhausted the great brightness in the northern land.

sentences.zh: 攀招搖而上躋兮，忽蹈廓而淩虛。

translations.literal: He climbed Zhaoyao and ascended, suddenly treading vastness and mounting the void.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed Zhaoyao and ascended, suddenly treading vastness and mounting the void.

sentences.zh: 登閶闔而遺眷兮，頫玄黃於地輿。

translations.literal: He climbed the Gate of Heaven and left longing behind, looking down on black and yellow in the carriage of earth.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the Gate of Heaven and left longing behind, looking down on black and yellow in the carriage of earth.

sentences.zh: 召黔雷以先導兮，覲天帝於清都。

translations.literal: He summoned Qianlei to guide him ahead and visited the Heavenly Thearch in the Pure Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Qianlei to guide him ahead and visited the Heavenly Thearch in the Pure Capital.

sentences.zh: 觀渾儀以寓目兮，拊造化之大爐。

translations.literal: He gazed upon the armillary sphere and laid his hand on the great furnace of creation.
translations.idiomatic: He gazed upon the armillary sphere and laid his hand on the great furnace of creation.

sentences.zh: 爰辨惑於上皇兮，稽吉凶之元符。

translations.literal: There he resolved doubts before the High Sovereign and examined the primal tokens of fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: There he resolved doubts before the High Sovereign and examined the primal tokens of fortune and misfortune.

sentences.zh: 唐則天而民咨兮，癸亂常而感虞。

translations.literal: Tang modeled himself on Heaven and the people sighed; Gui disordered the constant norms and moved Yu to concern.
translations.idiomatic: Tang modeled himself on Heaven and the people sighed; Gui disordered the constant norms and moved Yu to concern.

sentences.zh: 孔揮涕於西狩兮，臧考祥于婁句。

translations.literal: Confucius wiped tears at the western hunt, and Zang examined omens at Louju.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius wiped tears at the western hunt, and Zang examined omens at Louju.

sentences.zh: 蹠肆暴而保乂兮，顏履仁而夙徂。

translations.literal: Zhi indulged violence and yet preserved himself; Yan practiced humanity and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi indulged violence and yet preserved himself; Yan practiced humanity and died early.

sentences.zh: 何否泰之靡所兮，眩榮辱之不圖？

translations.literal: Why do obstruction and peace have no fixed place, and why are glory and disgrace dazzling beyond prediction?
translations.idiomatic: Why do obstruction and peace have no fixed place, and why are glory and disgrace dazzling beyond prediction?

sentences.zh: 運可期兮不可思，道可知兮不可為。

translations.literal: Fortune can be awaited but not thought into being; the Way can be known but not forced.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune can be awaited but not thought into being; the Way can be known but not forced.

sentences.zh: 求之者勞兮欲之者惑，信天任命兮理乃自得。

translations.literal: Those who seek it labor; those who desire it are deluded. Trust Heaven and accept fate, and principle is obtained of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Those who seek it labor; those who desire it are deluded. Trust Heaven and accept fate, and principle is obtained of itself.

sentences.zh: 且也四位為匠，乾巛為均。

translations.literal: Moreover, the four positions are craftsmen, and Qian and Kun are the potter's wheel.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the four positions are craftsmen, and Qian and Kun are the potter's wheel.

sentences.zh: 散而為物，結而為人。

translations.literal: Scattered, they become things; gathered, they become humans.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered, they become things; gathered, they become humans.

sentences.zh: 陽降陰升，一替一興。

translations.literal: Yang descends and yin rises; one falls and one flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: Yang descends and yin rises; one falls and one flourishes.

sentences.zh: 流而為川，滯而為陵。

translations.literal: Flowing, it becomes rivers; stopping, it becomes hills.
translations.idiomatic: Flowing, it becomes rivers; stopping, it becomes hills.

sentences.zh: 禍不可攘，福不可征。

translations.literal: Disaster cannot be pushed away, and blessing cannot be summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster cannot be pushed away, and blessing cannot be summoned.

sentences.zh: 其否兮有豫，其泰兮有數。

translations.literal: Its obstruction has preparation; its peace has number.
translations.idiomatic: Its obstruction has preparation; its peace has number.

sentences.zh: 成形兮未察，靈像兮巳固。

translations.literal: Before formed shape can be examined, the numinous image is already fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Before formed shape can be examined, the numinous image is already fixed.

sentences.zh: 承明訓以發蒙兮，審性命之靡求。

translations.literal: Receiving bright instruction to open ignorance, he examined nature and fate and found nothing to seek.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving bright instruction to open ignorance, he examined nature and fate and found nothing to seek.

sentences.zh: 將澄神而守一兮，奚飄飄而遐遊！

translations.literal: He would clarify the spirit and guard the One; why drift about in distant wandering?
translations.idiomatic: He would clarify the spirit and guard the One; why drift about in distant wandering?

sentences.zh: 斐陳辭以告退兮，主悖惘而永歎。

translations.literal: With patterned words he declared his withdrawal; the host was bewildered and sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: With patterned words he declared his withdrawal; the host was bewildered and sighed long.

sentences.zh: 惟升降之不仍兮，詠別易而會難。

translations.literal: Thinking that rising and descending do not follow one another, he sang that parting is easy and meeting hard.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking that rising and descending do not follow one another, he sang that parting is easy and meeting hard.

sentences.zh: 願大饗以致好兮，盍息駕於一飧。

translations.literal: Wishing to offer a great feast and express goodwill, why not rest the carriage for one meal?
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to offer a great feast and express goodwill, why not rest the carriage for one meal?

sentences.zh: 會司儀于有始兮，延嘉賓于九乾。

translations.literal: He met the master of ceremony at the place of beginning and invited honored guests from the nine heavens.
translations.idiomatic: He met the master of ceremony at the place of beginning and invited honored guests from the nine heavens.

sentences.zh: 陳鈞天之廣樂兮，展萬舞之至歡。

translations.literal: He arrayed the broad music of Juntian and displayed the perfect joy of the myriad dances.
translations.idiomatic: He arrayed the broad music of Juntian and displayed the perfect joy of the myriad dances.

sentences.zh: 枉矢鑠其在手兮，狼弧翾其斯彎。

translations.literal: The bent arrow shone in his hand, and the Wolf Bow fluttered as it was drawn.
translations.idiomatic: The bent arrow shone in his hand, and the Wolf Bow fluttered as it was drawn.

sentences.zh: 睨翟犬於帝側兮，殪熊羆於靈軒。

translations.literal: He glanced at Di dogs by the Thearch's side and felled bears and brown bears by the numinous carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He glanced at Di dogs by the Thearch's side and felled bears and brown bears by the numinous carriage.

sentences.zh: 爾乃清道夙蹕，載輪修祖。

translations.literal: Thereupon the road was cleared and early passage barred; the wheels were loaded and the ancestral rite performed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the road was cleared and early passage barred; the wheels were loaded and the ancestral rite performed.

sentences.zh: 班命授號，轙輈整旅。

translations.literal: Commands were distributed and titles granted; yoke and pole were set and the procession ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Commands were distributed and titles granted; yoke and pole were set and the procession ordered.

sentences.zh: 兆司郁以郕路兮，萬靈森而陳庭。

translations.literal: Zhaosi Yu completed the road, and ten thousand spirits stood thickly arrayed in the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaosi Yu completed the road, and ten thousand spirits stood thickly arrayed in the court.

sentences.zh: 豐隆軒其警眾兮，鉤陳帥以屬兵。

translations.literal: Fenglong raised the carriage and warned the multitude; Gouchen led and assembled the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fenglong raised the carriage and warned the multitude; Gouchen led and assembled the troops.

sentences.zh: 堪輿竦而進時兮，文昌肅以司行。

translations.literal: Kanyu rose and advanced the season; Wenchang solemnly oversaw the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Kanyu rose and advanced the season; Wenchang solemnly oversaw the journey.

sentences.zh: 抗蚩尤之修旃兮，建雄虹之采旌。

translations.literal: They raised Chiyou's long banner and set up the colored standard of the mighty rainbow.
translations.idiomatic: They raised Chiyou's long banner and set up the colored standard of the mighty rainbow.

sentences.zh: 乘雲車電鞭之扶輿委移兮，駕應龍青虯之容裔陸離。

translations.literal: He rode a cloud carriage with lightning whip, rolling and swaying, and yoked responsive dragons and blue qiulong, flowing and dazzling.
translations.idiomatic: He rode a cloud carriage with lightning whip, rolling and swaying, and yoked responsive dragons and blue qiulong, flowing and dazzling.

sentences.zh: 俯游光逸景倏爍徽霍兮，仰流旌垂旄焱攸扡纚。

translations.literal: Below, wandering light and fleeing shadows flashed and flared; above, streaming banners and hanging yak-tails blazed and trailed.
translations.idiomatic: Below, wandering light and fleeing shadows flashed and flared; above, streaming banners and hanging yak-tails blazed and trailed.

sentences.zh: 前湛湛而攝進兮，後僸而方馳。

translations.literal: Ahead was deep and gleaming as they advanced in order; behind was hushed as they were just galloping.
translations.idiomatic: Ahead was deep and gleaming as they advanced in order; behind was hushed as they were just galloping.

sentences.zh: 且啟行于重陽兮，奄稅駕乎少儀。

translations.literal: They set out at Double Yang and suddenly halted the team at Shaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: They set out at Double Yang and suddenly halted the team at Shaoyi.

sentences.zh: 跨列缺兮規乾巛，揮玉關兮出天門。

translations.literal: He crossed Lieque and measured Qian and Kun, waved at the jade pass, and went out through Heaven's gate.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Lieque and measured Qian and Kun, waved at the jade pass, and went out through Heaven's gate.

sentences.zh: 涉漢津兮望昆侖，經赤霄兮臨玄根。

translations.literal: He crossed the ford of the Milky Way and gazed toward Kunlun, passed through red clouds and approached the dark root.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the ford of the Milky Way and gazed toward Kunlun, passed through red clouds and approached the dark root.

sentences.zh: 觀品物兮終復魂，形已消兮氣猶存。

translations.literal: He watched all things finally return their souls; form had vanished, but qi still remained.
translations.idiomatic: He watched all things finally return their souls; form had vanished, but qi still remained.

sentences.zh: 眺懸舟之離離兮，懷舊都之藹藹。

translations.literal: He looked toward the hanging boats, bright and arrayed, and cherished the old capital, dense and distant.
translations.idiomatic: He looked toward the hanging boats, bright and arrayed, and cherished the old capital, dense and distant.

sentences.zh: 仍繁榮而督引兮，將遄降而速邁。

translations.literal: Following luxuriant splendor, he urged the guides on, about to descend swiftly and hasten away.
translations.idiomatic: Following luxuriant splendor, he urged the guides on, about to descend swiftly and hasten away.

sentences.zh: 華雲依霏而翼衡兮，日月炫晃而映蓋。

translations.literal: Flowered clouds clustered and drifted, winging the crossbar; sun and moon dazzled and reflected on the canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Flowered clouds clustered and drifted, winging the crossbar; sun and moon dazzled and reflected on the canopy.

sentences.zh: 蹈煙煴兮辭天衢，心闣𦐇兮識故居。

translations.literal: He trod smoky vapor and left Heaven's thoroughfare; his heart opened wide and recognized the old dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: He trod smoky vapor and left Heaven's thoroughfare; his heart opened wide and recognized the old dwelling.

sentences.zh: 路遂遒兮情欣欣，奄忽歸兮反常閭。

translations.literal: The road then grew firm and his feelings joyful; suddenly he returned to his ordinary gate.
translations.idiomatic: The road then grew firm and his feelings joyful; suddenly he returned to his ordinary gate.

sentences.zh: 修中和兮崇彝倫，大道繇兮味琴書。

translations.literal: He cultivated central harmony and honored constant relations; following the Great Way, he savored zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated central harmony and honored constant relations; following the Great Way, he savored zither and books.

sentences.zh: 樂自然兮識窮達，澹無思兮心恆娛。

translations.literal: He delighted in naturalness and understood poverty and success; calm and without striving thought, his heart was always at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in naturalness and understood poverty and success; calm and without striving thought, his heart was always at ease.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良，與夏侯湛等十七人策為下第，拜中郎。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Worthy and Good; together with Xiahou Zhan and seventeen others, his policy answer was graded in the lower class, and he was appointed gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as Worthy and Good; together with Xiahou Zhan and seventeen others, his policy answer was graded in the lower class, and he was appointed gentleman.

sentences.zh: 武帝詔曰：「省諸賢良答策，雖所言殊塗，皆明于王義，有益政道。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu issued an edict: "I have examined the policy answers of the Worthy and Good men. Although what they said followed different paths, all were clear about royal principle and beneficial to governance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu issued an edict: "I have examined the policy answers of the Worthy and Good men. Although what they said followed different paths, all were clear about royal principle and beneficial to governance.

sentences.zh: 欲詳覽其對，究觀賢士大夫用心。」

translations.literal: I wish to study their answers in detail and fully observe the intentions of these worthy scholar-officials."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to study their answers in detail and fully observe the intentions of these worthy scholar-officials."

sentences.zh: 因詔諸賢良方正直言，會東堂策問，曰：「頃日食正陽，水旱為災，將何所修，以變大眚？

translations.literal: He then ordered the Worthy and Good, Upright and Straight-speaking candidates to assemble in the Eastern Hall for policy questions, saying: "Recently the sun was eclipsed at zhengyang, and floods and droughts have brought disaster. What should be cultivated to transform this great calamity?
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Worthy and Good, Upright and Straight-speaking candidates to assemble in the Eastern Hall for policy questions, saying: "Recently the sun was eclipsed at zhengyang, and floods and droughts have brought disaster. What should be cultivated to transform this great calamity?

sentences.zh: 及法令有不宜於今，為公私所患苦者，皆何事？

translations.literal: As for statutes and ordinances unsuited to the present age that cause distress to both public and private interests—what are all these matters?
translations.idiomatic: Which laws today harm both state and subject alike?

sentences.zh: 凡平世在於得才，得才者亦借耳目以聽察。

translations.literal: In general, peace in an age lies in obtaining talent; those who obtain talent likewise borrow ears and eyes to listen and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Stable rule rests on finding the right men, and rulers must keep eyes and ears open.

sentences.zh: 若有文武器能有益於時務而未見申敘者，各舉其人。

translations.literal: If there are civil and martial talents that could aid current affairs yet have not been recommended and documented, each shall nominate such persons.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who knows officials whose skills could serve the realm must put their names forward.

sentences.zh: 及有負俗謗議，宜先洗濯者，亦各言之。」

translations.literal: As for anyone burdened by public slander who ought first to be cleansed, each of you should also speak of him."
translations.idiomatic: As for anyone burdened by public slander who ought first to be cleansed, each of you should also speak of him."

sentences.zh: 虞對曰：「臣聞古之聖明，原始以要終，體本以正末。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu answered: "I have heard that the sages of antiquity traced beginnings in order to grasp endings and embodied the root in order to correct the branches.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu answered: "I have heard that the sages of antiquity traced beginnings in order to grasp endings and embodied the root in order to correct the branches.

sentences.zh: 故憂法度之不當，而不憂人物之失所；

translations.literal: Therefore they worried that laws and standards were inappropriate, not that men and affairs lost their stations;
translations.idiomatic: They worried first about bad law, not misplaced personnel;

sentences.zh: 憂人物之失所，而不憂災害之流行。

translations.literal: they worried that men and affairs lost their stations, not that disasters spread abroad.
translations.idiomatic: then about mismatched appointments, not random natural catastrophes.

sentences.zh: 誠以法得於此，則物理於彼；

translations.literal: Truly because when law obtains here, natural principle is ordered there;
translations.idiomatic: When statutes align below, heaven's pattern rights itself above;

sentences.zh: 人和於下，則災消於上。

translations.literal: harmony among those below, then calamities dissolve above.
translations.idiomatic: harmony in the realm dissolves omens in the sky.

sentences.zh: 其有日月之眚，水旱之災，則反聽內視，求其所由，遠觀諸物，近驗諸身。

translations.literal: If there are blemishes of sun and moon, disasters of flood and drought, then turn listening inward and seek their causes; gaze far at myriad things, examine near upon one's person.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven sends eclipse or flood, a ruler searches policy and conscience alike.

sentences.zh: 耳目聽察，豈或有蔽其聰明者乎？

translations.literal: In listening with ears and inspecting with eyes—could anything obstruct clarity and brightness?
translations.idiomatic: Has anything dulled your ears or eyes?

sentences.zh: 動心出令，豈或有傾其常正者乎？

translations.literal: In stirring the mind and issuing orders—could anything overturn constant correctness?
translations.idiomatic: Have decrees strayed from steady principle?

sentences.zh: 大官大職，豈或有授非其人者乎？

translations.literal: In great offices and great posts—could anyone have been appointed who was not the right person?
translations.idiomatic: Have high posts gone to unworthy men?

sentences.zh: 賞罰黜陟，豈或有不得其所者乎？

translations.literal: In rewards, punishments, demotions, and promotions—could anyone have failed to obtain what was fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Have rewards and punishments missed their mark?

sentences.zh: 河濱山岩，豈或有懷道釣築而未感於夢兆者乎？

translations.literal: Along rivers and mountain cliffs—could anyone embracing the Way, fishing or building, have failed to stir dream-portents?
translations.idiomatic: Have recluses whose virtue should move heaven gone unnoticed?

sentences.zh: 方外遐裔，豈或有命世傑出而未蒙膏澤者乎？

translations.literal: Beyond the borders in distant corners—could anyone outstanding for the age have failed to receive enriching moisture?
translations.idiomatic: Have frontier talents lacked your nurturing rain?

sentences.zh: 推此類也，以求其故，詢事考言，以盡其實，則天人之情可得而見，咎征之至可得而救也。

translations.literal: Extend reasoning of this kind to seek its causes; inquire into affairs and examine words to exhaust substance—then dispositions of Heaven and men may be observed and arrivals of blameful omens may be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: Ask such questions honestly and heaven's intent becomes legible; omens can then be answered with reform.

sentences.zh: 若推之於物則無忤，求之於身則無尤，萬物理順，內外咸宜，祝史正辭，言不負誠，而日月錯行，夭癘不戒，此則陰陽之事，非吉凶所在也。

translations.literal: If this is extended to things, there is no violation; if it is sought in oneself, there is no fault. The principles of the myriad things are orderly, inner and outer are both appropriate, the invocators and scribes correct their words, and speech does not betray sincerity. Yet if the sun and moon move awry and untimely pestilence gives no warning, then this belongs to the affairs of yin and yang and is not where good or bad fortune lies.
translations.idiomatic: If this is extended to things, there is no violation; if it is sought in oneself, there is no fault. The principles of the myriad things are orderly, inner and outer are both appropriate, the invocators and scribes correct their words, and speech does not betray sincerity. Yet if the sun and moon move awry and untimely pestilence gives no warning, then this belongs to the affairs of yin and yang and is not where good or bad fortune lies.

sentences.zh: 期運度數，自然之分，固非人事所能供禦，其亦振廩散滯，貶食省用而已矣。

translations.literal: Expected cycles and reckonings of fate are natural allotments—fundamentally not what human affairs can supply or control; one may only open granaries to relieve blockage, reduce food, and curtail expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Calendar fate lies beyond men; all we can do is open granaries, tighten belts, and ease suffering.

sentences.zh: 是故誠遇期運，則雖陶唐、殷湯有所不變；

translations.literal: Therefore if one truly meets the destined period, even Tao Tang and Yin Tang could not change it;
translations.idiomatic: When heaven fixes a season of doom, even Yao and Tang could not shift it;

sentences.zh: 苟非期運，則宋、衛之君，諸侯之相，猶能有感。

translations.literal: if it is not the destined period, then even lords of Song and Wei and ministers among the feudal lords could still produce resonant effects.
translations.idiomatic: yet outside such doom minor sovereigns could still move heaven by virtue.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下審其所由，以盡其理，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty examine the grounds thereof and exhaust their principles—then the realm will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Probe causes this thoroughly and the empire profits.

sentences.zh: 臣生長蓽門，不逮異物，雖有賢才，所未接識，不敢瞽言妄舉，無以疇答聖問。」

translations.literal: I was born and raised behind a brushwood gate and have not encountered extraordinary men. Though worthy talents surely exist, I have not met or known them, and I dare not speak blindly or nominate rashly; I have no means to answer Your sagely question."
translations.idiomatic: I was born and raised behind a brushwood gate and have not encountered extraordinary men. Though worthy talents surely exist, I have not met or known them, and I dare not speak blindly or nominate rashly; I have no means to answer Your sagely question."

sentences.zh: 擢為太子舍人，除聞喜令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Household Gentleman of the Heir Apparent and appointed magistrate of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to crown prince's gentleman and magistrate of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 時天子留心政道，又吳寇新平，天下乂安，上《太康頌》以美晉德。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven devoted mind to government ways; moreover the Wu foe had newly been pacified and the realm was peaceful—he presented "The Taikang Ode" to praise Jin virtue.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor focused on good rule and Wu had just surrendered, he offered his Taikang ode praising the Jin.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its text says:
translations.idiomatic: The ode begins:

sentences.zh: :於休上古，人之資始。

translations.literal: How splendid was high antiquity—the beginning that endowed mankind.
translations.idiomatic: Glory to deepest antiquity—source of every blessing.

sentences.zh: 四隩咸宅，萬國同軌。

translations.literal: The four marches all dwell; myriad states share one track.
translations.idiomatic: All quarters settled; every kingdom rode one axle-track.

sentences.zh: 有漢不競，喪亂靡紀。

translations.literal: Han lost its competitiveness; turmoil lost all norm.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han faltered; chaos erased every statute.

sentences.zh: 畿服外叛，侯衛內圮。

translations.literal: The royal domain rebelled without; guards collapsed within.
translations.idiomatic: Heartlands rose in revolt; palace guards crumbled within.

sentences.zh: 天難既降，時惟鞠凶。

translations.literal: Heaven's hardship having descended, the hours knew only crushing evil.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's scourge arrived; the age reeked of cruelty.

sentences.zh: 龍戰獸爭，分裂遐邦。

translations.literal: Dragons battled and beasts strove; distant regions split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Warlords tore the provinces like beasts at war.

sentences.zh: 備僭岷蜀，度逆海東。

translations.literal: Bei presumptuously seized Min and Shu; Du crossed to the eastern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei seized Shu beyond Min; enemies sailed the eastern sea.

sentences.zh: 權乃緣間，割據三江。

translations.literal: Sun Quan then exploited the breach and carved out the three rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan exploited the breach and held the Yangzi triple fork.

sentences.zh: 明明上帝，臨下有赫。

translations.literal: Bright August Heaven above looks down with awesome power.
translations.idiomatic: August Heaven glares from above.

sentences.zh: 乃宣皇威，致天之辟。

translations.literal: Then the martial sovereign spread awe and executed Heaven's punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Our martial emperor wielded awe and heaven's sentence.

sentences.zh: 奮武遼隧，罪人斯獲。

translations.literal: His might was roused at Liaosui; the guilty were captured.
translations.idiomatic: His hosts thundered along Liaosui and seized the guilty.

sentences.zh: 撫定朝鮮，奄征韓、貊。

translations.literal: He pacified Joseon and campaigned to Han and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: He settled Korea and marched against Han and Mo.

sentences.zh: 文既應期，席捲梁、益。

translations.literal: When culture answered the hour, he swept Liang and Yi like rolling up a mat.
translations.idiomatic: When civil virtue matched the hour, Liang and Yi rolled up like mats.

sentences.zh: 元憝委命，九夷重譯。

translations.literal: The chief villain surrendered his fate; the nine Yi arrived through successive interpreters.
translations.idiomatic: The arch rebel yielded his mandate; nine Yi peoples reached court through relay interpreters.

sentences.zh: 邛、冉、哀牢，是焉底績。

translations.literal: Qiong, Ran, and Ailao—there he laid his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Southwestern Qiong, Ran, and Ailao bowed to his achievement.

sentences.zh: 我皇之登，二國既平。

translations.literal: When Our Emperor ascended, those two states were already pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When our emperor mounted the throne, both rival realms had fallen.

sentences.zh: 靡適不懷，以育群生。

translations.literal: None who stayed away failed to cherish him; he nurtured the masses.
translations.idiomatic: None beyond reach refused him; he fed every life.

sentences.zh: 吳乃負固，放命南冥。

translations.literal: Wu then relied on terrain and defied command in the southern deep.
translations.idiomatic: Wu still hugged its rivers and flouted edicts in the southern dark.

sentences.zh: 聲教未暨，弗及王靈。

translations.literal: Sound and instruction had not reached them; kingly numinous power did not extend.
translations.idiomatic: Civilizing teaching had not touched them; royal majesty stalled.

sentences.zh: 皇震其威，赫如雷霆。

translations.literal: The sovereign shook his might—awe like thunderclap.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's wrath crashed like thunder.

sentences.zh: 截彼江、沔，荊、舒以清。

translations.literal: He cut through Jiang and Han; Jing and Shu were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: He severed Jiang and Han until Jing and Shu ran clear.

sentences.zh: 邈矣聖皇，參乾兩離。

translations.literal: Far-flung is the sage sovereign—paired with Qian, twin Li.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty the sage king—spanning heaven's pivot like paired trigrams.

sentences.zh: 陶化以正，取亂以奇。

translations.literal: He molded transformation with rectitude; seized chaos with surprise.
translations.idiomatic: He shaped order through candor and seized chaos by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 耀武六旬，輿徒不疲。

translations.literal: For sixty days he displayed arms—yet carriers never tired.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty days of campaigning wearied neither wagons nor men.

sentences.zh: 飲至數實，幹旄無虧。

translations.literal: They drank at return and counted rewards—royal banners unfurled without flaw.
translations.idiomatic: Victory wine flowed; banners flew spotless.

sentences.zh: 洋洋四海，率禮和樂。

translations.literal: Vast is the four seas—all observe rites and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Across four seas all tread ritual and song.

sentences.zh: 穆穆宮廟，歌雍詠鑠。

translations.literal: Solemn the palace shrines—they sing Yong and chant splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Temples echo with hymns of praise.

sentences.zh: 光天之下，莫匪帝略。

translations.literal: Beneath heaven's effulgence none escape the emperor's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Under radiant heaven none escape his design.

sentences.zh: 窮發反景，承正受朔。

translations.literal: Even farthest barbarians and sunset realms receive orthodox calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Even distant tribes facing polar gloom accept his calendar.

sentences.zh: 龍馬騤騤，風于華陽。

translations.literal: Dragon-horses prance; winds breathe at Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-steeds stamp; winds sigh along Huayang.

sentences.zh: 弓矢橐服，干戈戢藏。

translations.literal: Bows and arrows in quiver-sleeves; shields and spears stored away.
translations.idiomatic: Bows rest in cases; shields and spears gather dust.

sentences.zh: 嚴嚴南金，業業餘皇。

translations.literal: Stern southern metal—towering war-galleys.
translations.idiomatic: Southern bells ring from towering fleets.

sentences.zh: 雄劍班朝，造舟為梁。

translations.literal: Hero blades ranked at court; built boats bridge the stream.
translations.idiomatic: Keen swords line the hall; pontoon bridges span the waves.

sentences.zh: 聖明有造，實代天工。

translations.literal: The sage's brilliance creates—truly replacing Heaven's craft.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's creation rivals heaven's workmanship.

sentences.zh: 天地不違，黎元時邕。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth do not oppose him; the black-haired folk prosper in season.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth assent; commoners thrive in step.

sentences.zh: 三務斯協，用底厥庸。

translations.literal: The three tasks harmonize—thus his merit is brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: The three prime duties align; his merit closes perfect.

sentences.zh: 既遠其跡，將明其蹤。

translations.literal: Already remote his traces—soon plain his tracks.
translations.idiomatic: His footprints fade yet blaze plain on stone.

sentences.zh: 喬山惟嶽，望帝之封。

translations.literal: Lofty Mount Qiao—Emperor Shun's fief mound.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Qiao towers—mark of Emperor Shun's mound.

sentences.zh: 猗歟聖帝，胡不封哉！

translations.literal: Oh sage emperor—why was he not enfeoffed!
translations.idiomatic: O sage liege—why withhold your mound!

sentences.zh: 以母憂解職。

translations.literal: He resigned office mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 久之，召補尚書郎。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was summoned to supplement as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Much later he returned as a secretary at the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 將作大匠陳勰掘地得古尺，尚書奏：「今尺長於古尺，宜以古為正。」

translations.literal: When Chief Architect Chen Xie dug in the earth and obtained an ancient foot-rule, the Secretariat memorialized: "The present chi is longer than the ancient chi; the ancient one should be taken as correct."
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Architect Chen Xie dug in the earth and obtained an ancient foot-rule, the Secretariat memorialized: "The present chi is longer than the ancient chi; the ancient one should be taken as correct."

sentences.zh: 潘嶽以為慣用已久，不宜復改。

translations.literal: Pan Yue held that habit had long used the present measure and it was unsuitable to change again.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue protested that generations had used the longer chi.

sentences.zh: 虞駁曰：「昔聖人有以見天下之賾而擬其形容，象物制器，以存時用。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu refuted this: "In the past, when the sages saw the profundities of the realm, they modeled their forms and appearances and fashioned implements after things in order to preserve timely use.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu refuted this: "In the past, when the sages saw the profundities of the realm, they modeled their forms and appearances and fashioned implements after things in order to preserve timely use.

sentences.zh: 故參天兩地，以正算數之紀；

translations.literal: Therefore they matched heaven triply and earth doubly to rectify reckoning of calculations;
translations.idiomatic: They paired heaven's three lights with earth's two forces to anchor mathematics;

sentences.zh: 依律計分，以定長短之度。

translations.literal: they relied on pitch pipes to compute fractions to settle measures of length.
translations.idiomatic: they tied length to pitch-pipe fractions.

sentences.zh: 其作之也有則，故用之也有征。

translations.literal: Their making had patterns; therefore their application had verification.
translations.idiomatic: Design followed rule, so use matched proof.

sentences.zh: 考步兩儀，則天地無所隱其情；

translations.literal: Examining the two luminaries in step—Heaven and Earth cannot hide disposition;
translations.idiomatic: Align sun and moon and heaven hides nothing;

sentences.zh: 准正三辰，則懸象無所容其謬；

translations.literal: aligning and correcting the three celestial markers—suspended phenomena cannot harbor error;
translations.idiomatic: true the three celestial markers and stars cannot lie;

sentences.zh: 施之金石，則音韻和諧；

translations.literal: applied to metal and stone—tones and resonance harmonize;
translations.idiomatic: strike bells and stones and pitch locks;

sentences.zh: 措之規矩，則器用合宜。

translations.literal: laid on compass and square—vessels and tools fit use.
translations.idiomatic: lay compass and square and every vessel fits.

sentences.zh: 一本不差而萬物皆正，及其差也，事皆反是。

translations.literal: One root without discrepancy and myriad things are correct; when discrepancy arises, affairs reverse this.
translations.idiomatic: One true gauge orders all; error inverts everything.

sentences.zh: 今尺長於古尺幾於半寸，樂府用之，律呂不合；

translations.literal: Now the present rule exceeds the ancient by nearly half an inch; when the Music Bureau uses it, pitch pipes do not match;
translations.idiomatic: Today's chi overshoots the old by half an inch—music falls out of tune;

sentences.zh: 史官用之，曆象失占；

translations.literal: when clerks of history use it, celestial patterns lose prognostications;
translations.idiomatic: historians lose celestial forecasts;

sentences.zh: 醫署用之，孔穴乖錯。

translations.literal: when the medical office uses it, acupuncture points go awry.
translations.idiomatic: physicians miss every point.

sentences.zh: 此三者，度量之所由生，得失之所取征，皆絓閡而不得通，故宜改今而從古也。

translations.literal: These three are what measures stem from and where gain and loss take verification—all are tangled and obstructed and cannot communicate—therefore it is fitting to change the present and follow the ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Music, calendar, and medicine all ride on measure—each now jams—so we must revert to the ancient chi.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞之制，同律度量衡，仲尼之訓，謹權審度。

translations.literal: Institutions of Tang and Yu unified pitch pipes, measures, weights, and balances; Confucius's teaching was careful with weights and examined measures.
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun unified pitch, length, volume, and weight; Confucius urged careful scales.

sentences.zh: 今兩尺並用，不可謂之同；

translations.literal: Now two rules are used together—it cannot be called unified;
translations.idiomatic: Two rulers at once cannot mean unity;

sentences.zh: 知失而行，不可謂之謹。

translations.literal: knowing the error yet proceeding—it cannot be called careful.
translations.idiomatic: knowing error yet marching on is not caution;

sentences.zh: 不同不謹，是謂謬法，非所以軌物垂則，示人之極。

translations.literal: Neither unified nor careful—this is called mistaken law; it is not how to regulate things, hand down norms, or show people utmost standards.
translations.idiomatic: Neither unified nor careful is false law—no model for the realm.

sentences.zh: 凡物有多而易改，亦有少而難變，亦有改而致煩，有變而之簡。

translations.literal: Among things some are many and easy to alter, some few and hard to change; some alterations bring trouble, some changes lead to simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Some reforms stir trouble; others simplify.

sentences.zh: 度量是人所常用，而長短非人所戀惜，是多而易改者也。

translations.literal: Measures are what people constantly use, yet lengths are not what people cling to—these are many and easy to alter.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone uses yardsticks daily yet hardly fetishizes a chi—easy to fix.

sentences.zh: 正失於得，反邪于正，一時之變，永世無二，是變而之簡者也。

translations.literal: Correcting loss into gain, returning deviation to rectitude—a single generation's change, none different for ages—is change tending toward simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Righting wrong measures once sets generations straight—that is simple reform.

sentences.zh: 憲章成式，不失舊物，季末苟合之制，異端雜亂之用，當以時厘改，貞夫一者也。

translations.literal: Statutes following established patterns without losing old objects—expedient compromises of late decadence and miscellaneous usages from heterodox schools ought to be rectified in due course toward unity.
translations.idiomatic: Guard true precedent; sweep away Late Han shortcuts and odd usages until only one measure remains.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜如所奏。」

translations.literal: Your servant believes it is proper to follow the memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes it is proper to follow the memorial."

sentences.zh: 又表論封禪，見《禮志》。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on feng and shan sacrifices—see the "Treatise on Rites."
translations.idiomatic: His essay on the Feng and Shan rites appears in the Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 虞以漢末喪亂，譜傳多亡失，雖其子孫不能言其先祖，撰《族姓昭穆》十卷，上疏進之，以為足以備物致用，廣多聞之益。

translations.literal: Because in the disorder at the end of Han many genealogies and transmissions had been lost, so that even descendants could not speak of their ancestors, Zhi Yu compiled ten fascicles of Zuxing Zhaomu, "Clan Surnames and Generational Order," and submitted them with a memorial, considering them enough to prepare things for use and broaden the benefit of wide learning.
translations.idiomatic: Because in the disorder at the end of Han many genealogies and transmissions had been lost, so that even descendants could not speak of their ancestors, Zhi Yu compiled ten fascicles of Zuxing Zhaomu, "Clan Surnames and Generational Order," and submitted them with a memorial, considering them enough to prepare things for use and broaden the benefit of wide learning.

sentences.zh: 以定品違法，為司徒所劾，詔原之。

translations.literal: For violating regulations in fixing ranks he was impeached by the Minister of Education; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of education impeached him for irregular promotions; the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 時太廟初建，詔普增位一等。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Temple was first erected; an edict universally raised rank one degree.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial temple opened, an edict promoted every official one rank.

sentences.zh: 後以主者承詔失旨，改除之。

translations.literal: Later because the responsible official carried out the edict contrary to intent, the promotion was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaucrats botched the order and the bonus rank was rescinded.

sentences.zh: 虞上表曰：「臣聞昔之聖明，不愛千乘之國而惜桐葉之信，所以重至尊之命而達于萬國之誠也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu submitted a memorial: "I have heard that the ancient sages did not begrudge a state of a thousand chariots yet treasured the trust of the paulownia leaf; by this they honored the supreme command and conveyed sincerity to the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu submitted a memorial: "I have heard that the ancient sages did not begrudge a state of a thousand chariots yet treasured the trust of the paulownia leaf; by this they honored the supreme command and conveyed sincerity to the myriad states.

sentences.zh: 前《乙巳赦書》，遠稱先帝遺惠餘澤，普增位一等，以酬四海欣戴之心。

translations.literal: The former Yisi amnesty edict far praised the late emperor's lingering grace and residual moisture and universally raised rank one degree to repay hearts of the four seas who rejoiced and bore allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: The prior Yisi edict credited the late emperor's grace and raised every rank to reward loyal hearts.

sentences.zh: 驛書班下，被於遠近，莫不鳥騰魚躍，喜蒙德澤。

translations.literal: Dispatches were posted far and near—none did not leap like birds or fish, rejoicing to receive virtue's moisture.
translations.idiomatic: Courier notices raced everywhere; subjects danced like fish and birds under fresh rain.

sentences.zh: 今一旦更以主者思文不審，收既往之詔，奪已澍之施，臣之愚心竊以為不可。」

translations.literal: Now, all at once, because the responsible office considered the wording carelessly, it would withdraw a past edict and take back favors already poured forth. In my foolish heart, I privately believe this is impermissible."
translations.idiomatic: Now, all at once, because the responsible office considered the wording carelessly, it would withdraw a past edict and take back favors already poured forth. In my foolish heart, I privately believe this is impermissible."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his protest.

sentences.zh: 元康中，遷吳王友。

translations.literal: During Yuankang he was transferred to be Companion to the Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuankang he became companion to the Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 時荀顗撰《新禮》，使虞討論得失而後施行。

translations.literal: At that time Xun Yi compiled the New Rites and had Yu debate gains and losses before implementing.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi drafted new ritual statutes and had Zhi Yu vet them before promulgation.

sentences.zh: 元皇后崩，杜預奏：「諒暗之制，乃自上古，是以高宗無服喪之文，而唯文稱不言。

translations.literal: When Empress Yuan died, Du Yu memorialized: "The institution of silent mourning comes from high antiquity; therefore there is no text saying Gaozong wore mourning, and the documents only say that he did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Yuan died, Du Yu memorialized: "The institution of silent mourning comes from high antiquity; therefore there is no text saying Gaozong wore mourning, and the documents only say that he did not speak.

sentences.zh: 漢文限三十六日。

translations.literal: Han Wendi limited it to thirty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi capped mourning at thirty-six days.

sentences.zh: 魏氏以降，既虞為節。

translations.literal: From Wei onward, completion of the Yu sacrifice became the measure.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei, mourning ended after the Yu sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 皇太子與國為體，理宜釋服，卒哭便除。」

translations.literal: The crown prince shares substance with the state. By principle, he should set aside mourning garments and remove them after the final weeping."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince shares substance with the state. By principle, he should set aside mourning garments and remove them after the final weeping."

sentences.zh: 虞答預書曰：「唐稱遏密，殷雲諒暗，各舉事以為名，非既葬有殊降。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu answered Du Yu in a letter: "Tang spoke of stopping music, and Yin spoke of silent mourning. Each used an event as its name; it was not that after burial there was some separate reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu answered Du Yu in a letter: "Tang spoke of stopping music, and Yin spoke of silent mourning. Each used an event as its name; it was not that after burial there was some separate reduction.

sentences.zh: 周室以來，謂之喪服。

translations.literal: Since Zhou times it has been called mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhou people simply called these mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 喪服者，以服表喪。

translations.literal: Mourning dress means using garments to display mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress visibly signals grief.

sentences.zh: 今帝者一日萬機，太子監撫之重，以宜奪禮，葬訖除服，變制通理，垂典將來，何必附之于古，使老儒致爭哉！」

translations.literal: Now the emperor has ten thousand affairs in a single day, and the heir apparent bears the weight of oversight and care. It is proper to curtail ritual, remove mourning after burial, alter the rule to accord with principle, and hand down a precedent for the future. Why must one attach it to antiquity and make old scholars argue!"
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor has ten thousand affairs in a single day, and the heir apparent bears the weight of oversight and care. It is proper to curtail ritual, remove mourning after burial, alter the rule to accord with principle, and hand down a precedent for the future. Why must one attach it to antiquity and make old scholars argue!"

sentences.zh: 皇太孫尚薨，有司奏「御服齊衰期」。

translations.literal: When the imperial grandson Shang died, the responsible office memorialized: "The imperial mourning garments should be zicui for one year."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial grandson Shang died, the responsible office memorialized: "The imperial mourning garments should be zicui for one year."

sentences.zh: 詔令博士議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the erudites to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered academic officials to debate it.

sentences.zh: 虞曰：「太子生，舉以成人之禮，則殤理除矣。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu said: "When the heir apparent was born, he was raised according to the rites for an adult, so the principle for those who die young is removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu said: "When the heir apparent was born, he was raised according to the rites for an adult, so the principle for those who die young is removed.

sentences.zh: 太孫亦體君傳重，由位成而服全，非以年也。」

translations.literal: The imperial grandson likewise embodied the ruler and transmitted the great charge; because his position was complete, the mourning garments were complete, not because of his age."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson likewise embodied the ruler and transmitted the great charge; because his position was complete, the mourning garments were complete, not because of his age."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: They followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 虞又議玉輅、兩社事，見《輿服志》。

translations.literal: Yu also deliberated the jade chariot and the two altars of soil—see the Treatise on Carriages and Robes.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials on the jade carriage and paired soil altars appear in the Treatise on Carriages and Robes.

sentences.zh: 後曆秘書監、衛尉卿，從惠帝幸長安。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as Director of the Palace Library and Minister of the Guards, following Emperor Hui to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He later directed the imperial library and commanded the guards, accompanying Emperor Hui west to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 及東軍來迎，百官奔散，遂流離鄠、杜之間，轉入南山中，糧絕饑甚，拾橡實而食之。

translations.literal: When eastern armies came to welcome them, the hundred officials fled in disorder; he drifted destitute between Hu and Du, then turned into the southern hills—food cut off, terribly hungry, he gathered oak fruits and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: When eastern relief arrived the court scattered; he wandered between Hu and Du and fled into the Zhongnan hills, starving until he gathered acorns to eat.

sentences.zh: 後得還洛，曆光祿勳、太常卿。

translations.literal: Later he was able to return to Luoyang, serving successively as Guangluxun and Taichang Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was able to return to Luoyang, serving successively as Guangluxun and Taichang Qing.

sentences.zh: 時懷帝親郊。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Huai personally sacrificed at the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai personally performed the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 自元康以來，不親郊祀，禮儀弛廢。

translations.literal: Since Yuankang, he had not personally attended suburban sacrifice—rites grew lax and fell into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuankang no emperor had personally worshipped heaven—outer ritual had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 虞考正舊典，法物粲然。

translations.literal: Yu collated old canons—implements and regalia shone complete.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu restored the old liturgy so vessels and banners gleamed in proper array.

sentences.zh: 及洛京荒亂，盜竊縱橫，人饑相食。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell to chaos, theft ran rampant and starving people ate each other.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's collapse unleashed thieves and cannibal famine.

sentences.zh: 虞素清貧，遂以餒卒。

translations.literal: Yu had always been poor and clean—thereupon he starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Always poor and honest, he died of starvation.

sentences.zh: 虞撰《文章志》四卷，注解《三輔決錄》，又撰古文章，類聚區分為三十卷，名曰《流別集》，各為之論，辭理愜當，為世所重。

translations.literal: Yu compiled Records of Literary Works in four rolls, annotated Judgments on the Three Auxiliaries, also compiled ancient compositions classified into thirty rolls titled Collected Genres, each with commentary—phrasing and reasoning apt, esteemed by the age.
translations.idiomatic: He left a four-scroll literary gazetteer, glosses on the Sanfu judgments, and thirty fascicles of categorized ancient prose called Collected Genres with critical essays—widely admired.

sentences.zh: 虞善觀玄象，嘗謂友人曰：「今天下方亂，避難之國，其唯涼土乎！」

translations.literal: Zhi Yu was skilled at observing the dark celestial signs; he once told a friend: "The realm is about to fall into chaos. Among states for avoiding disaster, surely only the land of Liang will serve!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu was skilled at observing the dark celestial signs; he once told a friend: "The realm is about to fall into chaos. Among states for avoiding disaster, surely only the land of Liang will serve!"

sentences.zh: 性愛士人，有表薦者，恆為其辭。

translations.literal: By nature he cherished scholars; whenever someone submitted a memorial of recommendation he always drafted the wording for them.
translations.idiomatic: He loved nurturing scholars and habitually ghost-wrote recommendations.

sentences.zh: 東平太叔廣樞機清辯，廣談，虞不能對；

translations.literal: Taishu Guang of Dongping was acute and eloquent in debate; when Guang conversed at length Yu could not reply;
translations.idiomatic: Taishu Guang of Dongping sparkled in oral debate—Zhi Yu could not match him live;

sentences.zh: 虞筆，廣不能答；

translations.literal: when Yu wrote, Guang could not answer;
translations.idiomatic: when Zhi Yu wrote, Guang could not respond;

sentences.zh: 更相嗤笑，紛然於世雲。

translations.literal: They sneered at each other by turns—through the capital rumor ran confused.
translations.idiomatic: They traded barbs until Luoyang buzzed with gossip.

sentences.zh: 束晳

translations.literal: Shu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Shu Xi.

sentences.zh: 束晳，字廣微，陽平元城人，漢太子太傅疏廣之後也。

translations.literal: Shu Xi, courtesy name Guangwei, was a man of Yuancheng in Yangping—descendant of Han heir tutor Shu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi, styled Guangwei, came from Yuancheng in Yangping and descended from Shu Guang, tutor to the Han heir.

sentences.zh: 王莽末，廣曾孫孟達避難，自東海徙居沙鹿山南，因去疏之足，遂改姓焉。

translations.literal: At Wang Mang's end Guang's great-grandson Mengda fled turmoil, moved from Donghai to south of Mount Shalu, removed the foot radical from Shu and changed surname.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang fell, Guang's descendant Mengda fled east to Mount Shalu and shortened the surname Shu by dropping its foot radical.

sentences.zh: 祖混，隴西太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hun was governor of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shu Hun governed Longxi.

sentences.zh: 父龕，馮翊太守，並有名譽。

translations.literal: His father Kan was governor of Fengyi—both had fame.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu Kan governed Fengyi—both father and grandfather were renowned.

sentences.zh: 晳博學多聞，與兄璆俱知名。

translations.literal: Xi was broadly learned; he and his elder brother Qiu were both renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi read widely; he and his brother Qiu shared fame.

sentences.zh: 少游國學，或問博士曹志曰：「當今好學者誰乎？」

translations.literal: In youth he attended the Guoxue, the imperial academy. Someone asked Boshi Cao Zhi, an Erudite: "Among today's students, who loves learning?"
translations.idiomatic: In youth he attended the Guoxue, the imperial academy. Someone asked Boshi Cao Zhi, an Erudite: "Among today's students, who loves learning?"

sentences.zh: 志曰：「陽平束廣微好學不倦，人莫及也。」

translations.literal: Cao Zhi said: "Shu Guangwei of Yangping loves learning without weariness; no one can match him."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi said: "Shu Guangwei of Yangping loves learning without weariness; no one can match him."

sentences.zh: 還鄉里，察孝廉，舉茂才，皆不就。

translations.literal: Returning home he was inspected Filial and nominated Flourishing Talent—both without rising.
translations.idiomatic: Home callers nominated him Filial and Flourishing Talent—he declined both.

sentences.zh: 璆娶石鑒從女，棄之，鑒以為憾，諷州郡公府不得辟，故晳等久不得調。

translations.literal: Qiu married a niece of Shi Jian's cousin but divorced her; Jian bore resentment and hinted that commanderies and senior offices must not summon him—therefore Xi and others long went without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: His brother divorced Shi Jian's niece; Shi Jian blocked both brothers from office until grudges faded.

sentences.zh: 太康中，郡界大旱，晳為邑人請雨，三日而雨注，眾謂晳誠感，為作歌曰：「束先生，通神明，請天三日甘雨零。

translations.literal: During Taikang, there was a great drought in the commandery. Shu Xi prayed for rain on behalf of the townspeople, and after three days rain poured down. The people said Xi had moved Heaven by sincerity and made a song: "Master Shu, who understands spirits bright, asked Heaven, and after three days sweet rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: During Taikang, there was a great drought in the commandery. Shu Xi prayed for rain on behalf of the townspeople, and after three days rain poured down. The people said Xi had moved Heaven by sincerity and made a song: "Master Shu, who understands spirits bright, asked Heaven, and after three days sweet rain fell.

sentences.zh: 我黍以育，我稷以生。

translations.literal: Our millet thereby grows; our glutinous millet thereby lives.
translations.idiomatic: Our sorghum grows; our millet thrives.

sentences.zh: 何以疇之？

translations.literal: How shall we repay him?
translations.idiomatic: How shall we repay him?

sentences.zh: 報束長生。」

translations.literal: We repay Master Changsheng."
translations.idiomatic: We repay Master Changsheng."

sentences.zh: 晳與衛恆厚善，聞恆遇禍，自本郡赴喪。

translations.literal: Xi was thick as friends with Wei Heng; hearing Heng met disaster he hurried from his commandery to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: Close to Wei Heng, he raced from home to mourn Heng's murder.

sentences.zh: 嘗為《勸農》及《餅》諸賦，文頗鄙俗，時人薄之。

translations.literal: He once composed fu such as Encourage Agriculture and Cakes—the language rather vulgar; people of the time slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: His fu on farming and cakes sounded coarse—contemporaries sneered.

sentences.zh: 而性沈退，不慕榮利，作《玄居釋》以擬《客難》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: Yet his nature was retiring—he did not covet glory or profit; he composed Explanation of Dwelling in Mystery modeled on Guest's Difficulty, its text saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yet he spurned rank and fashioned his Explanation of Dwelling in Mystery after the Guest's Difficulty:

sentences.zh: 束晳閒居，門人並侍。

translations.literal: Shu Xi dwelt in leisure—disciples stood attendance together.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi lived in quiet retirement surrounded by disciples.

sentences.zh: 方下帷深譚，隱几而咍，含毫散藻，考撰同異，在側者進而問之曰：「蓋聞道尚變通，達者無窮。

translations.literal: As he lowered the curtain for deep discussion, leaned on the armrest and laughed, held his brush and scattered literary brilliance, and examined and compiled agreements and differences, those beside him came forward and asked: "We have heard that the Way values adaptation and that those who understand it are inexhaustible.
translations.idiomatic: As he lowered the curtain for deep discussion, leaned on the armrest and laughed, held his brush and scattered literary brilliance, and examined and compiled agreements and differences, those beside him came forward and asked: "We have heard that the Way values adaptation and that those who understand it are inexhaustible.

sentences.zh: 世亂則救其紛，時泰則扶其隆。

translations.literal: Age chaotic—then rescue its tangles; age tranquil—then uphold its prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Rescue chaos when the age tangles; uphold greatness when peace reigns.

sentences.zh: 振天維以贊百務，熙帝載而鼓皇風。

translations.literal: Raise heaven's net to aid the myriad tasks; brighten the emperor's record and drum royal winds.
translations.idiomatic: Hold up heaven's warp for every task; brighten the monarch's merit and fan imperial virtue abroad.

sentences.zh: 生則率土樂其存，死則宇內哀其終。

translations.literal: Living, then all within the soil rejoices in his existence; dying, then within the seas they mourn his end.
translations.idiomatic: Alive, the realm rejoices with him; dead, every shore mourns.

sentences.zh: 是以君子屈己伸道，不恥幹時。

translations.literal: Therefore gentlemen bend themselves to extend the Way, not ashamed to pursue timely employment.
translations.idiomatic: So worthies bend pride to advance the Way and seize office without shame.

sentences.zh: 上國有不索何獲之言，《周易》著躍以求進之辭。

translations.literal: The Central States have the saying "nothing sought, nothing gained"; the Changes marks leaping to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland says seek or starve; the Zhou yi praises those who leap toward duty.

sentences.zh: 莘老負金鉉以陳烹割之說，齊客當康衢而詠《白水》之詩。
