translations.literal: Old Shen shouldered bronze tripods expounding butcher-kings; the Qi traveler sang White Water on the broad avenue.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's cook preached over cauldrons; a Qi pilgrim sang White Water in the highway.

sentences.zh: 今先生耽道修藝，嶷然山峙，潛朗通微，洽覽深識，夜兼忘寐之勤，晝騁鑽玄之思，曠年累稔，不墮其志。

translations.literal: Now, sir, you steep yourself in the Way and cultivate arts—towering like a mountain, latent brilliance penetrating subtlety, browsing deeply and knowing broadly—by night forgetting sleep's toil, by day racing after arcane thought—year piled on year without abandoning your resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you bury yourself in learning like a silent peak—years of sleepless reading—never yielding.

sentences.zh: 鱗翼成而愈伏，術業優而不試。

translations.literal: Yet scales and wings fully formed you hide still deeper; arts perfected yet never tested.
translations.idiomatic: Fully fledged, you burrow deeper; mastery ripe, you refuse trial.

sentences.zh: 乃欲闔櫝辭價，泥蟠深處，永戢琳琅之耀，匿首窮魚之渚，當唐年而慕長沮，邦有道而反甯武。

translations.literal: You would shut the coffer and decline valuation, coil like mud in deep recesses, forever sheathing gleaming jade, hiding your head on islets where stranded fish dwell—when Tang reigns you envy Chang Ju; when the state has the Way you imitate Ning Wu.
translations.idiomatic: You would bury treasure like fish in drying pools—longing for Chang Ju even under Tang's golden rule.

sentences.zh: 識彼迷此，愚竊不取。

translations.literal: Seeing them lost yet holding this course—in my foolishness I dare not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring their folly wins no praise from me.

sentences.zh: 若乃士以援登，進必待求，附勢之黨橫擢，則林藪之彥不抽，丹墀步紈誇之童，東野遺白顛之叟。

translations.literal: Moreover scholars climb through patronage—advancement awaits solicitation; when factions of opportunists seize posts unchecked, forest worthies cannot emerge; silk-shod boys swagger on vermilion steps while white-haired elders linger east of town.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars rise through patrons—when climbers glut court, hermits starve while silk youths parade and gray scholars rot outside.

sentences.zh: 盍亦因數都而事博陸，憑鷁首以涉洪流，蹈翠雲以駭逸龍，振光耀以驚沈鰌。

translations.literal: Why not seize season and emulate Lu's minister, ride kingfisher prow across vast currents, tread emerald clouds to startle soaring dragons, shake radiance to alarm sunk fish?
translations.idiomatic: Better borrow Bo Lu's tide—rise on floods and startle dragons.

sentences.zh: 徒屈蟠于陷井，眄天路而不遊，學既積而身困，夫何為乎秘丘。

translations.literal: Content to coil in a pit gazing at heaven's road yet never roaming—learning piles while the body languishes—what use hiding on secret hills?
translations.idiomatic: Why lie in wells studying heaven yet waste away?

sentences.zh: 且歲不我與，時若奔駟，有來無反，難得易失。

translations.literal: Moreover years do not wait on us; seasons gallop like swift horses—what comes does not return; hard to gain, easy to lose.
translations.idiomatic: Years gallop—gain once, lose forever.

sentences.zh: 先生不知盱豫之讖悔遲，而忘夫朋盍之義務疾，亦豈能登海湄而抑東流之水，臨虞泉而招西歸之日？

translations.literal: Sir, do you not know hesitation's regret arrives late while forgetting fellowship demands haste—can you climb the ocean verge and dam the eastern flood, stand by Yu's spring and beckon the western sun?
translations.idiomatic: Hesitation invites regret; no man dams east tides or recalls western sun.

sentences.zh: 徒以曲畏為梏，儒學自桎，囚大道於環堵，苦形骸於蓬室。

translations.literal: Only take twisted fear as fetters, Confucian study as self-shackles, imprison the great Way within a mud wall, torture your frame inside a thatched room.
translations.idiomatic: Do not chain the Way to hovel dread.

sentences.zh: 豈若托身權戚，憑勢假力，擇棲芳林，飛不待翼，夕宿七娥之房，朝享五鼎之食，匡三正則太階平，贊五教而玉繩直。

translations.literal: How compare lodging with powerful kin, borrowing influence to perch in fragrant woods—soaring needs no wings—sleep nights in towers of seven beauties, dine mornings on five-tripod feasts—support the three norms then the Grand Stairway levels; aid the five teachings then the Jade Cord hangs straight?
translations.idiomatic: Compare patronage—palace nights, tripod feasts—against fasting alone?

sentences.zh: 孰若茹藿餐蔬，終身自匿哉！」

translations.literal: How compare chewing greens and eating vegetable stalks, hiding life-long?"
translations.idiomatic: Or gnaw greens forever in hiding?"

sentences.zh: 束子曰：「居！

translations.literal: Master Shu said: "Sit!
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi answered: "Sit.

sentences.zh: 吾將導爾以君子之道，諭爾以出處之事。

translations.literal: I shall guide you in the gentleman's Way and instruct you in matters of withdrawal and emergence.
translations.idiomatic: Let me teach the gentleman's path of serving or hiding.

sentences.zh: 爾其明受餘訊，謹聽餘志。

translations.literal: You must clearly receive my inquiry and heedfully listen to my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hear me out carefully.

sentences.zh: 昔元一既啟，兩儀肇立，離光夜隱，望舒晝戢，羽族翔林，蟩蛁赴濕，物從性之所安，士樂志之所執，或背豐榮以岩棲，或排蘭闥而求入，在野者龍逸，在朝者鳳集。

translations.literal: When primordial unity opened, the two modes began—lunar radiance hid by night, moon chariot rested by day; feathered kin soar forests, crawling things hurry to damp—things follow nature's ease, gentlemen delight in mind's grasp—some turn from glory to cliff dwellings, some push through orchid gates to enter court—those in wilds hide like dragons; those at court gather like phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: Since chaos split into yin and yang, creatures and sages alike seek fit dwelling—some flee court, some embrace it.

sentences.zh: 雖其軌跡不同，而道無貴賤，必安其業，交不相羨，稷、契奮庸以宣道，巢、由洗耳以避禪，同垂不朽之稱，俱入賢者之流。

translations.literal: Although their tracks differ, the Way knows no noble or base—each settles his task, envying not the other; Ji and Qi strove in office to broadcast the Way; Chao and Xu washed ears to flee abdication—both earn immortality's name and enter the stream of worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Office and reclusion differ outwardly yet share worth—Yi Yin and Duke Ji served; Chao Fu and Xu You fled—and both became paragons.

sentences.zh: 參名比譽，誰劣誰優？

translations.literal: Set names side by side—who proves inferior, who superior?
translations.idiomatic: Compare them fairly—who falls short?

sentences.zh: 何必貪與二八為群，而恥為七人之疇乎！

translations.literal: Why must you crave joining the Eightfold bands yet feel shame matching the Seven Worthies?
translations.idiomatic: Why envy the Eight Neighbors yet scorn the Seven Sages?

sentences.zh: 且道睽而通，士不同趣，吾竊綴處者之末行，未敢聞子之高喻，將忽蒲輪而不眄，夫何權戚之雲附哉！

translations.literal: Moreover when ways diverge yet communicate, scholars pursue unlike aims—I merely stitch myself to the recluse's tail—I dare not hear your lofty metaphor—shall I ignore the herb wagon and never glance—what talk of attaching to powerful kin?
translations.idiomatic: Paths fork—call me late hermit if you will—I ignore wagons of summons and scorn power brokers.

sentences.zh: 昔周、漢中衰，時難自托，福兆既開，患端亦作，朝游巍峨之宮，夕墜崢嶸之壑，晝笑夜歎，晨華暮落，忠不足以衛己，禍不可以預度，是士諱登朝而競赴林薄。

translations.literal: In the past, when Zhou and Han declined midway, the age was difficult and men could not entrust themselves to it. Once signs of blessing opened, sources of trouble also arose: in the morning one roamed the lofty palace, by evening one fell into a jagged ravine; by day one laughed and at night sighed, flourishing in the morning and falling by dusk. Loyalty was not enough to protect oneself, and disaster could not be predicted. Therefore gentlemen avoided going up to court and competed to hasten into the forests.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when Zhou and Han declined midway, the age was difficult and men could not entrust themselves to it. Once signs of blessing opened, sources of trouble also arose: in the morning one roamed the lofty palace, by evening one fell into a jagged ravine; by day one laughed and at night sighed, flourishing in the morning and falling by dusk. Loyalty was not enough to protect oneself, and disaster could not be predicted. Therefore gentlemen avoided going up to court and competed to hasten into the forests.

sentences.zh: 或毀名自汙，或不食其祿，比從政於匣笥之龜，譬官者於郊廟之犢，公孫泣涕而辭相，楊雄抗論於赤族。

translations.literal: Some ruined names with self-filth; some refused salaries—compare taking office to tortoise in a box; compare officials to calves at suburban altars—Gongsun wept declining minister; Yang Xiong argued though clan faced execution.
translations.idiomatic: Men smeared themselves or refused grain—office seemed boxed turtles or sacrificial calves—ministers wept or debated unto death.

sentences.zh: 今大晉熙隆，六合寧靜。

translations.literal: Now great Jin shines—the six harmonies tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Today Jin rules calm seas.

sentences.zh: 蜂蠆止毒，熊羆輟猛，五刑勿用，八紘備整，主無驕肆之怒，臣無犛纓之請，上下相安，率禮從道。

translations.literal: Wasps halt poison; bears and brown bears cease fierceness—five punishments unused; eight cords prepared—lord bears no arrogant wrath; ministers seek no ox-haired pardon—high and low dwell secure; all observe ritual and follow the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons sleep; punishments idle—throne and ministers trust each other.

sentences.zh: 朝養觸邪之獸，庭有指佞之草，禍戮可以忠逃，寵祿可以順保。

translations.literal: Court nurtures truth-touching beasts; courtyard grows slander-pointing grass—execution flees the loyal; favor follows the tractable.
translations.idiomatic: Palace beasts sniff evil; magical grass marks flattery—loyalty earns life.

sentences.zh: 且夫進無險懼，而惟寂之務者，率其性也。

translations.literal: Moreover advancement harbors no cliff-edge fear—yet cleaving to silence alone follows native temperament.
translations.idiomatic: Risk-free promotion suits some temperaments.

sentences.zh: 兩可俱是，而舍彼趣此者，從其志也。

translations.literal: When both options fit yet one rejects this for that—follow heart's bent.
translations.idiomatic: When both paths serve, choose passion.

sentences.zh: 蓋無為可以解天下之紛，澹泊可以救國家之急，當位者事有所窮，陳策者言有不入，翟璜不能回西鄰之寇，平、勃不能正如意之立，幹木臥而秦師退，四皓起而戚姬泣。

translations.literal: Utter non-action untangles realm chaos; utter simplicity meets state emergencies—those enthroned reach impasses; advisers miss ears—Zhai Huang could not turn back western neighbors' raid; Chen Ping and Zhou Bo could not legitimize Prince Ruyi's installation—Duanmu Ke lay ill yet Qin armies withdrew; Four Hoary Heads rose and Lady Qi wept.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawal can steady crises: Zhai Huang failed to stop western raids; Chen Ping and Zhou Bo could not place Liu Ruyi; yet Duanmu Ke merely stayed home and Qin fled; four graybeards emerged and Lady Qi wept fate.

sentences.zh: 夫如是何舍何執，何去何就？

translations.literal: Given this—what cling to, what adopt; what leave, what take?
translations.idiomatic: So what stays fixed?

sentences.zh: 謂山岑之林為芳，穀底之莽為臭。

translations.literal: They call mountaincrest woods fragrant and valley weeds rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain air smells sweet; swamps reek.

sentences.zh: 守分任性，唯天所授，鳥不假甲於龜，魚不借足於獸，何必笑孤竹之貧而羨齊景之富！

translations.literal: Guard allotment and follow nature—only heaven grants—birds borrow no armor from tortoises; fish borrow no feet from beasts—why mock lone bamboo's poverty and envy Qi Jing's wealth!
translations.idiomatic: Each creature uses heaven's gift—why mock the poor or envy kings?

sentences.zh: 恥布衣以肆志，甯文裘而拖繡。

translations.literal: Ashamed of plain cloth yet indulging will—better patched fur dragging embroidered train.
translations.idiomatic: Rather coarse robe with purpose than silk without.

sentences.zh: 且能約其躬，則儋石之畜以豐；

translations.literal: When able to restrain the person, then a peck of grain yields plenty;
translations.idiomatic: Restrain appetite—a peck fills you;

sentences.zh: 苟肆其欲，則海陵之積不足；

translations.literal: if unrestrained in desire, even Hailing granaries cannot suffice.
translations.idiomatic: indulge—Hailing stores empty.

sentences.zh: 存道德者，則匹夫之身可榮；

translations.literal: Preserve morality—then a commoner's body may shine;
translations.idiomatic: Virtue glorifies a commoner;

sentences.zh: 忘大倫者，則萬乘之主猶辱。

translations.literal: forget great relations—even a lord of ten thousand chariots remains disgraced.
translations.idiomatic: sin disgraces emperors.

sentences.zh: 將研六籍以訓世，守寂泊以鎮俗，偶鄭老於海隅，匹嚴叟於僻蜀。

translations.literal: I shall grind the six classics to instruct the age; keep silence and simplicity to steady custom—pair old Zheng by the sea; match Yan Jun in Shu wilds.
translations.idiomatic: I study the six classics to teach the world; couple Zheng on the coast with Yan in Shu.

sentences.zh: 且世乙太虛為輿，玄爐為肆，神游莫競之林，心存無營之室，榮利不擾其覺，殷憂不幹其寐，捐誇者之所貪，收躁務之所棄，雉聖籍之荒蕪，總群言之一至。

translations.literal: Moreover taking Great Void as carriage, dark furnace as market—spirit roams trackless groves; mind lodges desireless chamber—glory does not disturb waking; deep grief does not touch sleep—discard what boasters crave; gather what bustle discards—order sage texts' wasteland; gather myriad tongues to one arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Ride emptiness as cart; wander mind in silent rooms—spurn fame's trash; harvest truth's scraps.

sentences.zh: 全素履於丘園，背纓緌而長逸，請子課吾業於千載，無聽吾言於今日也。」

translations.literal: Keep plain sandals in hill gardens; turn from cap tassels forever—ask me again after ages—heed me not today."
translations.idiomatic: Keep straw shoes in hills—judge me later—not today."

sentences.zh: 張華見而奇之。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua saw it and deemed him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua marveled at the piece.

sentences.zh: 石鑒卒，王戎乃辟璆。

translations.literal: When Shi Jian died, Wang Rong then summoned Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Jian died Wang Rong finally called Shu Qiu.

sentences.zh: 華召晳為掾，又為司空、下邳王晃所辟。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua summoned Xi as clerk; also the Prince of Xiapi, Prince Huang, summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua took Shu Xi as aide; Prince Huang of Xiapi also summoned him.

sentences.zh: 華為司空，復以為賊曹屬。

translations.literal: When Hua, Zhang Hua, became Sikong, Minister of Works, he again made Shu Xi a subordinate clerk in the bandit-suppression office.
translations.idiomatic: When Hua, Zhang Hua, became Sikong, Minister of Works, he again made Shu Xi a subordinate clerk in the bandit-suppression office.

sentences.zh: 時欲廣農，晳上議曰：

translations.literal: At the time the court wished to broaden agriculture, and Shu Xi submitted a proposal, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the court wanted to expand agriculture, Shu Xi submitted a proposal:

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書，以倉廩不實，關右饑窮，欲大興田農，以蕃嘉穀，此誠有虞戒大禹盡力之謂。

translations.literal: I have humbly seen the edict saying that the granaries are not full and the region west of the passes is hungry and poor, and that You wish greatly to promote farming in order to multiply good grain. This is truly what the Yu ruler meant when he warned Yu the Great to exert all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: I have humbly seen the edict saying that the granaries are not full and the region west of the passes is hungry and poor, and that You wish greatly to promote farming in order to multiply good grain. This is truly what the Yu ruler meant when he warned Yu the Great to exert all his strength.

sentences.zh: 然農穰可致，所由者三：一曰天時不諐，二曰地利無失，三曰人力咸用。

translations.literal: Yet abundant harvests can be brought about through three causes: first, Heaven's seasons must not go awry; second, the advantages of the land must not be lost; third, human labor must all be used.
translations.idiomatic: Yet abundant harvests can be brought about through three causes: first, Heaven's seasons must not go awry; second, the advantages of the land must not be lost; third, human labor must all be used.

sentences.zh: 若必春無霡霂之潤，秋繁滂沱之患，水旱失中，雩禳有請。

translations.literal: If spring lacks soaking rain, autumn suffers repeated downpours, flood and drought lose the mean, and prayers for rain and sacrifice are required,
translations.idiomatic: If spring lacks soaking rain, autumn suffers repeated downpours, flood and drought lose the mean, and prayers for rain and sacrifice are required,

sentences.zh: 雖使羲和平秩，后稷親農，理疆甽于原隰，勤藨蓘于中田，猶不足以致倉庾盈億之積也。

translations.literal: then even if Xi and He regulated the seasons and Hou Ji personally farmed, ordering boundaries and furrows on highlands and lowlands and diligently weeding and hoeing the central fields, it would still not be enough to fill granaries by the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: then even if Xi and He regulated the seasons and Hou Ji personally farmed, ordering boundaries and furrows on highlands and lowlands and diligently weeding and hoeing the central fields, it would still not be enough to fill granaries by the hundred millions.

sentences.zh: 然地利可以計生，人力可以課致，詔書之旨，亦將欲盡此理乎？

translations.literal: But the advantages of the land can be produced by planning, and human labor can be achieved by assessment. Is this not also the principle the edict intends to exhaust?
translations.idiomatic: But the advantages of the land can be produced by planning, and human labor can be achieved by assessment. Is this not also the principle the edict intends to exhaust?

sentences.zh: 今天下千城，人多遊食，廢業占空，無田課之實。

translations.literal: Now across the many cities of the realm, many people eat idly, abandon occupations, occupy empty registers, and have no real field assessments.
translations.idiomatic: Now across the many cities of the realm, many people eat idly, abandon occupations, occupy empty registers, and have no real field assessments.

sentences.zh: 較計九州，數過萬計。

translations.literal: When calculated across the nine provinces, their number exceeds the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When calculated across the nine provinces, their number exceeds the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 可申嚴此防，令鑒司精察，一人失課，負及郡縣，此人力之可致也。

translations.literal: This guard should be made strict: let the inspecting offices examine closely, and if one person misses his assessment, responsibility should reach the commandery and county. This is how human labor can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: This guard should be made strict: let the inspecting offices examine closely, and if one person misses his assessment, responsibility should reach the commandery and county. This is how human labor can be achieved.

sentences.zh: 又州司十郡，土狹人繁，三魏尤甚，而豬羊馬牧，布其境內，宜悉破廢，以供無業。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the ten commanderies under the province, the land is narrow and the people numerous, especially in the Three Wei, yet pig, sheep, and horse pastures are spread throughout their territory. They should all be abolished and supplied to those without occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the ten commanderies under the province, the land is narrow and the people numerous, especially in the Three Wei, yet pig, sheep, and horse pastures are spread throughout their territory. They should all be abolished and supplied to those without occupations.

sentences.zh: 業少之人，雖頗割徙，在者猶多，田諸菀牧，不樂曠野，貪在人間。

translations.literal: Even if some people with little occupation are divided off and moved, many remain; they till gardens and pastures, dislike open country, and covet being among settled communities.
translations.idiomatic: Even if some people with little occupation are divided off and moved, many remain; they till gardens and pastures, dislike open country, and covet being among settled communities.

sentences.zh: 故謂北土不宜畜牧，此誠不然。

translations.literal: Thus to say that the northern lands are unsuitable for herding is truly incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Thus to say that the northern lands are unsuitable for herding is truly incorrect.

sentences.zh: 案古今之語，以為馬之所生，實在冀北，大賈牂羊，取之清渤，放豕之歌，起于钜鹿，是其效也。

translations.literal: According to sayings ancient and modern, the place where horses are born is truly north of Ji; great merchants obtained ewes from Qing and Bohai; and the song of releasing pigs arose in Julu. These are the proofs.
translations.idiomatic: According to sayings ancient and modern, the place where horses are born is truly north of Ji; great merchants obtained ewes from Qing and Bohai; and the song of releasing pigs arose in Julu. These are the proofs.

sentences.zh: 可悉徙諸牧，以充其地，使馬牛豬羊齕草于空虛之田，遊食之人受業於賦給之賜，此地利之可致者也。

translations.literal: All the pastures can be shifted to fill that land, letting horses, cattle, pigs, and sheep graze on empty fields while idle eaters receive occupations through allotments and grants. This is how the advantages of the land can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: All the pastures can be shifted to fill that land, letting horses, cattle, pigs, and sheep graze on empty fields while idle eaters receive occupations through allotments and grants. This is how the advantages of the land can be achieved.

sentences.zh: 昔騅駓在坰，史克所以頌魯僖；

translations.literal: In former times, piebald and dark horses in the outskirts were why Shi Ke praised Duke Xi of Lu;
translations.idiomatic: In former times, piebald and dark horses in the outskirts were why Shi Ke praised Duke Xi of Lu;

sentences.zh: 卻馬務田，老氏所以稱有道，豈利之所以會哉？

translations.literal: sending away horses and attending to fields was why Master Lao called a ruler possessed of the Way. Is this not where benefit comes together?
translations.idiomatic: sending away horses and attending to fields was why Master Lao called a ruler possessed of the Way. Is this not where benefit comes together?

sentences.zh: 又如汲郡之吳澤，良田數千頃，濘水停洿，人不墾植。

translations.literal: Again, at Wu Marsh in Ji commandery, there are several thousand qing of good fields, but muddy water lies stagnant and people do not cultivate them.
translations.idiomatic: Again, at Wu Marsh in Ji commandery, there are several thousand qing of good fields, but muddy water lies stagnant and people do not cultivate them.

sentences.zh: 聞其國人，皆謂通泄之功不足為難，舄鹵成原，其利甚重。

translations.literal: I hear that the local people all say the work of opening drains is not difficult, and that turning saline wetland into plains would bring very great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that the local people all say the work of opening drains is not difficult, and that turning saline wetland into plains would bring very great benefit.

sentences.zh: 而豪強大族，惜其魚捕之饒，構說官長，終於不破。

translations.literal: Yet powerful families prize the abundance of fishing there, fabricate arguments for officials, and in the end prevent the work from being opened.
translations.idiomatic: Yet powerful families prize the abundance of fishing there, fabricate arguments for officials, and in the end prevent the work from being opened.

sentences.zh: 此亦穀口之謠，載在史篇。

translations.literal: This too is like the song of Gukou, recorded in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: This too is like the song of Gukou, recorded in the histories.

sentences.zh: 謂宜復下郡縣，以詳當今之計。

translations.literal: I believe the matter should again be sent down to the commanderies and counties, to examine the plan appropriate to the present.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the matter should again be sent down to the commanderies and counties, to examine the plan appropriate to the present.

sentences.zh: 荊、揚、兗、豫，污泥之土，渠塢之宜，必多此類，最是不待天時而豐年可獲者也。

translations.literal: In Jing, Yang, Yan, and Yu, muddy lands and places suited to canals and dikes must often be like this; these are precisely harvests that can be obtained without waiting on Heaven's seasons.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing, Yang, Yan, and Yu, muddy lands and places suited to canals and dikes must often be like this; these are precisely harvests that can be obtained without waiting on Heaven's seasons.

sentences.zh: 以其雲雨生於畚臿，多稌生於決泄，不必望朝隮而黃潦臻，禜山川而霖雨息。

translations.literal: For their clouds and rain arise from baskets and spades, and their abundant rice grows from cutting channels and draining water; one need not look for morning rainbows before yellow floodwater arrives, or sacrifice to mountains and rivers before long rains cease.
translations.idiomatic: For their clouds and rain arise from baskets and spades, and their abundant rice grows from cutting channels and draining water; one need not look for morning rainbows before yellow floodwater arrives, or sacrifice to mountains and rivers before long rains cease.

sentences.zh: 是故兩周爭東西之流，史起惜漳渠之浸，明地利之重也。

translations.literal: Thus the two Zhou contended over eastern and western flows, and Shi Qi valued the irrigation of the Zhang canal, showing the importance of land advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the two Zhou contended over eastern and western flows, and Shi Qi valued the irrigation of the Zhang canal, showing the importance of land advantage.

sentences.zh: 宜詔四州刺史，使謹按以聞。

translations.literal: An edict should be sent to the inspectors of the four provinces, ordering them to investigate carefully and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict should be sent to the inspectors of the four provinces, ordering them to investigate carefully and report.

sentences.zh: 又昔魏氏徙三郡人在陽平頓丘界，今者繁盛，合五六千家。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the past the Wei moved people from three commanderies into the Yangping and Dunqiu region, and now they flourish, numbering five or six thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the past the Wei moved people from three commanderies into the Yangping and Dunqiu region, and now they flourish, numbering five or six thousand households.

sentences.zh: 二郡田地逼狹，謂可徙還西州，以充邊土，賜其十年之復，以慰重遷之情。

translations.literal: The fields of the two commanderies are cramped; I think they can be moved back to the western province to fill the borderlands, and granted ten years of tax exemption to comfort them for being moved again.
translations.idiomatic: The fields of the two commanderies are cramped; I think they can be moved back to the western province to fill the borderlands, and granted ten years of tax exemption to comfort them for being moved again.

sentences.zh: 一舉兩得，外實內寬，增廣窮人之業，以辟西郊之田，此又農事之大益也。

translations.literal: One action would gain two benefits: the exterior would be filled and the interior loosened, the occupations of poor people enlarged, and the western fields opened. This too would be a great benefit to agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: One action would gain two benefits: the exterior would be filled and the interior loosened, the occupations of poor people enlarged, and the western fields opened. This too would be a great benefit to agriculture.

sentences.zh: 轉佐著作郎，撰《晉書·帝紀》、十《志》，遷轉博士，著作如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant gentleman of composition, compiled the Annals of the Emperors and ten Treatises of the Book of Jin, was promoted and transferred to erudite, and continued his work on composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to assistant gentleman of composition, where he compiled the imperial annals and ten treatises for the Book of Jin; later he became erudite while continuing his historiographic work.

sentences.zh: 初，太康二年，汲郡人不准盜發魏襄王墓，或言安釐王塚，得竹書數十車。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the second year of Taikang, Bu Zhun, a man of Ji commandery, robbed and opened the tomb of King Xiang of Wei, though some say it was King Anli's tomb, and obtained several tens of cartloads of bamboo writings.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the second year of Taikang, Bu Zhun of Ji commandery broke into the tomb of King Xiang of Wei, though some said it was King Anli's tomb, and recovered dozens of cartloads of bamboo texts.

sentences.zh: 其《紀年》十三篇，記夏以來至周幽王為犬戎所滅，以事接之，三家分，仍述魏事至安釐王之二十年。

translations.literal: Its Annals in thirteen scrolls record from Xia down to King You of Zhou destroyed by the Quan Rong, then links events to the three families' partition, still narrating Wei affairs to the twentieth year of King Axi.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen-scroll Bamboo Annals run from Xia through Western Zhou's fall, then carry Wei down to 299 BCE.

sentences.zh: 蓋魏國之史書，大略與《春秋》皆多相應。

translations.literal: These were probably historical writings of the state of Wei, and in broad outline they mostly corresponded with the Chunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: These were probably historical writings of the state of Wei, and in broad outline they mostly corresponded with the Chunqiu.

sentences.zh: 其中經傳大異，則雲夏年多殷；

translations.literal: Where its classics and commentaries differ greatly, it says the Xia calendar had more years than Yin's;
translations.idiomatic: It claims Xia recorded more years than Shang;

sentences.zh: 益幹啟位，啟殺之；

translations.literal: Yi usurped Qi's place; Qi killed him;
translations.idiomatic: Yi seized Qi's throne and Qi killed him;

sentences.zh: 太甲殺伊尹；

translations.literal: Tai Jia killed Yi Yin;
translations.idiomatic: Tai Jia executed Yi Yin;

sentences.zh: 文丁殺季曆；

translations.literal: Wen Ding killed Ji Li;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Ding killed Ji Li;

sentences.zh: 自周受命，至穆王百年，非穆王壽百歲也；

translations.literal: from Zhou receiving the mandate to King Mu was one hundred years—it does not mean King Mu lived one hundred years;
translations.idiomatic: A century from Zhou's Mandate to Mu does not mean King Mu reached one hundred;

sentences.zh: 幽王既亡，有共伯和者攝行天子事，非二相共和也。

translations.literal: after You perished, one Duke He of Gong acted as Son of Heaven—it is not the two ministers' joint regency.
translations.idiomatic: After King You fell, the Earl of Gong named He ruled as regent—not the joint stewardship of two Zhou ministers that later gloss became "harmony."

sentences.zh: 其《易經》二篇，與《周易》上下經同。

translations.literal: Its two scrolls of the Yijing were the same as the upper and lower texts of the Zhouyi.
translations.idiomatic: Its two scrolls of the Yijing were the same as the upper and lower texts of the Zhouyi.

sentences.zh: 《易繇陰陽卦》二篇，與《周易》略同，《繇辭》則異。

translations.literal: Changes' Hexagram Stems Yin and Yang in two scrolls resemble the Zhou yi though the line texts differ.
translations.idiomatic: The yin-yang line scrolls echo the Zhou yi with variant line statements.

sentences.zh: 《卦下易經》一篇，似《說卦》而異。

translations.literal: Changes under the hexagrams in one scroll resembles Shuo Gua with differences.
translations.idiomatic: A single scroll of sub-hexagram Changes resembles the Shuo Gua with differences.

sentences.zh: 《公孫段》二篇，公孫段與邵陟論《易》。

translations.literal: Gong Sun Duan in two scrolls—Duan and Shao Zhi discuss the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls on Gongsun Duan debate the Changes with Shao Zhi.

sentences.zh: 《國語》三篇，言楚、晉事。

translations.literal: Guo yu in three scrolls—speaks of Chu and Jin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Three scrolls of state conversations cover Chu and Jin.

sentences.zh: 《名》三篇，似《禮記》，又似《爾雅》《論語》。

translations.literal: Ming in three scrolls—resemble the Record of Rites, also the Erya and Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Three scrolls of "Names" read like the Record of Rites, Erya, and Analects.

sentences.zh: 《師春》一篇，書《左傳》諸卜筮，「師春」似是造書者姓名也。

translations.literal: Spring Master in one scroll—records the Zuo zhuan's divinations; "Master Spring" may be the compiler's name.
translations.idiomatic: The "Shi Chun" scroll lists Zuo divinations; the title may record an author's name.

sentences.zh: 《瑣語》十一篇，諸國卜夢妖怪相書也。

translations.literal: Suo yu in eleven scrolls—various states' dream and omen divinations.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven scrolls of petty talk collect omens and dreams from many states.

sentences.zh: 《梁丘藏》一篇，先敘魏之世數，次言丘藏金玉事。

translations.literal: Liangqiu Zang in one scroll—first traces Wei reign-counts, then speaks of hill treasures.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangqiu Zang scroll counts Wei generations then catalogs buried treasure.

sentences.zh: 《繳書》二篇，論弋射法。

translations.literal: Jiao shu in two scrolls—discuss archery methods.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls on knot-shooting arts.

sentences.zh: 《生封》一篇，帝王所封。

translations.literal: Sheng Feng in one scroll—records kings' enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: One scroll of living enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 《大曆》二篇，鄒子談天類也。

translations.literal: Great Calendar in two scrolls—like Zou Yan's celestial discussions.
translations.idiomatic: Two scrolls of macro-calendars akin to Zou Yan's astronomy.

sentences.zh: 《穆天子傳》五篇，言周穆王遊行四海，見帝台、西王母。

translations.literal: Mu Tianzi zhuan in five scrolls—relates King Mu of Zhou touring seas and meeting Xi Wangmu.
translations.idiomatic: Five scrolls of King Mu's travels among seas and holy peaks.

sentences.zh: 《圖詩》一篇，畫贊之屬也。

translations.literal: Diagram Poems in one scroll—belongs with inscribed praises.
translations.idiomatic: One scroll of picture poems like engraved encomia.

sentences.zh: 又雜書十九篇：《周食田法》，《周書》，《論楚事》，《周穆王美人盛姬死事》。

translations.literal: There were also nineteen miscellaneous writings: Zhou Shitian fa, Zhoushu, Lun Chushi, and the account of the death of King Mu of Zhou's beauty Sheng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: There were also nineteen miscellaneous writings: Zhou Shitian fa, Zhoushu, Lun Chushi, and the account of the death of King Mu of Zhou's beauty Sheng Ji.

sentences.zh: 大凡七十五篇，七篇簡書折壞，不識名題。

translations.literal: Altogether seventy-five scrolls; seven bamboo bundles snapped beyond reading titles.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-five pieces survived; seven bundles shattered unreadable.

sentences.zh: 塚中又得銅劍一枚，長二尺五寸。

translations.literal: They also recovered one bronze sword two chi five cun long.
translations.idiomatic: One bronze sword measured two and a half feet.

sentences.zh: 漆書皆科斗字。

translations.literal: All lacquer writing used tadpole script.
translations.idiomatic: Every lacquer text showed tadpole seal forms.

sentences.zh: 初發塚者燒策照取寶物，及官收之，多燼簡斷劄，文既殘缺，不復詮次。

translations.literal: First diggers burned slips seeking jewels; when officials reclaimed them, many slips charred and snapped—the writing ruined beyond collation.
translations.idiomatic: Looters burned bundles for treasure; imperial clerks found charred scraps impossible to order.

sentences.zh: 武帝以其書付秘書校綴次第，尋考指歸，而以今文寫之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu handed them to the palace library to splice order and rewrite into contemporary script.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu tasked the secretariat to reorder and transcribe into clerical script.

sentences.zh: 晳在著作，得觀竹書，隨疑分釋，皆有義證。

translations.literal: Xi served as compiler and inspected the bamboo texts— whenever doubts arose he partitioned explanations with proofs.
translations.idiomatic: Editing at the palace, Shu Xi glossed every doubtful passage.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He advanced to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗問摯虞三日曲水之義，虞對曰：「漢章帝時，平原徐肇以三月初生三女，至三日俱亡，村人以為怪，乃招攜之水濱洗祓，遂因水以泛觴，其義起此。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once asked Zhi Yu about the meaning of the third-day winding-water rite. Yu replied: "In the time of Emperor Zhang of Han, Xu Zhao of Pingyuan had three daughters born at the beginning of the third month; by the third day they had all died. The villagers thought this strange, gathered at the riverside to wash away defilement, and then floated cups on the water. Its meaning began from this."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked Zhi Yu about the meaning of the third-day winding-water rite. Yu replied: "In the time of Emperor Zhang of Han, Xu Zhao of Pingyuan had three daughters born at the beginning of the third month; by the third day they had all died. The villagers thought this strange, gathered at the riverside to wash away defilement, and then floated cups on the water. Its meaning began from this."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「必如所談，便非好事。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If it is truly as you say, then it was no happy affair."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If it is truly as you say, then it was no happy affair."

sentences.zh: 晳進曰：「虞小生，不足以知，臣請言之。

translations.literal: Shu Xi came forward and said: "Yu is a young man and cannot know enough. Your servant asks to explain it.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi came forward and said: "Yu is a young man and cannot know enough. Your servant asks to explain it.

sentences.zh: 昔周公成洛邑，因流水以泛酒，故逸詩云『羽觴隨波』。

translations.literal: Ancient Duke Zhou completed Luoyi and floated wine along flowing water—thus stray poems say 'cup feathers drift with waves.'
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhou floated cups when founding Luoyang—matching lost poems.

sentences.zh: 又秦昭王以三日置酒河曲，見金人奉水心之劍，曰：『令君制有西夏。』

translations.literal: Further King Zhaoxiang of Qin feasted by the river bend on the third day and saw a golden man present a sword from water's heart, saying 'your lordship shall rule Western Xia.'
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Qin held a third-day river banquet and dreamed river gods gifting swords.

sentences.zh: 乃霸諸侯，因此立為曲水。

translations.literal: then he rose among feudal lords—therefore established winding-water rites.
translations.idiomatic: That feast founded the winding-water ritual.

sentences.zh: 二漢相緣，皆為盛集。」

translations.literal: The two Han dynasties continued the practice, and all made it a splendid gathering."
translations.idiomatic: The two Han dynasties continued the practice, and all made it a splendid gathering."

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜晳金五十斤。

translations.literal: The emperor rejoiced greatly and awarded Xi fifty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, he gave Shu Xi fifty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 時有人于嵩高山下得竹簡一枚，上兩行科斗書，傳以相示，莫有知者。

translations.literal: Once someone found beneath Song Mountain a bamboo slip with two columns of tadpole script—shown around, nobody could read it.
translations.idiomatic: Hikers at Songshan found tadpole-writing slips nobody could decipher.

sentences.zh: 司空張華以問晳，晳曰：「此漢明帝顯節陵中策文也。」

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Hua asked Shu Xi about it, and Xi said: "This is policy text from Emperor Ming of Han's Xianjie tomb."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhang Hua asked Shu Xi about it, and Xi said: "This is policy text from Emperor Ming of Han's Xianjie tomb."

sentences.zh: 檢驗果然，時人伏其博識。

translations.literal: Inspection proved him right—people admired his erudition.
translations.idiomatic: Checks proved him right—scholars hailed his learning.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫為相國，請為記室。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun as minister of state invited him as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Lun summoned him private secretary.

sentences.zh: 晳辭疾罷歸，教授門徒。

translations.literal: Xi pleaded illness, resigned home, taught disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi pleaded sickness, retired to teach.

sentences.zh: 年四十卒，元城市裏為之廢業，門生故人立碑墓側。

translations.literal: He died at forty—the Yuan marketplace halted trade; disciples and friends raised a stele beside his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: His death at forty closed Yuan markets; friends carved his monument.

sentences.zh: 晳才學博通，所著《三魏人士傳》，《七代通記》、《晉書·紀》、《志》，遇亂亡失。

translations.literal: Shu Xi was broadly learned and fully versed in talent and scholarship; the San Wei renshi zhuan, Qidai tongji, Jinshu annals, and Jinshu treatises that he wrote were lost in the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi was broadly learned and fully versed in talent and scholarship; the San Wei renshi zhuan, Qidai tongji, Jinshu annals, and Jinshu treatises that he wrote were lost in the disorder.

sentences.zh: 其《五經通論》、《發蒙記》、《補亡詩》、文集數十篇，行於世雲。

translations.literal: Yet his Five Classics Comprehensive Discussion, Enlightenment Notes, Supplementary Lost Poems, and collected writings dozens of scrolls still circulated.
translations.idiomatic: His Five Classics synthesis, primer, supplement poems, and essays survived in tens of scrolls.

sentences.zh: 王接

translations.literal: Wang Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Wang Jie.

sentences.zh: 王接，字祖遊，河東猗氏人，漢京兆尹尊十世孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Jie, courtesy name Zuyou, was a man of Yishi in Hedong—tenth-generation descendant of Han metropolitan governor Wang Zun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie, styled Zuyou, came from Yishi in Hedong—descended from Han Governor Wang Zun.

sentences.zh: 父蔚，世修儒史之學。

translations.literal: His father Wei perpetuated Confucian historiography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Wei taught classics and history.

sentences.zh: 魏中領軍曹羲作《至公論》，蔚善之，而著《至機論》，辭義甚美。

translations.literal: Wei central commander Cao Xi wrote On Perfect Impartiality which Wei praised—Wei wrote On Ultimate Pivot with exquisite argument.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xi's essay inspired Wang Wei's counterpiece.

sentences.zh: 官至夏陽侯相。

translations.literal: He rose to magistrate of Xiayang marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: He became Xiayang county administrator.

sentences.zh: 接幼喪父，哀毀過禮，鄉親皆歎曰：「王氏有子哉！」

translations.literal: Jie lost his father when young, and his grief harmed him beyond ritual. The neighbors all sighed: "The Wang clan has a son indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Jie lost his father when young, and his grief harmed him beyond ritual. The neighbors all sighed: "The Wang clan has a son indeed!"

sentences.zh: 渤海劉原為河東太守，好奇，以旌才為務。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan of Bohai became governor of Hedong; he loved the extraordinary and made honoring talent his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan of Bohai became governor of Hedong; he loved the extraordinary and made honoring talent his duty.

sentences.zh: 同郡馮收試經為郎，七十餘，薦接于原曰：「夫驊騮不總轡，則非造父之肆；

translations.literal: His fellow commanderyman Feng Shou passed the classics examination and became a gentleman when he was over seventy. He recommended Jie to Liu Yuan, saying: "If a Hualiu horse is not gathered under the reins, it is not in Zaofu's stable;
translations.idiomatic: His fellow commanderyman Feng Shou passed the classics examination and became a gentleman when he was over seventy. He recommended Jie to Liu Yuan, saying: "If a Hualiu horse is not gathered under the reins, it is not in Zaofu's stable;

sentences.zh: 明月不流光，則非隋侯之掌。

translations.literal: bright moon without flowing light never rests in Suihou's palm.
translations.idiomatic: hidden gems need patrons.

sentences.zh: 伏惟明府苞黃中之德，耀重離之明，求賢與能，小無遺錯，是以鄙老思獻所知。

translations.literal: I humbly consider Your Honor harbors yellow-center virtue and doubled-li brilliance—seeking worth without missing trifles—so this old man wishes to offer what he knows.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Liu Yuan to hire Wang Jie.

sentences.zh: 竊見處士王接，岐嶷俊異，十三而孤，居喪盡禮，學過目而知，義觸類而長，斯玉鉉之妙味，經世之徽猷也。

translations.literal: I have noted recluse Wang Jie—precocious and singular—orphaned at thirteen—mourning fulfilled ritual—learning grasped at sight—principles extend by analogy—such is jade-handle savor and guiding-world subtle plan.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Jie's orphan brilliance.

sentences.zh: 不患玄黎之不啟，竊樂春英之及時。」

translations.literal: I do not worry that the dark dawn will not open; I privately rejoice that spring blossoms arrive in time."
translations.idiomatic: I do not worry that the dark dawn will not open; I privately rejoice that spring blossoms arrive in time."

sentences.zh: 原即禮命，接不受。

translations.literal: Yuan immediately summoned with ritual—Jie declined.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan invited him—Jie refused.

sentences.zh: 原乃呼見曰：「君欲慕肥遁之高邪？」

translations.literal: Liu Yuan then summoned him and said: "Do you wish to emulate the height of withdrawing in fat reclusion?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan then summoned him and said: "Do you wish to emulate the height of withdrawing in fat reclusion?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「接薄祜，少孤而無兄弟，母老疾篤，故無心為吏。」

translations.literal: He replied: "My fortune is meager. I was orphaned young and have no brothers; my mother is old and gravely ill, and therefore I have no heart for office."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "My fortune is meager. I was orphaned young and have no brothers; my mother is old and gravely ill, and therefore I have no heart for office."

sentences.zh: 及母終，柴毀骨立，居墓次積年，備覽眾書，多出異義。

translations.literal: When mother died he wasted to bones beside her tomb for years—reading every book—often dissenting received glosses.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he lived by the mound emaciated, disputing classical readings.

sentences.zh: 性簡率，不修俗操，鄉里大族多不能善之，唯裴頠雅知焉。

translations.literal: Nature frank and blunt—cared not for vulgar conduct—great local clans mostly disliked him—only Pei Yi truly understood.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt honesty offended magnates; only Pei Yi befriended him.

sentences.zh: 平陽太守柳澹、散騎侍郎裴遐、尚書僕射鄧攸皆與接友善。

translations.literal: Liu Dan, governor of Pingyang, Pei Xia, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Deng You, Director of the Secretariat, were all friendly with Wang Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan, governor of Pingyang, Pei Xia, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Deng You, Director of the Secretariat, were all friendly with Wang Jie.

sentences.zh: 後為郡主簿，迎太守溫宇，宇奇之，轉功曹史。

translations.literal: Later he became county chief clerk—welcoming governor Wen Yu—Yu marveled and transferred him merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: As chief clerk to Governor Wen Yu he earned promotion.

sentences.zh: 州辟部平陽從事。

translations.literal: The province summoned him Pingyang staff.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial office took him on.

sentences.zh: 時泰山羊亮為平陽太守，薦之于司隸校尉王堪，出補都官從事。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Liang of Taishan was governor of Pingyang. He recommended Wang Jie to Wang Kan, Commandant of the Capital District, and Jie went out to fill the post of duguan aide.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yang Liang of Taishan was governor of Pingyang. He recommended Wang Jie to Wang Kan, Commandant of the Capital District, and Jie went out to fill the post of duguan aide.

sentences.zh: 永甯初，舉秀才。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongning he was nominated Flourishing Talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning brought his Flourishing Talent nomination.

sentences.zh: 友人滎陽潘滔遺接書曰：「摯虞、卞玄仁並謂足下應和鼎味，可無以應秀才行。」

translations.literal: His friend Pan Tao of Yingyang sent Jie a letter: "Zhi Yu and Bian Xuanren both say that you should harmonize the flavors in the tripod; you cannot have no response to the nomination as Flourishing Talent."
translations.idiomatic: His friend Pan Tao of Yingyang sent Jie a letter: "Zhi Yu and Bian Xuanren both say that you should harmonize the flavors in the tripod; you cannot have no response to the nomination as Flourishing Talent."

sentences.zh: 接報書曰：「今世道交喪，將遂剝亂，而識智之士鉗口韜筆，禍敗日深，如火之燎原，其可救乎？

translations.literal: Jie replied in a letter: "Now the Way of the age is being lost, and stripping chaos is about to follow, while men of knowledge and wisdom clamp their mouths and hide their brushes. Disasters deepen day by day, like fire burning across a plain. How can this be rescued?
translations.idiomatic: Jie replied in a letter: "Now the Way of the age is being lost, and stripping chaos is about to follow, while men of knowledge and wisdom clamp their mouths and hide their brushes. Disasters deepen day by day, like fire burning across a plain. How can this be rescued?

sentences.zh: 非榮斯行，欲極陳所見，冀有覺悟耳。」

translations.literal: This journey is not for glory; I wish to state fully what I see, hoping there may be awakening."
translations.idiomatic: This journey is not for glory; I wish to state fully what I see, hoping there may be awakening."

sentences.zh: 是歲，三王義舉，惠帝復阼，以國有大慶，天下秀孝一皆不試，接以為恨。

translations.literal: That year the three princes rose—Emperor Hui restored throne—because the state held great celebration all Flourishing Talent and Filial nominees skipped exams—Jie regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty skipped examinations—Jie resented missing his chance.

sentences.zh: 除中郎，補征虜將軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed gentleman cadet—supplemented marshal to the general who conquers barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He became aide to the northern expedition marshal.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之役，侍中嵇紹為亂兵所害，接議曰：「夫謀人之軍，軍敗則死之；

translations.literal: At the Battle of Dangyin, Attendant-in-Ordinary Ji Shao was killed by rebel troops. Jie argued: "One who plans another man's army dies when the army is defeated;
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Dangyin, Attendant-in-Ordinary Ji Shao was killed by rebel troops. Jie argued: "One who plans another man's army dies when the army is defeated;

sentences.zh: 謀人之國，國危則亡之，古之道也。

translations.literal: One who plots another's state perishes when it totters—such was antiquity's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Those who steer another man's throne answer with their lives when calamity comes—that maxim closed his plea.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之役，百官奔北，唯嵇紹守職以遇不道，可謂臣矣，又可稱痛矣。

translations.literal: At Dangyin the hundred officials fled—only Ji Shao kept post facing outrage—worthy minister—painfully admirable.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Ji Shao's martyr loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今山東方欲大舉，宜明高節，以號令天下。

translations.literal: Now east of the mountains prepares great campaign—we should proclaim lofty integrity to rally the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He urged honoring martyrs to inspire north China.

sentences.zh: 依《春秋》褒三累之義，加紹致命之賞，則遐邇向風，莫敢不肅矣。」

translations.literal: If, following the Chunqiu principle of praising through three layers of accumulation, Ji Shao is granted the reward for giving his life, then near and far will turn toward the custom, and none will dare fail in reverence."
translations.idiomatic: If, following the Chunqiu principle of praising through three layers of accumulation, Ji Shao is granted the reward for giving his life, then near and far will turn toward the custom, and none will dare fail in reverence."

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Court accepted.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒欲遷駕長安，與關東乖異，以接成都王佐，難之，表轉臨汾公相國。

translations.literal: Prince Hejian Sima Yong wished to move the capital to Chang'an—estranged from east—assigning Jie aide to Prince Chengdu Sima Ying—Jie resisted—was transferred minister to Linjin duke.
translations.idiomatic: He resisted Yong's Chang'an move and earned transfer.

sentences.zh: 及東海王越率諸候討顒，尚書令王堪統行台，上請接補尚書殿中郎，未至而卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: When Prince Donghai Sima Yue led lords against Yong—minister Wang Kan commanded mobile headquarters—summoned Jie as palace gentleman—before arrival he died age thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kan summoned him but he died at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 接學雖博通，特精《禮》《傳》。

translations.literal: Though Jie's learning vast he especially mastered Rites and Zuo commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He specialized in ritual and Zuo.

sentences.zh: 常謂《左氏》辭義贍富，自是一家書，不主為經發。

translations.literal: He often said Zuo's language rich—stands as its own book—not merely glossing classics.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Zuo as independent history.

sentences.zh: 《公羊》附經立傳，經所不書，傳不妄起，于文為儉，通經為長。

translations.literal: Gongyang attaches to classics—classics silent means commentary silent—text economical yet penetrating classics superior.
translations.idiomatic: He preferred Gongyang's disciplined ties to the canon.

sentences.zh: 任城何休訓釋甚詳，而黜周王魯，大體乖硋，且志通《公羊》而往往還為《公羊》疾病。

translations.literal: He Xiu of Rencheng gave very detailed explanations, but his demotion of Zhou and treating Lu as king broadly conflicted with the text; moreover, though his aim was to explicate the Gongyang, he often instead became a disease of the Gongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu of Rencheng gave very detailed explanations, but his demotion of Zhou and treating Lu as king broadly conflicted with the text; moreover, though his aim was to explicate the Gongyang, he often instead became a disease of the Gongyang.

sentences.zh: 接乃更注《公羊春秋》，多有新義。

translations.literal: Jie therefore reannotated Gongyang Spring and Autumn with fresh interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote new Gongyang commentary.

sentences.zh: 時秘書丞衛恆考正汲塚書，未訖而遭難。

translations.literal: When secretary Cheng Wei Heng collated Ji tomb texts unfinished he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng's Ji collation halted by death.

sentences.zh: 佐著作郎束皙述而成之，事多證異義。

translations.literal: Assistant compiler Shu Xi completed it—facts often diverged.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi finished with disputed readings.

sentences.zh: 時東萊太守陳留王庭堅難之，亦有證據。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Tingjian of Chenliu, governor of Donglai, challenged it, and he too had evidence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Tingjian of Chenliu, governor of Donglai, challenged it, and he too had evidence.

sentences.zh: 皙又釋難，而庭堅已亡。

translations.literal: Xi rebutted but Tingjian had died.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xi answered after Tingjian died.

sentences.zh: 散騎侍郎潘滔謂接曰：「卿才學理議，足解二子之紛，可試論之。」

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Pan Tao told Wang Jie: "Your talent, learning, principle, and argument are enough to resolve the dispute between the two men; you may try to discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Pan Tao told Wang Jie: "Your talent, learning, principle, and argument are enough to resolve the dispute between the two men; you may try to discuss it."

sentences.zh: 接遂詳其得失。

translations.literal: Jie detailed their merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie weighed both sides.

sentences.zh: 摯虞、謝衡皆博物多聞，咸以為允當。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu and Xie Heng—both encyclopedic—deemed his verdict fair.
translations.idiomatic: Experts approved.

sentences.zh: 又撰《列女後傳》七十二人，雜論議、詩賦、碑頌、駁難十餘萬言，喪亂盡失。

translations.literal: He also compiled a Houzhuan to the Lienu, the Exemplary Women, for seventy-two women, together with miscellaneous discussions, poems and fu, stele inscriptions and hymns, and refutations and difficult arguments totaling more than one hundred thousand words; all were lost in the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled a Houzhuan to the Lienu, the Exemplary Women, for seventy-two women, together with miscellaneous discussions, poems and fu, stele inscriptions and hymns, and refutations and difficult arguments totaling more than one hundred thousand words; all were lost in the disorder.

sentences.zh: 長子愆期，流寓江南，緣父本意，更注《公羊》，又集《列女後傳》云。

translations.literal: Eldest son Yanqi fled south—following father's intent reannotated Gongyang and reassembled women's sequel.
translations.idiomatic: His son carried on Gongyang work in exile.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: 【Historical appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Section: historians' verdict.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：皇甫謐素履幽貞，閒居養疾，留情筆削，敦悅丘墳，軒冕未足為榮，貧賤不以為恥，確乎不拔，斯固有晉之高人者歟！

translations.literal: Historians say: Huangfu Mi walked plain virtue in seclusion—nursed illness at leisure—devoted heart to brush-cutting—delighted in tomb texts—carriage caps could not tempt him—poverty brought no shame—firmly unmoved—surely Jin's lofty men!
translations.idiomatic: The editors praise Huangfu Mi as Jin's supreme recluse scholar.

sentences.zh: 洎乎《篤終》立論，薄葬昭儉，既戒奢于季氏，亦無取于王孫，可謂達存亡之機矣。

translations.literal: Down to writing Steadfast to the End advocating thin burial—warning extravagance like Jisun yet avoiding Wangsun Qing's extreme—he grasped life and death's hinge.
translations.idiomatic: They commend his funeral essay balancing thrift.

sentences.zh: 摯虞、束皙等並詳覽載籍，多識舊章，奏議可觀，文詞雅贍，可謂博聞之士也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu, Shu Xi, and others examined transmitted writings in detail—well versed in old statutes—their memorials reward reading; phrasing refined and ample—may be called gentlemen of broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu and Shu Xi mastered classical precedent—eloquent memorialists rightly famed as polymaths.

sentences.zh: 或攝官延閣，裁成言事之書；

translations.literal: Some held provisional posts in the palace extension pavilion—edited directive writings on policy.
translations.idiomatic: Some staffed the imperial library and drafted state papers.

sentences.zh: 或蒞政秩宗，參定禋郊之禮。

translations.literal: Some governed as ministers of rites—jointly settled suburban sacrifice ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Others directed worship and fixed suburban ritual.

sentences.zh: 虞既厄於從理，皙乃年位不充，天之報施，何其爽也！

translations.literal: Yu suffered obstruction by circumstance—Xi never enjoyed rank matching his years—how uneven heaven's rewards!
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu died thwarted; Shu Xi died young—heaven seemed unjust.

sentences.zh: 王接才調秀出，見賞知音，惜其夭枉，未申驥足，嗟夫！

translations.literal: Wang Jie's talents towered—recognized by discerning patrons—pitiful his premature cut-off never stretched swift stallions—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie won admirers yet died before his prime.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：士安好逸，棲心蓬蓽。

translations.literal: Encomium says: Gentleman Mi loved ease—nested heart in brush-thatched hut.
translations.idiomatic: Verse praise: Huangfu Mi sought calm in a humble hut.

sentences.zh: 屬意文雅，忘懷榮秩。

translations.literal: Intent fixed on literary elegance—forgetting glory of office.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished care on letters and forgot titles.

sentences.zh: 遺制可稱，養生乖術。

translations.literal: Testament writings worthy—yet nurturing life misguided arts.
translations.idiomatic: His funeral tract shines though regimen proved fatal.

sentences.zh: 摯虞博聞，廣微絕群。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu broadly learned—Guangwei unmatched among peers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu was encyclopedic; Shu Guangwei stood apart.

sentences.zh: 財成禮度，刊緝遺文。

translations.literal: Completed ritual norms—edited surviving texts.
translations.idiomatic: They framed ritual and collated relic texts.

sentences.zh: 魏篇式序，漢冊斯分。

translations.literal: Wei bamboo texts ordered—Han registers thereby distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: They sequenced Wei slips and sorted Han archives.

sentences.zh: 祖遊後出，亦播清芬。

translations.literal: Zuyou appearing later—also spread pure fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zuyou followed—another sweet reputation.
